groups.title: Core
groups.doc: What every page needs: a stage on a canvas, the world of blobs it draws, the camera, and the bones that move them. Start here.

groups.title: Movement
groups.doc: Moves written by hand, poses mixed together, feet that find the ground, loose parts that swing after the body, and morphs.

groups.title: Creatures
groups.doc: Cutting a creature out of shapes, hanging it on bones and growing its fur, and the creatures that come ready made.

groups.title: Shapes and scenes
groups.doc: Scenes written as data and the shapes they are cut from: buildings, rock, plants, worn land and weather, scenes put together from a land and props, the weather, clouds and wind every scene shares, and the sun, moon and sky that light them through a day.

groups.title: Pixels and sprites
groups.doc: Drawing a stage as pixel art, as brush and ink marks, as characters, cel shaded, in neon, as stained glass, in watercolor, as a halftone print, knitted, for 3D glasses, as clay, a blueprint, a thermal camera, cut paper, a mosaic or an old television, as blocks or glitching, and baking a creature into a sprite sheet.

groups.title: Styles
groups.doc: The looks as one catalog: each style's settings with their limits, names and where they start, the value a page holds for them, and the look each makes for the stage. The same definitions every page of this site draws from.

groups.title: Simulation
groups.doc: The solvers under cloth, under sand, snow and goo, under the ripples of a pond, under lava, under a bubbling potion and under a fire, for when you want to step them yourself.

groups.title: Picking, detail and edits
groups.doc: Finding what a tap hit, drawing fewer blobs far away, cutting and painting live, depth for effects after the draw, what a mirror shows, a lens with glow and focus blur, see-through blobs put in order where they cross, and solid shapes to stand on.

groups.title: Files and models
groups.doc: Writing and reading rigged .glb files, and turning an ordinary rigged model into splats.

modules.title: Stage: a creature or scene on a canvas

entries.name: MIRROR_PACE
entries.doc: How many times a second a stage draws its mirror's picture again, at most (`Stage.setMirror`).

entries.name: StageActor
entries.doc: What a stage shows: blobs, the skin that ties them to bones, and the skeleton.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob, and by how much.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones, and their pose.

props.name: morphs
props.doc: Blend shapes (from an opened .glb): a clip's weights, or `setMorphWeights` while none play, reshape the blobs on the CPU.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How much of its own light each blob gives, a byte a blob (255 all of it): a flame, a lit window. It only matters under live lights.

props.name: laid
props.doc: Blobs of a face laid over another part (voxel.ts `laid`: a pane on its frame), a byte a blob: drawn as blocks, a cell takes their color before the color of what they lie on.

props.name: soft
props.doc: Stays blobs while the stage draws blocks (`setBlocks`): grass and the like, drawn among the cubes. It makes no cubes.

props.name: flows
props.doc: A surface that moves by itself and is sent up again with `reshape` (a pond's): while the stage draws blocks it is columns that follow it, or stays blobs, as the look's `flow` says.

props.name: weather
props.doc: Weather laid over a scene (its clouds, rain, snow): while the stage draws blocks it is cubes too, or stays blobs among them, as the look's `weather` says.

props.name: lies
props.doc: Lies on the scene's surfaces (snow lying): while the stage draws blocks it is raised half a cube, onto the cubes' tops, which stand up to a cube over the surface the blobs lie on.

props.name: blockCell
props.doc: The side of its cubes while the stage draws blocks (`setBlocks`), where it was cut on a grid of its own; left out, the look's `cell`.

props.name: hole
props.doc: While the stage draws blocks, the square (x and z, rest units) whose cubes are not drawn, where a finer cut is laid in (blocks.ts `BlockSource.hole`).

props.name: keepCubes
props.doc: Its blobs never change in place, so while the stage draws blocks its cubes are made once and kept (blocks.ts `BlockSource.keepCubes`).

props.name: far
props.doc: As big as a world: while the stage draws blocks, its squares far away are drawn with cubes two or four times as big (blocks.ts `BlockSource.far`).

entries.name: Show
entries.doc: What the view shows: the blobs, the bones that move them, or both (bones on top).

entries.name: PickedBone
entries.doc: A bone found under the pointer (or stepped to): what the page says about it.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone's index in the skeleton.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name for people: 'left forearm'.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: How many blobs it moves at all.

entries.name: StageOptions
entries.doc: How a `Stage` starts.

props.name: offscreen
props.doc:
Draws into a render target and copies each frame to a 2D canvas on request: headless test browsers can render
WebGPU but not show it.

props.name: lights
props.doc: Builds each world with live lights (`setLights`), as Scan Studio does.

props.name: shadowDensity
props.doc: How dark what stands in a casting light's way makes it (the world's `shadowDensity`): left out, soft shadows that thin things let light through.

props.name: webgl
props.doc: Uses the WebGL 2 backend even where WebGPU would start: for testing the fallback.

props.name: cleanCuts
props.doc: Builds each world so cuts (`setEdits`) have a clean edge, tested per pixel (`setCleanCuts` turns it off and on).

props.name: exactShapes
props.doc: Builds each world to draw blobs in their true shape on screen (`EngineOptions.exactShapes`; `setExactShapes` turns it off and on).

props.name: peel
props.doc: Builds each world so see-through blobs can be put in order where they cross (`setPeel`; `EngineOptions.peel`).

props.name: timer
props.doc:
Asks the GPU to time its own work, so `gpuTimes` can say how long a frame takes on the GPU alone. Where the
browser offers no timer (WebGL without `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`, WebGPU without `timestamp-query`) it
does nothing. Off by default: each pass then writes two timestamps.

entries.name: GpuTimes
entries.doc: How long the GPU spent on one frame, in milliseconds (`Stage.gpuTimes`).

props.name: compute
props.doc: Compute passes: posing, projecting, sorting, lighting. WebGL has none, so 0 there.

props.name: render
props.doc: Render passes: drawing the blobs and every pass after them (pixel art, outlines, the lens).

props.name: cpu
props.doc: The CPU's share: posing and handing the frame to the GPU (on WebGL, sorting too). The two overlap, so a frame takes about the larger of this and the GPU's.

entries.name: Stage
entries.doc:
The engine's front door: one rigged creature (or a scene) on a canvas, drawn
by `SplatWorld` through three.js's WebGPU renderer, which falls back to
WebGL 2 where a browser has no WebGPU. Every blob is moved by its bones on
the GPU, so a creature can have hundreds of thousands. It plays a clip or a
poser, orbits, picks bones, draws pixel art and bakes sprite sheets.

  const stage = await Stage.start(canvas)
  stage.setActor(makeFox(20000), recordClip('trot', ...))

On blobscape.dev it is the Creature page's view (`CreatureStage`) and every
engine experiment's.

`offscreen` draws into a render target and copies each frame to a 2D canvas
on request: headless test browsers can render WebGPU but not show it.

props.name: renderer
props.doc: The three.js renderer the stage made and draws with.

props.name: backend
props.doc: Which backend the renderer started on: WebGPU, or WebGL 2 where a browser has none.

props.name: orbit
props.doc: Where the camera looks from. Set it to move the view.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Whether time moves on. False holds the pose.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast time runs: 1 is real time, 0.5 half speed.

props.name: step
props.doc:
Held frames: above 0, the pose only moves on every `step` seconds and the picture is left alone in between,
like animation drawn at a few frames a second. In pixel mode that is what stops edges crawling.

props.name: onFirstFrame
props.doc: Called once, after the first frame with a creature in it has been drawn.

props.name: mode
props.doc: How a blob on several bones takes its shape: see `SkinMode`. Change it with `setMode`.

props.name: blobCount
props.doc: How many blobs the creature shown has.

props.name: blockCount
props.type: { blocks: number; faces: number; levels: number[] } | undefined
props.doc: How many cubes and faces are on show while the scene is drawn as blocks.

props.name: sortKind
props.doc: Which depth sort the world uses: the counting sort, or the exact radix sort (slower; ties always in one order).

props.name: time
props.doc: Seconds into the clip, or the time a poser is showing.

props.name: glitchNow
props.doc: The glitch laid on the last frame drawn (none while no burst is on).

props.name: artSize
props.doc: Pixel mode's art size in pixels, once a frame has been drawn.

props.name: timesGpu
props.doc: Whether `gpuTimes` can answer: the stage was started with `timer` and the browser lets the GPU time its work.

methods.name: setSharpness
methods.doc:
How many device pixels to a CSS pixel the stage draws at, at most (2 where never set; the screen's own where that
is less). Under 2 on a sharp screen every pass has fewer pixels to fill, for a softer picture: a page may ask for
it on a phone while it draws a costly look.

signatures.code: setSharpness(most: number): void

methods.name: start
methods.doc: Starts a stage on a canvas: makes the renderer (WebGPU, or WebGL 2 where there is none) and begins drawing.

signatures.code: start(display: HTMLCanvasElement, opts?: StageOptions): Promise<Stage>

methods.name: shown
methods.doc:
Resolves once a frame drawn from now on is through the GPU: called after `setActor`, that is when the new
creature is really on screen, which on a phone can be seconds after the call returns (buffers to fill, shaders
to build). A page keeps its waiting mark up until then. At once on an `offscreen` stage, which draws only when asked.

signatures.code: shown(): Promise<void>

methods.name: setActor
methods.doc:
Shows a creature, replacing the last one, and plays `clip` on it. `extras` are more actors drawn in the same
world, sorted blob by blob with the first: things that move on their own and not by its bones, such as the
surface of a pond (`reshape` sends one up again after its blobs were changed). Clips, posers, picking, tints and
sheets are all about the first actor.

signatures.code: setActor(actor: StageActor, clip?: Clip, extras?: StageActor[]): void

methods.name: setBlocks
methods.doc:
Draws the scene as blocks (blocks.ts): its blobs snapped onto a grid of `look.cell`, each filled cell a cube in
one flat color, lit face by face, with the shadows blocks cast on each other. Cubes ride the bones their blobs
did, so the scene still moves. The stage's lights (`setLights`) shine on the faces as lamps and its ambient light
dims the look's own. It suits blobs with no light baked into them, and scenes more than small creatures. Leave
the look out to stop. Kept for the next actor too; the cubes are made again for each. Not in pixel mode, and it
comes before every other look.

signatures.code: setBlocks(look?: BlockLook): void

methods.name: tint
methods.doc:
Shows the actor in other colors without changing it: `paint` gives each blob's color (sRGB, 0–1) from its own and
its place in the list, and may give a fourth number, a share of the blob's own opacity (0 hides it). Left out,
its own colors come back. It stays through a new actor, until it is taken off; `highlight` and `refresh` send the
actor's own colors again, so call it again after them, and take it off before `bake`.

signatures.code: tint(paint?: (color: readonly [number, number, number], blob: number) => readonly number[]): void

methods.name: setFarDetail
methods.doc:
Level of detail by distance (lod.ts `FarRule`), kept for every world from now on: past `from` fewer blobs are drawn
the further off they are, each grown to cover for the rest, so a world as big as an island draws far ground with
fewer, bigger blobs. Leave it out for every blob. The soft actors drawn among blocks keep every blob.

signatures.code: setFarDetail(rule?: FarRule): void

methods.name: setSort
methods.doc:
Changes how blobs are sorted by depth: 'bins' is quick, 'radix' settles every tie the same way each frame, which
pixel art with hard edges wants.

signatures.code: setSort(kind: "bins" | "radix"): void

methods.name: useLights
methods.doc:
Whether worlds are built with live lights (the `lights` option, changed after the start), from the next
`setActor` on: a page turns them on for the one creature that wants them and leaves the rest as light to draw as
they were.

signatures.code: useLights(on: boolean): void

methods.name: setClip
methods.doc: Plays another clip on the creature shown, or none. `from` is the time it starts at, in seconds (left out, time runs on).

signatures.code: setClip(clip?: Clip, from?: number): void

methods.name: setAfter
methods.doc:
Runs `after` each time the creature is posed, once its clip or poser has set the bones and before loose parts
swing: for a change laid on top of any move, such as a head turned to look at something. It must leave the
skeleton updated. It stays through a new clip and goes with a new actor.

signatures.code: setAfter(after?: (sk: Skeleton, t: number) => void): void

methods.name: setPoser
methods.doc: Poses from the time instead of a clip; `t` starts at `from` seconds.

signatures.code: setPoser(poser?: (sk: Skeleton, t: number) => void, from?: number): void

methods.name: recolor
methods.doc:
Takes one actor's colors and opacities again after they were changed in place (the one shown or one of its
`extras`), when nothing moved: a floor that scorches.

signatures.code: recolor(actor: StageActor): void

methods.name: setSwing
methods.doc: Loose parts that swing after the body while a move plays (a `Swing` made for this actor's skeleton), or none.

signatures.code: setSwing(swing?: { update: any; reset: any }): void

methods.name: setMorphWeights
methods.doc: The morphs' weights while no clip keys them (the clip's own weights win while it plays).

signatures.code: setMorphWeights(w: ArrayLike<number>): void

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: After the actor's blobs were changed in place (a poser may do it each frame): the engine takes them again.

signatures.code: refresh(): void

methods.name: reshape
methods.doc:
After one actor's blobs were changed in place (the one shown or one of its `extras`): the engine takes that
actor's centers, shapes and colors again and leaves the rest alone, which is what a pond's surface wants each
frame. The count must not change, and the blobs must stay about where they were.

signatures.code: reshape(actor: StageActor): void

methods.name: setMirror
methods.doc:
Draws what a flat mirror shows of the scene (`SplatMirror`) and hands each picture to `seen` as it is read back,
a frame or two later: for water, or a polished floor, whose blobs color themselves from it (`seenIn`). The
picture is drawn again when the pose or the view changes, at most `MIRROR_PACE` times a second. `lift` leaves
out blobs lower than that over the plane (the mirror's own). Offscreen, `frame` waits for the picture of its
own moment before it draws. Left out, the mirror is taken away.

signatures.code: setMirror(mirror?: { plane: MirrorPlane; lift?: number; width?: number; seen: (image: MirrorImage) => void }): void

methods.name: seek
methods.doc: Moves the clock to `seconds` and draws that moment: for a page that kept its own time while this stage was paused.

signatures.code: seek(seconds: number): void

methods.name: setMode
methods.doc: Changes how a blob on several bones takes its shape: see `SkinMode`.

signatures.code: setMode(m: SkinMode): void

methods.name: setLightEase
methods.doc:
Eases live light over about `frames` frames (the world's `lightEase`; 0 is none; WebGPU only), kept for the next
actor too: a shadow's edge crossing a blob fades instead of popping. For lights that move slowly, like a sun.

signatures.code: setLightEase(frames: number): void

methods.name: setShadowDensity
methods.doc:
How dark what stands in a casting light's way makes it (the world's `shadowDensity`), kept for the next actor too:
lower for fur and grass, which shade themselves dark at the engine's own.

signatures.code: setShadowDensity(density: number | undefined): void

methods.name: setFog
methods.doc: Distance fog toward `color` (linear) from `near` to `far` units from the camera (`far` 0 is none); kept for the next actor too.

signatures.code: setFog(color: [number, number, number], near: number, far: number): void

methods.name: setEdits
methods.doc:
Cuts by shape, live (edit.ts): spheres, boxes or upright cylinders in world space, kept for the next actor too;
[] clears them. On a stage made with `cleanCuts` the edge is the shape's own line.

signatures.code: setEdits(edits: readonly ShapeEdit[]): void

methods.name: setExactShapes
methods.doc: On a stage made with `exactShapes`: whether blobs are drawn in their true shape (the default) or flattened from their middles.

signatures.code: setExactShapes(on: boolean): void

methods.name: setCleanCuts
methods.doc: On a stage made with `cleanCuts`: whether cuts have the clean edge (the default) or drop whole blobs.

signatures.code: setCleanCuts(on: boolean): void

methods.name: setOutline
methods.doc:
Draws outlines over the picture as a pen would (inkLines.ts): round the subject, where one thing stands in front
of another, and between its parts. Leave the pen out to stop. With any look, or none; pixel mode has its own lines.

signatures.code: setOutline(pen?: OutlinePen): void

methods.name: setCel
methods.doc:
Cel shading (splat-core/cel.ts), on a stage made with `lights`: every blob flat in its own color, the light cut
into two or three tones with clean edges, shadows cast by what stands in the light's way, and an even outline.
The tones are cut from the look's own light, and the stage's lights (`setLights`) stay as the scene's lamps: where
they reach is one more tone in their color, and the ambient light dims both tones. Its fill takes the place of the
stage's marks while it is on; leave the look out to have them back. Kept for the next actor too. It shades the blobs' own colors, so it suits blobs
that have no light baked into them. In pixel mode it shades the small picture the pixel art is made from, so the
light falls in bands that follow each form a pixel at a time; the outline is the pixel art's own then.

signatures.code: setCel(look?: CelLook): void

methods.name: setNeon
methods.doc:
Neon (splat-core/neon.ts): tubes of glowing light along the outlines, in each thing's own color at full strength
or the look's colors, with pulses of light running along them by the stage's clock; the bodies are kept dark and
catch the light as it passes. On a stage made with `lights`, whatever gives its own light (`Actor.glow`: a lamp, a
lit window, a flame) is filled with it and lights the bodies round it too. Every blob is drawn flat in its own color while it is on, with the stage's lights
put by, so it suits blobs that have no light baked into them. Leave the look out to stop. Kept for the next
actor too. Not in pixel mode; ASCII and cel shading come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setNeon(look?: NeonLook): void

methods.name: setWash
methods.doc:
Watercolor (splat-core/wash.ts): the picture laid on paper as thin see-through washes whose edges run and dry
darker, with the paper's grain showing through, the lightest places left bare, a wash of the look's sky behind
and a faint pencil line underneath. The paper covers the canvas. Every blob is drawn flat in its own color while
it is on, under the stage's own lights. Leave the look out to stop. Kept for the next actor too. Not in pixel
mode; ASCII, cel shading, neon and stained glass come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setWash(look?: WashLook): void

methods.name: setHalftone
methods.doc:
Halftone screen print (splat-core/halftone.ts): the picture printed in the look's few see-through inks, each as
dots on its own turned screen fixed on the paper, the dots growing and running together where the picture is
dark in that ink, the plates a little off true and the ink taking unevenly; the subject's sky is printed behind
it, or the paper left bare. The paper covers the canvas. Every blob is drawn flat in its own color while it is
on, under the stage's own lights. Leave the look out to stop. Kept for the next actor too. Not in pixel mode;
ASCII, cel shading, neon, stained glass and watercolor come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setHalftone(look?: HalftoneLook): void

methods.name: setFilter
methods.doc:
One of the looks laid over the whole picture (splat-core/filters.ts): a thermal camera, an old CRT or tape, a
blueprint, a mosaic, paper cutouts or claymation. The look covers the canvas. The blueprint and paper cutouts draw
every blob flat in its own color with no lights; the thermal camera draws what gives its own light over white so
it runs hot; claymation moves in held frames (`ClayLook.fps`) unless the stage holds its own. Leave the look out to
stop. Kept for the next actor too. Not in pixel mode; the other looks come first if set, and outlines and the
lens wait.

signatures.code: setFilter(look?: FilterLook): void

methods.name: setKnit
methods.doc:
Knitting (splat-core/knit.ts): the picture as a sweater, a grid of stitches fixed on the screen, each a V of
yarn in the look's yarn nearest what it shows, with the sweater's own pattern of bands and snow dots knitted
round the subject. The knitting covers the canvas. Every blob is drawn flat in its own color while it is on, with
the stage's lights put by, so it suits blobs in flat colors with no light baked into them. Leave the look out to
stop. Kept for the next actor too. Not in pixel mode; ASCII, cel shading, neon, stained glass and watercolor
come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setKnit(look?: KnitLook): void

methods.name: setAnaglyph
methods.doc:
3D glasses (splat-core/anaglyph.ts): the frame drawn from a left and a right eye either side of the camera and
laid over each other in red and cyan, so that through red and cyan glasses the scene stands in depth. What the
view looks at sits at the screen (unless the look's `pop` pushes the screen back), the backdrop behind it. The
blobs are drawn as they are (marks, lights), sorted once for each eye. Leave the look out to stop. Kept for the
next actor too. Not in pixel mode; the other looks come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setAnaglyph(look?: AnaglyphLook): void

methods.name: setGlass
methods.doc:
Stained glass (splat-core/glass.ts): every surface cut into panes of flat colored glass that stay on it as the
view turns, lead between the panes and round every part, the light behind, and the empty picture round the
subject glazed too, so the canvas is covered. Every blob is drawn flat in its own color while it is on, with
the stage's lights put by, and lead runs wherever that color changes, so it suits blobs in flat colors with no
light baked into them. Leave the look out to stop. Kept for the next actor too. Not in pixel mode; ASCII, cel
shading and neon come first if set, and outlines and the lens wait.

signatures.code: setGlass(look?: GlassLook): void

methods.name: setGlyphs
methods.doc:
Draws the picture as characters (glyphPass.ts): a grid of cells fixed on the screen, each with the character whose
ink matches how much of the cell there is to show, or a stroke along an edge that runs through it. Leave the look
out to stop. Not in pixel mode; outlines and the lens wait while it is on.

signatures.code: setGlyphs(look?: GlyphLook): void

methods.name: glyphText
methods.doc: The picture as text, a line a row of cells, while it is drawn as characters (`setGlyphs`) and once a frame has been.

signatures.code: glyphText(): Promise<string | undefined>

methods.name: setLens
methods.doc:
Draws the picture through a lens (lens.ts): light spilling round bright things, and blur for whatever is nearer
or farther than the distance in focus. Leave the look out to stop. Not in pixel mode, and outlines take its place
while they are on.

signatures.code: setLens(look?: OpticsLook): void

methods.name: setPeel
methods.doc:
On a stage made with `peel`: takes the nearest `layers` blobs (1 to `MAX_PEEL`) off the front of each pixel one at
a time (peel.ts), so see-through blobs that cross are each in front on their own side; 0 stops. Everything that is
not blobs is drawn under them all. Costs a draw of the blobs a layer and one more. Not in pixel mode, and any
other look comes first.

signatures.code: setPeel(layers: number): void

methods.name: setMarks
methods.doc:
Draws every blob as a brush mark or an ink stroke, or as soft dots again when left out; kept for the next actor
too. The marks belong to the blobs, so they stay put as the view turns.

signatures.code: setMarks(look?: MarkLook): void

methods.name: setLights
methods.doc:
Live lights on the world (needs the `lights` option); kept for the next actor too. A light is at a place or from a
direction (a sun); `ambient` is one brightness or a linear color.

signatures.code: setLights(lights: Light[], ambient?: number | readonly [number, number, number]): void

methods.name: setGlowGain
methods.doc:
How many times its own color a blob that gives its own light (`Actor.glow`) is drawn under live lights (the
world's `glowGain`), kept for the next actor too. Over 1 only with a lens (`setLens`), which lets what is brighter
than white glow; drawn straight to the screen it clips.

signatures.code: setGlowGain(gain: number): void

methods.name: setFloor
methods.doc: A floor `size` across in half-unit squares, so the grid shows how big each creature is.

signatures.code: setFloor(size: number): void

methods.name: setShow
methods.doc: Shows the blobs, the bones, or both.

signatures.code: setShow(s: Show): void

methods.name: setPixels
methods.doc:
Pixel mode on (with a look) or off. `size` is how many CSS pixels across
one art pixel is; the art is that many times smaller than the view.

signatures.code: setPixels(look?: PixelLook, size?: number): void

methods.name: setGlitch
methods.doc:
Tech glitch over pixel mode's art (splat-core/glitch.ts): now and then a burst of slid rows, split color and
corrupted blocks, in steps of the stage's own clock, so a loop drawn frame by frame joins up. The art read back
(`pixelFrames`) stays clean: `glitchArt(art, stage.glitchNow)` lays the same glitch on it. Leave the look out to
stop. Only in pixel mode.

signatures.code: setGlitch(look?: GlitchLook): void

methods.name: pixelFrames
methods.doc: Pixel mode's last frame as it was drawn small, and as finished art (exactly in the look's colors): for tests and for saving.

signatures.code: pixelFrames(): Promise<{ small: Frame; art: Frame; before?: Frame; parts?: Frame; ranks?: Frame; time: number; fine?: { small: Frame; parts: Frame; solid?: Frame } } | undefined>

methods.name: pick
methods.doc:
The bone under a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left), as the creature stands now:
the bone that holds most of the blob the pointer is on. Undefined when the pointer is off the creature.

signatures.code: pick(x: number, y: number): PickedBone | undefined

methods.name: rayAt
methods.doc: The line from the camera through a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left), in world space.

signatures.code: rayAt(x: number, y: number): { origin: [number, number, number]; direction: [number, number, number] } | undefined

methods.name: screenAt
methods.doc:
Where a point in world space falls on the view, in CSS pixels from its top left, for drawing over the picture;
undefined behind the camera. `orbit` is the view to use when it is not the stage's own yet.

signatures.code: screenAt(p: ArrayLike<number>, orbit?: Orbit): { x: number; y: number } | undefined

methods.name: hitAt
methods.doc: The bone under a point on the view (CSS pixels from its top left) and where the pointer meets it, in world space.

signatures.code: hitAt(x: number, y: number): { bone: number; point: [number, number, number] } | undefined

methods.name: boneInfo
methods.doc: What the page says about a bone.

signatures.code: boneInfo(bone: number): PickedBone | undefined

methods.name: highlight
methods.doc: Lights up one bone and the blobs it moves (or none).

signatures.code: highlight(bone?: number): void

methods.name: invalidate
methods.doc:
Asks for the next `frames` frames to be drawn. Call it after changing something the stage can't see, such as its
`orbit`.

signatures.code: invalidate(frames?: number): void

methods.name: gpuTimes
methods.doc:
Poses and draws the frame as it stands `frames` times over and asks the GPU how long it spent: per frame, in
milliseconds. Unlike `timed`, the GPU's own clock, so the browser's late and wandering report of work done does
not come into it, and the time is split between compute and drawing. Null where the stage can't time the GPU
(`timesGpu`): start it with `timer` and use `timed` as the fallback.

signatures.code: gpuTimes(frames?: number): Promise<GpuTimes | null>

methods.name: frame
methods.doc: Offscreen only: draws the frame `t` seconds into the clip and copies it to the page.

signatures.code: frame(t: number): Promise<void>

methods.name: bake
methods.doc:
Draws the creature on show as a pixel-art sprite sheet (bakeSheet.ts), with
the floor and bones out of the picture and the live view paused, then puts
the view back as it was.

signatures.code: bake(moves: SheetMove[], opts: BakeOptions, progress?: (done: number, total: number) => void): Promise<BakedSheet>
