entries.name: SceneDoc
entries.doc:
A pixel-art scene written as data: no code, so it can be typed by hand, kept
in a file, or written by Claude from a prompt (docs/scene-descriptions.md).
`checkScene` says what is wrong with one, in words that point at the place;
`compileScene` turns a sound one into what the voxel builder, the bones and
pixel mode need.

Units: about 1 is a small house, and a whole scene is about 4 across. y is up, the ground is y = 0, and the
camera starts on the +z side. Colors are '#rrggbb'.

props.name: name
props.doc: The scene's name.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds before everything repeats: 4 to 60.

props.name: light
props.type: { from?: Vec3; ambient?: number; shadow?: number; ramp?: number; crevice?: number; wear?: number; bounce?: number }
props.doc:
The baked sun: `from` points toward it. `ramp` (0–1, 0.7 when left out) turns shade toward cool violet and full
sun toward warm yellow, as a painter's ramp does; `crevice` (0.5) darkens corners and cracks; `wear` (0.5)
lightens sharp outer edges. 0 turns any of them off. `bounce` (off unless set) lets surfaces throw their color onto
what faces them, as a red wall warms the floor beside it; it costs build time, so use it where it shows.

props.name: lamps
props.doc:
Its lamps as a whole: 'always' keeps everything that says `lit: 'dark'` shining at any time of day, as in a cave or
a dungeon, where it is never day. Left out, each goes by its own `lit`.

props.name: tags
props.doc: What its land is, from the fixed list (tags.ts: grassy, rocky, sandy, snowy, sea, pond, night): Scene Creator's search finds the land by these.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The colors the picture is drawn in, 2 to 32.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky behind, top and bottom. Left out, the background is clear.

props.name: skyReach
props.doc: How far down the picture the sky's blend runs before it is all the bottom color: 0.05 to 1, the whole way when left out.

props.name: look
props.type: { dither?: number; glow?: number; outline?: boolean; edges?: boolean; steps?: boolean; bands?: number; heat?: number; selout?: boolean; cycle?: { colors: string[]; times: number }[] }
props.doc:
The pixel look it asks for: how much dither and glow, and whether to draw an outline and edge lines. `steps` paints
the scene in steps of its palette as it is cut (each blob takes one palette color, a step of its own paint from shade
to sun), so shade falls in flat bands; left out, shading is smooth and the picture is matched to the palette pixel by pixel.
Art-pixel effects (after Ink Studio's, MIT): `bands` (1 or 2) draws glow in flat rings, `heat` (1 to 3 pixels) makes
the air shimmer above anything glowing, `selout` softens the outline where it goes round something lit, and `cycle`
steps scene pixels of a few palette colors round their list a whole number of `times` a loop, as old games ran
water, fire and lights.

props.name: disc
props.doc:
How wide each surface disc is, as a share of the grid: 0.4 to 1, 0.55 when left out. Small discs keep paint
crisp but let about a tenth of what lies behind a surface show through; a subject whose far side or inner
parts are much darker or lighter than its near side (a head over an open jaw) wants 0.75, as creatures use.

props.name: trueShell
props.doc:
Cut every surface one cell deep in true distance, not in the shape's own units: a shape whose distance changes
faster than one for one (anything `rough`, worn land on a slope) otherwise leaves its skin thinner than a cell in
places, and the inside of the far side shows through. With `disc` 0.75 it is what keeps solid ground solid from
every side (the floating islands are checked for it). It costs a few blobs more.

props.name: big
props.doc:
A big place to walk round rather than a diorama: things may stand up to 8 from the middle, it may carry 128 bones,
a part may be about 6 units across and the parts four times the surface between them. It takes about four times as
long to cut, so a scene is big only when it needs the room.

props.name: huge
props.doc:
A place far bigger again, to explore on foot (Biome Islands): things may stand up to 20 from the middle and it may
carry 230 bones; with its specks it must still stay inside the 255 one byte names. Implies `big`.

props.name: grid
props.doc:
The grid it is cut on, as a share of the detail's own: 0.5 to 1, 1 when left out. A small subject in a scene of
open water or sky (the lighthouse on its rock) takes a finer grid, so its bricks and windows get as many cells as
a bigger subject's would. It costs blobs: 0.72 is about twice as many.

props.name: camera
props.doc: Where the view starts. `swing` rocks it gently from side to side by that many degrees, once a loop.

props.name: bones
props.doc: Things that move. The land itself needs none: parts with no bone stand still.

props.name: parts
props.doc: Everything in the scene, each a shape with its paint.

props.name: moves
props.doc: What moves, each a whole number of times a loop.

props.name: lights
props.doc: Live lights, at most four: they light what is near them, frame by frame.

props.name: air
props.doc: What hangs in the air: distance haze, low mist, beams of light and drifting specks.

props.name: cover
props.doc:
Snow, moss or dust laid over everything once it is cut (parts marked `bare` and glowing ones keep their paint):
`snow` settles on tops open to the sky, `moss` creeps over shut-in and up-turned faces in patches, `dust` lies
thin on every upturned face. `amount` 0 to 1, from a dusting to most of what faces up.

props.name: focus
props.doc: Where the eye goes: within `r` of `at` the scene is cut at full detail, further out on a grid twice as coarse, in about a quarter of the blobs.

props.name: water
props.doc: A pond whose surface ripples where rain lands on it and where things move through it.

props.name: lava
props.doc: A pool of molten rock that turns over, cools to a crust that cracks into plates, and bubbles (lava.ts): a shared recipe, as water is. A scene has water or lava, not both.

props.name: potion
props.doc: A round pool of potion that is stirred, marbles its colors and bubbles up and pops (potion.ts): a shared recipe, as water and lava are. A scene has one pool: water, lava or a potion. A prop may carry one (a cauldron's); it comes with it when set down where the land has none.

props.name: fires
props.doc: Fires that burn (fire.ts): hot gas rising off a bed of fuel, worked out as the water's ripples are: a shared recipe. At most `MAX_FIRES`.

props.name: heavens
props.doc:
The moon, the sun, the stars and how cloudy the sky is, from the shared recipes (heavens.ts): say where and how
many, and every scene's moon looks the same, cloud cover puts them out, and time of day brings the right ones. A
scene with a sky of its own (an eclipse, a red sun, three moons) draws it as parts instead.

entries.name: WaterDoc
entries.doc:
Water that moves (water.ts): a pond, a pool or a puddle. Wherever the still ground inside the box `from` to `to`
lies under `level` there is water, standing at that level, and its surface is a grid of heights stepped by the
wave equation. Rain that lands (`air.specks` of `rain` with `land`) falls onto it and each drop leaves its splash
where it comes down, so its rings spread from there, cross each other and bounce off the banks and whatever
stands in the water. One whole loop of it is worked out when the scene is made (`SceneWater`), so it repeats with
the scene. Dig the pond with a `cut` in the ground; float leaves on a bone that moves, since only what stays put
holds water back.

props.name: level
props.doc: The height its surface stands at.

props.name: from
props.doc: One corner of the ground looked over for water, [x, z].

props.name: to
props.doc: The opposite corner.

props.name: color
props.doc: The water's own color, seen looking straight down into it.

props.name: sky
props.doc: What its surface mirrors where nothing stands over it: the sky overhead, then the sky low down. The scene's `sky` when left out.

props.name: clear
props.doc: How solid it is looking straight down, 0 to 1: 0.5 when left out. Lower shows more of the bed and what swims under it.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A cell of its grid: 0.012 to 0.1, 0.022 when left out. The grid may hold 40,000 cells.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast a ring travels, units a second: 0.32 when left out.

props.name: damping
props.doc: The share of its motion the water loses a second, 0.05 to 0.95: 0.6 when left out.

props.name: ripple
props.doc: How many times steeper than it is the surface is drawn and lit, so small ripples read: 1 to 12, 4 when left out.

props.name: splash
props.doc: A raindrop's mark: a crater `r` across (half) and `depth` deep with a raised rim. About a cell and a half wide and a fifth of a cell deep when left out.

props.name: deep
props.doc: How deep the water is taken to be for the light a ripple gathers on the bed, which is what shows one from above: 0 to 2, 0.05 when left out. Too deep for the ripples' size and every crest is a white line.

props.name: bodies
props.type: { bone: string; at: Vec3; r: number; draft?: number }[]
props.doc:
What swims or floats through the surface, at most twelve: a ball of radius `r` round the point `at`, riding
`bone`. Where it breaks the surface it pushes aside the water it takes the place of, so a back that rises
leaves a ring and one that moves along leaves a wake. `draft` is how deep the water it moves is where it
crosses: a tenth of `r` when left out, which suits a fish whose back just shows; a post standing on the bed
moves the whole depth.

props.name: swells
props.type: { from: number; height: number; times: number; phase?: number }[]
props.doc:
Swells rolling in from the open sea, at most four, made by nothing in the scene: each is a long straight wave
train coming from the way `from` (degrees round the upright, measured as the camera's azimuth is: 0 from +z, 90
from +x), `height` meters from crest to rest, `times` crests a loop, starting `phase` (0 to 1) of the way through.
The water nearest that side is held to the swells as they would come in from beyond the scene, so they roll in
straight across the whole width of the water, bend round what stands in it, and what comes back out to that side
runs off rather than bouncing. Few, long and low is the sea: crests come `speed` × loop / `times` apart.

props.name: floats
props.type: { bone: string; at: Vec3; size: number }[]
props.doc:
What rides the water, at most twelve: the bone `bone` rises and falls with the surface at the point `at` (where
it sits on the water at rest) and tips with the surface's slope across `size` (half its length), steepened as the
surface is drawn (`ripple`). A boat, a buoy, a lily pad. Its own moves still apply under it.

props.name: foam
props.doc:
Foam where the water strikes what stands in it (a post, a rock, a bank): it gathers where the surge against a
wall runs up fast, spreads a little and fades over a second or two, and the surface is drawn white under it.
`foam` is how readily it gathers, 0 (none, when left out) to 4; 1 suits swells against posts.

entries.name: LavaDoc
entries.doc:
Lava that moves (lava.ts): molten rock wherever the still ground inside the box `from` to `to` lies under `level`,
found as water is (dig the pool with a `cut`). Its surface is the water's height field run slow and thick, and over
it a field of heat: rock wells up hot at `vents` and spreads out over the surface, cooling as it goes from white-hot
through orange and red to a dark crust, which breaks into plates with glowing cracks between them, piles up along
the bank and where two vents' spreads meet, and is broken open by bubbles. One whole loop is worked out when the
scene is made, as the water's is, and it glows by itself. Give the scene a light over it for what it lights.

props.name: level
props.doc: The height its surface stands at.

props.name: from
props.doc: One corner of the ground looked over for lava, [x, z].

props.name: to
props.doc: The opposite corner.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Its colors from cold to hot: crust, dull red, orange, white-hot. A dark crust and a red, orange and pale yellow glow when left out.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A cell of its grid: 0.012 to 0.1, 0.022 when left out.

props.name: cool
props.doc: Seconds for the surface to lose two thirds of its heat: 0.5 to 20, 3 when left out. Shorter, and the crust closes in nearer the vents.

props.name: flow
props.doc: How fast the surface moves out from a vent's edge, units a second: 0.005 to 0.5, 0.06 when left out.

props.name: plate
props.doc: How big the crust's plates are, units across: 0.02 to 1, 0.1 when left out.

props.name: vents
props.type: { at: [number, number]; r?: number; wander?: number; times?: number; phase?: number }[]
props.doc: Where hot rock wells up, at most six: round `at` ([x, z]), `r` across (half; a fifth of the pool's narrower side when left out), wandering `wander` round that spot (0) `times` a loop (1) from `phase`. One in the middle when left out.

props.name: bubbles
props.doc: How many bubbles burst a loop: 0 to 60, 8 when left out.

props.name: pop
props.doc: How wide a bubble is (half): 0.01 to 0.3, three cells when left out.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast a swell travels, units a second: 0.05 to 2, 0.12 when left out.

props.name: damping
props.doc: The share of its motion the surface loses a second, 0.05 to 0.95: 0.9 when left out.

props.name: ripple
props.doc: How many times steeper than it is the surface is drawn: 1 to 12, 3 when left out.

entries.name: PotionDoc
entries.doc:
A potion that brews (potion.ts): a round pool of liquid round `at` ([x, z]) out to `r`, at `level`, wherever the
still ground there lies under the level (dig the pot with a `cut`). Its surface is the water's height field, a
little thicker; it is stirred round, which draws its second color out through its own in spirals, small eddies
wander in it, and bubbles swell up into domes and pop, sending rings out and leaving froth that the stir carries
off. One whole loop is worked out when the scene is made, as the water's is. It glows unless told not to: give the
scene a light over it for what it lights.

props.name: at
props.doc: The pool's middle, [x, z].

props.name: r
props.doc: The pool's radius: 0.05 to 3.

props.name: level
props.doc: The height its surface stands at.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Its colors: deep (in its hollows), its own, its second (marbled through it), froth. A glowing pink when left out.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How brightly it glows, 0 (lit like anything else) to 1: 0.85 when left out.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A cell of its grid: 0.012 to 0.1, 0.022 when left out.

props.name: stir
props.doc: How many times a loop it is stirred round, a whole number from −6 to 6 (under 0 the other way): 1 when left out.

props.name: eddies
props.doc: How many small eddies wander in it: 0 to 6, 3 when left out.

props.name: bubbles
props.doc: How many bubbles pop a loop: 0 to 80, 18 when left out.

props.name: pop
props.doc: How wide a bubble is (half): 0.01 to 0.3, three cells when left out.

props.name: rise
props.doc: Seconds a bubble swells before it pops: 0.1 to 3, 0.7 when left out.

props.name: dome
props.doc: How high a bubble's dome stands, as a share of its half width: 0 to 1.5, 0.5 when left out.

props.name: froth
props.doc: Seconds froth takes to fade to a third: 0.1 to 10, 1.2 when left out.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast a ring travels, units a second: 0.05 to 2, 0.22 when left out.

props.name: damping
props.doc: The share of its motion the surface loses a second, 0.05 to 0.95: 0.7 when left out.

props.name: ripple
props.doc: How many times steeper than it is the surface is drawn: 1 to 12, 3 when left out.

entries.name: POTION_COLORS
entries.doc: The colors of a potion when a scene names none: deep, its own, its second, froth.

entries.name: LAVA_COLORS
entries.doc: The colors of lava when a scene names none: crust, dull red, orange, white-hot.

entries.name: AirDoc
entries.doc: A scene's air: haze, mist, shafts of light and specks.

props.name: haze
props.type: { color: string; from?: number; to?: number }
props.doc: Things far from the camera fade toward `color`: it starts `from` units past the view's target (0 when left out) and would be total at `to` (4).

props.name: mist
props.doc: Low banks of mist that drift slowly to and fro, at most four.

props.name: shafts
props.doc: Beams of light, as from a window or a gap in the leaves, at most six: what they land on is lit by them.

props.name: specks
props.doc: Swarms of small things, each moving on its own, at most eight swarms and 300 specks in all.

entries.name: MistDoc
entries.doc: One bank of mist.

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of the bank.

props.name: half
props.doc: Half its size along x, y (its depth) and z.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color.

props.name: thick
props.doc: How thick it is, 0 to 1 (0.5 when left out).

entries.name: ShaftDoc
entries.doc: One beam of light.

props.name: from
props.doc: Where it starts (a window, a crack, a lamp) and where it lands.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it lands.

props.name: r
props.doc: How wide it is, as a radius.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color.

props.name: strength
props.doc: How bright, 0 to 1 (0.6 when left out).

entries.name: SpeckKind
entries.doc:
What a swarm does: `dust` hangs and twinkles, `embers` rise and fade, `rain` falls fast as streaks, `snow` falls
slowly and sways, `leaves` flutter down, `fireflies` wander and blink, `bubbles` rise and wobble.

entries.name: LitWhen
entries.doc:
When something is lit: a lamp only when it is 'dark' (unless whoever sets the scene says its lamps always burn),
what belongs to the night itself only at 'night' (the moon, stars, fireflies: no setting brings them out by day),
a sun only by 'day', or 'always' (magic, lava, a crystal). A light, a glowing part or a swarm of glowing specks says
it with `lit`; `litFor` is what puts out the ones whose time it is not.

entries.name: SpeckDoc
entries.doc: One swarm of specks: dust, embers, rain, snow, leaves, fireflies or bubbles.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What they are, which sets how they move.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many.

props.name: from
props.doc: Two opposite corners of the box they live in: rain and snow fall from its top to its bottom, embers and bubbles rise from its bottom to its top.

props.name: to
props.doc: The box's opposite corner.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Each speck takes one of these.

props.name: size
props.doc: A speck's radius; left out, a size that suits the kind.

props.name: long
props.doc: Rain only: half a streak's length (0.07 when left out).

props.name: glow
props.doc: Whether they give off light; left out, embers and fireflies do.

props.name: lit
props.doc: When they are there, for specks that belong to a lamp or a time (a fire's embers, fireflies): gone for the rest. Left out, always.

props.name: land
props.doc: Rain, snow and leaves only: each lands on whatever stands still under it, lies a while and goes, then falls again. One whose spot has nothing under it comes down somewhere that has (the box's floor only when none is found).

props.name: wind
props.doc: Rain, snow and leaves only: how far the wind carries each sideways over its whole fall, [x, z]; rain slants along it.

props.name: shaken
props.doc:
Leaves only: shaken loose by the wind, so none fall in a calm or a breeze. Windy, some come down, straight down,
and land; in a gale all of them, carried away downwind before they can lie (`CompiledScene.blow`).

entries.name: BoneDoc
entries.doc: One bone of a scene: something for parts to ride on and moves to turn.

props.name: name
props.doc: What parts and moves call it.

props.name: at
props.doc: The point it turns and grows about.

props.name: parent
props.doc: Another bone it rides on (named earlier in the list).

props.name: prop
props.doc:
Marks a thing of its own (a mill, a tree, a sheep): its name as a prop in Scene Creator. The parts on this bone and
on the bones under it are the prop, and the scene comes apart into props by these marks with nothing picked by
hand. Not on a bone under another marked one.

props.name: tags
props.doc:
With `prop`, what the prop is and how it behaves, from the fixed list (tags.ts): kinds such as tree, rock or lamp
for search, and qualities the shared recipes act on (leafy, evergreen, floats).

entries.name: MoveAxis
entries.doc: An axis a bone turns about: 'x', 'y' or 'z', or any way as [x, y, z] (a prop set down turned writes one).

entries.name: moveAxis
entries.doc: The way an axis points, of length 1.

signatures.code: moveAxis(a: MoveAxis): Vec3

entries.name: PartDoc
entries.doc: One part of a scene: a shape, its paint and the bone that carries it.

props.name: shape
props.doc: Its shape.

props.name: paint
props.doc: Its paint.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it; left out, it is part of the land.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Gives off light and takes none: lamps, fire, stars, anything that must stay bright.

props.name: lit
props.doc:
When it is lit, for a part that is a lamp or part of one (a lantern's panes, a lit window, a flame, a star, the
sun): 'dark', 'night', 'day' or 'always'. For the rest of the time it is as `unlit` says. Left out, it never changes: right
for anything that only keeps its own color (a flower, a bird, foam), wrong for a lamp.

props.name: unlit
props.doc:
What is there while it is not lit: a color (the part in that paint, taking light and shade like any other), or
'gone' for something with nothing left behind (a flame, a star, the sun). Left out, a dull shade of its own paint.

props.name: noShadow
props.doc: Casts no shadow: thin things in the air.

props.name: laid
props.doc:
Laid on other parts (a pane on its frame): its own face is cut whole, and the face under it is what is left out.
`litFor` sets it on a lamp's part it has put out: a glowing pane and the dark frame it lies in would otherwise
each lose the face inside the other and leave a hole (Matt saw black windows by day, 2026-11-21).

props.name: grime
props.doc: A color that gathers in its corners and cracks, as moss or soot does.

props.name: bare
props.doc: Takes none of the scene's `cover`: water, glass, a fresh fire.

props.name: touches
props.doc: Meets other parts by design as it moves (foam round a bobbing buoy): the check for parts passing through each other lets it.

props.name: ink
props.doc:
Little drawn marks over it, one in some 4-by-4 blocks of pixels, never repeating: `hatch`, `stipple`, `cracks`,
`grain` (wood), `tufts` (grass) or `scales`. `amount` (0.5) is the share of blocks marked; `color` the ink, a
darker step of the paint when left out.

props.name: glass
props.type: { see?: number; mirror?: number; top?: boolean }
props.doc:
Water, ice or glass: it shows what lies behind it (`see`, 0.6) and mirrors what is over it (`mirror`, 0.3, more
at a glancing look), painted for the scene's own camera. Its paint tints what shows through, and where the line
from the eye leaves it with nothing met, a darker step of it shows, as the bottom of a pond does. `top` keeps it
to upturned faces, for a pond cut as one slab with earth sides.

props.name: strokes
props.doc: Dabs that follow the form: 0 to 1, how far each cell is drawn as a stroke along the level line round the shape. Shows as brushwork in the Blobs view.

props.name: placed
props.type: { foot: Vec3; at: Vec3; turn: number; size: number }
props.doc:
Where the prop this part belongs to was set down, when the part was written somewhere else: its shape and paint
are as written, moved from `foot` to `at`, turned `turn` degrees about the upright (counterclockwise seen from
above) and sized `size` times. A scene made of library props (compose.ts) writes it; nobody needs to by hand.

entries.name: ShapeDoc
entries.doc:
A shape, written as data: `kind` says which. The guide, docs/scene-descriptions.md in the repository, goes through
them all.
entries.type: { kind: "sphere"; at: Vec3; r: number } | { kind: "ball"; at: Vec3; r: Vec3 } | { kind: "box"; at: Vec3; half: Vec3; round?: number } | { kind: "cylinder"; at: Vec3; height: number; r: number; rTop?: number } | { kind: "cone"; from: Vec3; to: Vec3; r: number; rTo?: number } | { kind: "ring"; at: Vec3; r: number; tube: number } | { kind: "roof"; at: Vec3; half: [number, number]; height: number } | { kind: "join"; shapes: ShapeDoc[]; blend?: "smooth" | "chamfer" | "stairs"; by?: number; steps?: number } | { kind: "lathe"; at: Vec3; profile: [number, number][] } | { kind: "sweep"; path: Vec3[]; r: number; rTo?: number } | { kind: "text"; entries.name: PaintDoc
entries.doc: A part's paint: one color, or a pattern of several.
entries.type: string | { kind: "bands"; axis: "x" | "y" | "z"; size: number; colors: string[] } | { kind: "bricks"; size: [number, number]; colors: string[]; line: string } | { kind: "hex"; size: number; colors: string[]; line: string; deep?: string } | { kind: "speckle"; size: number; colors: string[] } | { kind: "patches"; size: number; colors: string[] } | { kind: "clumps"; size: number; base: string; colors: string[]; amount?: number; seed?: number } | { kind: "key"; colors: Record<string, string> } | { kind: "faces"; top?: PaintDoc; side: PaintDoc; under?: PaintDoc; up?: number } | { kind: "split"; axis: "x" | "y" | "z"; at: number; below: PaintDoc; above: PaintDoc } | { kind: "pieces"; colors: string[]; line?: string; ordered?: boolean } | { kind: "near"; shape: ShapeDoc; within: number; at?: number; near: PaintDoc; far: PaintDoc } | { kind: "waves"; size: number; colors: [string, string, string] }

entries.name: During
entries.doc:
When in the loop a move happens: [from, to] as shares of the loop (0 to 1). The move's `times` then fit between the
two, and for the rest of the loop the bone waits as the move starts and ends: a sprout or drift at nothing, a sway,
bob or pulse where its `phase` leaves it. `from` may be later than `to`, for a move that runs across the loop's
seam. This is how a scene tells a story: something appears at one moment, waves once at another and is gone.

entries.name: MoveDoc
entries.doc: Every move repeats a whole number of `times` in the loop (or in its `during`), so the scene loops.
entries.type: { kind: "spin"; bone: string; axis: MoveAxis; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During; wind?: number } | { kind: "sway"; bone: string; axis: MoveAxis; degrees: number; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During; wind?: number } | { kind: "bob"; bone: string; by: Vec3; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During } | { kind: "drift"; bone: string; by: Vec3; times: number; grow?: [number, number]; phase?: number; during?: During } | { kind: "pulse"; bone: string; size: [number, number]; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During } | { kind: "sprout"; bone: string; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During; rise?: number; fall?: number } | { kind: "pass"; bone: string; by: Vec3; times: number; phase?: number; during?: During } | { kind: "dissolve"; bone: string; times: number; by?: number; phase?: number; during?: During; rise?: number; fall?: number }

entries.name: FireDoc
entries.doc:
A fire that burns (fire.ts): fuel burning on a round bed heats the air over it, which rises, draws air in from the
sides and cools as it goes, and the flames are that hot gas. Their shape and height are not drawn: they follow from
the bed and from `height`, which says how long the gas holds its heat. Model the logs, the hearth or the wick as
parts; the fire is laid over them. Its light is one of the scene's `lights` that names it (`LightDoc.fire`).

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of the bed the fuel burns on (the top of the logs, a torch's head).

props.name: r
props.doc: How far out from there the bed burns.

props.name: height
props.doc: About how tall the flames stand; 3.6 times `r` where left out.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Its colors from its coolest gas to its hottest (deep orange, orange, yellow, white-hot where left out); palette colors, so pixel art can show them.

props.name: sparks
props.doc: Sparks thrown a second; 1.5 where left out, 0 for none.

props.name: lit
props.doc: When it burns: 'dark' for a campfire or a torch that is lit when it gets dark, 'always' for one that never goes out. Left out, it always burns.

props.name: seed
props.doc: Another fire of the same size burns differently with another seed.

entries.name: FIRE_COLORS
entries.doc: The colors of a fire when a scene names none: deep orange, orange, yellow, white-hot.

entries.name: MAX_FIRES
entries.doc: The most fires a scene can have.

entries.name: LightDoc
entries.doc: A point light in a scene.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it is.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color.

props.name: lit
props.doc:
When it shines: 'dark' (a lamp, a candle, a lit window, a campfire), 'night' (moonlight), 'day' or 'always'
(magic, lava, a crystal). Every light should say; left out, it always shines.

props.name: strength
props.doc: 1 is a torch; 3 lights dark ground brightly.

props.name: range
props.doc: How far it reaches.

props.name: flicker
props.doc: Flickers by this share of its strength, `times` per loop.

props.name: fire
props.doc:
It is the light of the scene's fire of this number (its place in `fires`): where the fire is played (`SceneFire`),
the light's strength follows how hard the fire burns from moment to moment, in place of `flicker`, which is what a
page that does not play the fire falls back on.

props.name: circle
props.type: { r: number; times: number; phase?: number }
props.doc: Goes round a circle of this radius about `at`, `times` per loop, starting `phase` (0 to 1) of the way round.

props.name: shadows
props.doc:
Casts shadows, worked out once when the scene is built, so they cost nothing as it plays and flicker with it. Only
the first four lights can, and not one that goes round a circle. Give it to a lamp or fire out in the open: a light
set inside something (a jar, a window, a hollow) to stand for its glow would shade everything outside.

props.name: during
props.doc: Shines only for this share of the loop, [from, to], coming up over the first fifth of it and dying away over the last: a flash, a spell.

props.name: clear
props.doc:
With `shadows`: how much open room there is round the light, 0.15 where left out. Nothing nearer the light than
this shades it. A light in a small hollow (a stone lantern's light box) sets it to the hollow's size, or the stone
right round it is taken for part of the lamp and lets the light through.

entries.name: checkScene
entries.doc:
Everything wrong with a scene description, each as `where: what`. Empty when
it is sound. It takes anything, so it can check what came back from a prompt.

signatures.code: checkScene(doc: unknown): string[]

entries.name: CompiledScene
entries.doc: A scene ready to build and play, from `compileScene`.

props.name: name
props.doc: The scene's name.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds the scene takes to repeat.

props.name: orbit
props.doc: Where the camera starts.

props.name: swing
props.doc: Degrees the view rocks to either side, once a loop: 0 holds still.

props.name: look
props.doc: The pixel look the scene asks for.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The scene's own palette.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The scene's bones.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Whether the scene asks to be painted in steps of its palette (`look.steps`).

props.name: touching
props.doc: The parts (by their place in the list) marked `touches`: they meet others by design.

props.name: haze
props.type: { color: Vec3; from: number; to: number }
props.doc: Distance haze, if the scene asks for it: the color (linear) and where it starts and would be total, in units past the view's target.

props.name: water
props.doc: The scene's water, if it has any, with its defaults filled in: what `SceneWater` plays.

props.name: fires
props.doc: The scene's fires, with their defaults filled in: what `SceneFire` plays.

props.name: landed
props.doc:
Raindrops of this scene's that come down on water over one loop (where it, or the `water` it was compiled with,
has some): where, when, and the share of its swarm before its speck (0 to 1), so a sky that shows only some of a
swarm (skyRecipes.ts `showWeather`) knows which of them are falling. Another scene's water can take them.

methods.name: spec
methods.doc: The shapes on a grid of `spacing`. With `steps` (a palette, 0–255), the scene is painted in steps of it as it is cut.

signatures.code: spec(spacing: number, steps?: Rgb[]): VoxelSpec

methods.name: empty
methods.doc: The parts (by their place in the list) that came out with no blobs at all, such as a shape whose hole swallows it: `checkScene` can't see those.

signatures.code: empty(built: { partOf: ArrayLike<number> }): number[]

methods.name: pose
methods.doc: Poses the bones for `t` seconds.

signatures.code: pose(sk: Skeleton, t: number): void

methods.name: blow
methods.doc:
After `pose` (before the bones are worked out): blows what falls (rain, snow, leaves) by a wind that may change
from moment to moment, `wind` ([x, z]) being how far sideways it carries a thing for each unit it falls. Each is
moved upwind by that over the fall it has still to come, so it still lands where it was planned to (and rings the
water, and lies, there), and rain's streaks lean along it. Snow and leaves are carried `DRIFT` times further.
With `wrap` (the square a swarm falls over, its middle and half width), a speck blown out of the square comes in
at its other side, so the slanting rain still fills it at every height (one that has landed is always inside).
Sways with `wind` lean downwind and swing wider by the root of how far the wind carries (a breeze a quarter of a
gale), so they gust with it, and flutter quicker as the wind rises. Spins with `wind` turn quicker by its level,
carried on from where they had got to as the level changes, so call it every frame, in a calm too (a wind of
[0, 0]). Leaves the wind shakes loose (`SpeckDoc.shaken`) fall only here. `level` is the wind's level
(`SkyState.wind`); left out, it is told from how far the wind carries.

signatures.code: blow(sk: Skeleton, t: number, wind: readonly [number, number], wrap?: { at: readonly [number, number]; half: number }, level?: number): void

methods.name: lights
methods.doc: The scene's live lights at a time, in seconds.

signatures.code: lights(t: number): PointLight[]

methods.name: ground
methods.doc:
The height of what stays put under (x, z), looking down from `top`, or `bottom` where nothing is: its still parts,
or its water's surface where that is what lies open to the sky. What falls from outside the scene lands on it.

signatures.code: ground(x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number): number

methods.name: lying
methods.doc:
Where snow lies under (x, z): as `ground`, but on whatever takes light, moving or not (a swaying crown, a turning
sail, a boat on the water, a walker), with the index of the bone that carries it (0 for the land or the water), so
the snow lying there can ride that bone (snowCover.ts `followSnow`). In the rest pose.

signatures.code: lying(x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number): { y: number; bone: number }

entries.name: WaterDrop
entries.doc: A raindrop coming down on water: where, when in the loop, and the share of its swarm before its speck.

props.name: x
props.doc: Where it comes down, across.

props.name: z
props.doc: Where it comes down, along.

props.name: at
props.doc: When, in seconds into the loop.

props.name: share
props.doc: The share of its swarm before its speck, 0 to 1.

entries.name: WaterPlan
entries.doc: A scene's water made ready (`CompiledScene.water`): its grid, its look, the rain that lands on it over one loop and what swims through it.

props.name: level
props.doc: The height the surface stands at.

props.name: x0
props.doc: The grid's corner along x.

props.name: z0
props.doc: The grid's corner along z.

props.name: nx
props.doc: Cells along x.

props.name: nz
props.doc: Cells along z.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A cell's side.

props.name: speed
props.doc: How fast a ring travels, units a second.

props.name: damping
props.doc: The share of its motion the water loses a second.

props.name: ripple
props.doc: How many times steeper than it is the surface is drawn and lit.

props.name: deep
props.doc: How deep the water is taken to be for the light a ripple gathers on the bed.

props.name: clear
props.doc: How solid the surface is looking straight down.

props.name: splash
props.doc: A raindrop's mark: its half width and its depth.

props.name: body
props.doc: The water's own color, linear.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky overhead as the surface mirrors it, linear.

props.name: horizon
props.doc: The sky low down, linear.

props.name: drops
props.doc: Every raindrop that lands on the water in one loop: where, and how many seconds into the loop.

props.name: bodies
props.type: { bone: number; at: Vec3; r: number; draft: number }[]
props.doc: What moves through the surface: a ball of radius `r` round the rest point `at`, riding the bone at index `bone`, moving water `draft` deep where it crosses.

props.name: swells
props.type: { from: number; height: number; times: number; phase: number }[]
props.doc: Swells coming in from the open sea: from the way `from` (degrees, as the camera's azimuth), `height` high, `times` crests a loop from `phase`.

props.name: floats
props.type: { bone: number; at: Vec3; size: number }[]
props.doc: What rides the water: the bone at index `bone`, sitting on it at `at`, tipped by its slope across `size`.

props.name: foam
props.doc: How readily foam gathers where the water strikes something standing in it: 0 for none.

props.name: lava
props.doc: Where the pool is molten rock (`SceneDoc.lava`): how it turns over, cools and bubbles.

props.name: potion
props.doc: Where the pool is a potion (`SceneDoc.potion`): how it is stirred, marbles and bubbles.

methods.name: wet
methods.doc: Whether there is water at a point: the still ground there lies under the level. It measures the ground each time, so ask once a cell.

signatures.code: wet(x: number, z: number): boolean

methods.name: stands
methods.doc: Whether something stands out of the water at a dry point (a rock, a bank, a post), rather than there being no ground at all (past the edge of a scene's sea). Measured each time, as `wet` is.

signatures.code: stands(x: number, z: number): boolean

entries.name: FirePlan
entries.doc: A scene's fire as compiled (`CompiledScene.fires`).

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of the bed of fuel.

props.name: r
props.doc: The bed's radius.

props.name: height
props.doc: How tall the flames stand.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Its colors from coolest to hottest, 0 to 1 as blobs hold them (sRGB).

props.name: sparks
props.doc: Sparks thrown a second.

props.name: seed
props.doc: What tells it from another fire of the same size.

props.name: lights
props.type: { index: number; flicker?: { by: number; times: number } }[]
props.doc: The scene's lights that are this fire's (their places among `lights`), each with the flicker it falls back on, which the fire's own burning takes the place of.

entries.name: DRIFT
entries.doc: How much further than rain the wind carries snow and leaves over the same fall: they fall slowly.

entries.name: FLUTTER
entries.doc: How much wider a sway with `wind` swings, as a share of how far it leans.

entries.name: FLUTTER_BEATS
entries.doc: How many times its own beat a sway with `wind` flutters in a breeze, a wind and a gale: quicker as it rises.

entries.name: SHAKEN_AWAY
entries.doc: How much further than a falling leaf drifts a gale carries a leaf it shakes loose: off and away.

entries.name: sprouted
entries.doc: A sprout's size through its life (0 to 1): grows from nothing over the first `rise` (40%), stands, and shrinks away over the last `fall` (15%).

signatures.code: sprouted(life: number, rise?: number, fall?: number): number

entries.name: DISSOLVE_RISE
entries.doc: The shares of a dissolve's time spent gathering and dissolving where it doesn't say.

entries.name: DISSOLVE_FALL
entries.doc: The shares of a dissolve's time spent gathering and dissolving where it doesn't say.

entries.name: DISSOLVE_BY
entries.doc: How far a dissolve's blobs drift where it doesn't say.

entries.name: dissolving
entries.doc: Poses a `dissolve` move `life` (0 to 1) through its time: how far gone the bone's blobs are, and their drift.

signatures.code: dissolving(sk: Skeleton, b: number, life: number, m: { by?: number; rise?: number; fall?: number }): void

entries.name: duringAt
entries.doc:
How far through its `during` a move is at `u` of the loop: 0 as it starts, 1 from its end until it starts again.
With none, `u` itself, so the move fills the loop.

signatures.code: duringAt(u: number, d?: During): number

entries.name: PASS_EDGE
entries.doc: The share of its way at each end over which a passing thing grows in and shrinks away.

entries.name: passed
entries.doc:
A `pass` move at `life` (0 to 1 along its way) for a thing drawn `phase` along it: how far it stands from where it
is drawn, as a share of the way, and its size, which is 0 at both ends so the jump back is never seen.

signatures.code: passed(life: number, phase: number): [number, number]

entries.name: compileScene
entries.doc: `ground` is the ground what falls lands on, in place of the description's own parts: weather laid over another scene (skyRecipes.ts) lands on that scene's.

signatures.code: compileScene(given: SceneDoc, options?: { puffs?: boolean; ground?: (x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number) => number; water?: number }): CompiledScene

entries.name: flickerAt
entries.doc: How bright a flickering light is `u` of the way through the loop, beside its own strength: two flickers out of step, so it doesn't beat like a clock, but still loops.
entries.type: (f: { by: number; times: number } | undefined, u: number) => number

entries.name: lightsAt
entries.doc: Described lights as they shine `u` of the way through the loop (0 to 1): flickering, going round, coming and going.

signatures.code: lightsAt(lights: readonly LightDoc[], u: number): PointLight[]

entries.name: UNLIT_LIGHT
entries.doc: How much of its lightness and of its color a lamp keeps while it is not lit, where its part names no `unlit` color.

entries.name: UNLIT_COLOR
entries.doc: How much of its lightness and of its color a lamp keeps while it is not lit, where its part names no `unlit` color.

entries.name: dulled
entries.doc: A color as a lamp of it looks while it is not lit: darker and nearly gray, as glass with nothing behind it.

signatures.code: dulled(color: string): string

entries.name: isLit
entries.doc: Whether something lit `when` is lit: by day or in the dark, with the scene's `lamps` deciding for those that wait for the dark.

signatures.code: isLit(when: LitWhen | undefined, dark: boolean, lamps?: "dark" | "always"): boolean

entries.name: hasLamps
entries.doc: Whether anything in a description is lit only some of the time, so that the time of day changes it.

signatures.code: hasLamps(doc: SceneDoc): boolean

entries.name: litFor
entries.doc:
A description as it stands by day (`dark` false) or in the dark: every light, glowing part and swarm of specks whose
`lit` says it is not lit now is put out. A light shines at strength 0 (it keeps its place in the list, which baked
lamp shadows and props' picks go by); a part stops glowing and takes its `unlit` color, or a dull shade of its own
paint (`dulled`), or is left out where it is `unlit: 'gone'`; specks are left out. `lamps` (the scene's own where
left out) set to 'always' keeps everything that waits for the dark lit. Colors it adds join the palette while there
is room. A description nothing changes in comes back as it is, so a caller can tell there is nothing to cut again.

signatures.code: litFor(given: SceneDoc, dark: boolean, lamps?: "dark" | "always"): SceneDoc

modules.title: Scenes made of a land and props
modules.doc:
Scenes made of props (Scene Creator, docs/scene-editor-plan.md). A **prop** is a scene description that holds one
thing (a windmill, a sheep, a witch) standing where it stood in the scene it came from, and the point it stands on.
A **project** is a land (a prop that everything stands on, which keeps the scene's sky, air and water) and props set
down on it, each moved, turned about the upright and sized.

A placed prop is cut where it is put, so its baked sun and shade are right for the way it faces, and its moves are
turned with it. Two ways to cut a project: apart (the land and each prop on their own, so moving one recuts only it:
what an editor wants) and merged (one grid for all, so props cast their baked shadows on the land and cull what they
stand in: what an export wants). Both are posed and lit by the same functions here.

entries.name: PropDoc
entries.doc: A thing that can be set down in a scene.

props.name: name
props.doc: What it is called in a list.

props.name: doc
props.doc: Its description: only its own parts, bones, moves and lights, where they stood in the scene it came from.

props.name: foot
props.doc: The point it stands on, in the description's own coordinates: what a placement moves, and what it turns about.

props.name: tags
props.doc: What it is and how it behaves, from the fixed list (tags.ts): search finds it by them and the shared recipes act on them.

props.name: water
props.type: { rides?: { bone: string; at: Vec3; size: number }[]; wakes?: { bone: string; at: Vec3; r: number; draft?: number }[] }
props.doc:
How it meets a land's water, where it is set down in one (`WaterDoc` floats and bodies, naming its own bones):
`rides` bob and tip on the surface (a boat, a buoy), `wakes` push the water aside as they move through it (a duck,
a fish). Left out on dry land; set down in water, they join the land's water.

entries.name: PropRef
entries.doc: A library prop by its id, or a prop written out in full (an imported one).

entries.name: Placed
entries.doc: One prop set down in a project.

props.name: prop
props.doc: Which prop it is.

props.name: still
props.doc: Holds still: its own moves are not played.

props.name: phase
props.doc: Its moves run this share of the loop later (0 to 1), so two of one prop side by side don't sway as one.

props.name: lit
props.doc:
Its lamps, where the project has a time of day: 'always' keeps them lit by day, 'dark' has them wait for the dark
whatever the project or the land says. Left out, it goes by the project's `light.lit`, then the land's own `lamps`.

entries.name: SceneProject
entries.doc: A scene made of a land and props: what Scene Creator edits and saves.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says a file is a project.

props.name: version
props.doc: The format's version.

props.name: name
props.doc: The scene's name.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds before everything repeats: every prop's moves are fitted to it.

props.name: land
props.doc: What everything stands on. It is never moved.

props.name: props
props.doc: The props set down on the land.

props.name: camera
props.doc: Where the view starts; the land's own camera when left out.

props.name: style
props.doc: How it is drawn: a style's id (Diorama's `STYLES`) and its settings, kept as the page gives them.

props.name: light
props.doc: The light, sky and air, where they differ from the land's own.

entries.name: ProjectLight
entries.doc:
A project's light, each left out where the land's own stands. The sun is baked into the cut (so a change cuts again)
unless it is `live`: then everything is cut unlit and the sun, the moon and the sky's own light shine live at the
hour (`daylight`), with shadows where the device draws them. Lamps are always live, so they move without a cut.

props.name: sun
props.doc: The baked sun: `turn` degrees round from +z (counterclockwise seen from above, as props turn) and `height` degrees up.

props.name: shade
props.doc: How much light reaches what the sun doesn't: 0 to 1.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky behind, top and bottom.

props.name: live
props.doc: The sun live, at this hour of the day (0 to 24).

props.name: lit
props.doc:
Every prop's lamps under a live sun: 'always' keeps them lit by day (a cave, a dungeon), 'dark' has them wait for
the dark. Left out, the land's own `lamps` says (a cave's land keeps what is set down in it lit). A prop's own
`lit` comes first.

props.name: lamps
props.doc: Lamps the visitor set down, at most `MAX_PROJECT_LAMPS`.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How strongly glowing things light what is round them and shine in the picture, as Diorama's Glow (0 to 4): the land's own when left out.

A shared weather or cloud cover laid over the scene (skyRecipes.ts: the same recipes every Diorama scene takes),

Whether it is dark in a project: by its live sun's hour. With no live sun there is no time of day, and everything is

Poses a placed prop: its description's own pose, played on a skeleton of its own as it was written, then turned as
the prop was (each bone's turn as R q R⁻¹, each slide by R and the size), so a sail that spun about z spins about the

the way turned into the prop's own.

props.doc:
Moves and lights it leaves behind: `during` drops whatever happens only in part of the loop (a witch who appears
and goes stands there instead), `pass` drops going by (a billboard Turkey Run slides past stands still).

What in a scene stands outside every prop it marks, each as `where: what`: a part on a bone that is no prop's, a

Lifts props out of a scene description and leaves what is left as its land. A light goes with the first prop whose

Compiles a project apart, the land and each prop on their own, which is what an editor wants: moving one prop

entries.name: mergedSpec

The whole project on one grid: the land's bones first (as its own pose expects), then each prop's under them as

scene would. With it, `mergedBones` maps each prop's bones into this skeleton.

entries.name: composeScene
entries.doc:
A scene written as a land and props set down on it (a `SceneProject`, the same thing Scene Creator saves) made into
one ordinary description, so Diorama, every style, the weather and the water draw it as they draw any scene.

The props are named, not copied: a scene that sets down the library's stone lantern gets the lantern as the library
has it today, so a change to a prop (its light, its sway) reaches every scene that uses it (Matt, 2026-11-21).

The land comes as it is (its sky, air, water, light, look and camera are the scene's). Each prop's parts keep their
shapes and paint as written and say where they were set down (`PartDoc.placed`); its bones, moves and lights are
moved, turned and sized here, and its bones renamed `<prop><i>/<bone>` so two of one prop never share a name.

signatures.code: composeScene(project: SceneProject, find: (id: string) => PropDoc | undefined): SceneDoc

modules.title: Tags on props and lands
modules.doc:
Tags for props and lands (Matt, 2026-11-22): words from one fixed list, so a search finds a thing by what it is and
the shared recipes act on what it is like, rather than guessing from its name. A tag outside the list is a mistake
the scene checker names, not a word that quietly does nothing.

Three sorts: a `kind` says what a prop is (search finds it by that), a `land` tag what a land is, and a `quality`
says how it behaves, which a recipe acts on.

entries.doc: What sort of tag it is: what a prop is, what a land is, or how a thing behaves.

entries.name: TagInfo

modules.title: Water in a scene written as data

entries.name: WAVE_LEVEL
entries.doc: How high one level of wind waves stands (the root mean square of the height), as a share of the scene's rain splash depth.

entries.name: SceneWater
entries.doc:
The water of a scene written as data (`SceneDoc.water`), played as the scene plays: from the time alone.

A scene repeats, and can be shown at any moment of its loop in any order (paused, stepped frame by frame to record
it), so its water can't be stepped along with the clock. Instead one whole loop of it is worked out here, once:
the pond (water.ts, the wave equation on a grid) is run through the loop with every raindrop of the scene's rain
splashing where and when it lands and every body the scene names pushing its own volume aside as its bone carries
it through the surface. It is run through a few loops first, so that the rings still crossing the pond when the
loop starts are the ones the end of the loop leaves, and the last run is kept as heights at `fps` moments a
second. `show` then lays the heights for a time back on the pond and shapes and colors the surface's blobs.

Nothing is drawn or keyed by hand: change the rain, the banks or a fish's path and the rings follow.

ctor.code: new SceneWater(scene: CompiledScene, options?: { fps?: number; warm?: number })

props.name: plan
props.doc: The scene's water as it was planned.

props.name: water
props.doc: The pond: its grid, and its heights at the time last shown.

props.name: surface
props.doc: The blobs that draw the surface, for the world (`reshape` it after each `show`).

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds before the water repeats: the scene's loop.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many moments of the loop are kept.

props.name: foam
props.doc: Foam on each cell as last laid by `set`, 0 to 1 (`WaterDoc.foam`); all 0 where the scene has none.

props.name: spray
props.doc:
Spray thrown up where the water strikes something hard enough (with `WaterDoc.foam`): droplets on one still
bone, placed for the moment by `show` (hand it to the stage beside the surface and `reshape` it too). It stays
blobs when the scene is drawn as blocks. None when the scene has no foam.

props.name: bursts
props.doc: Every burst of spray in the loop: where, when, which way away from what it struck, and how hard (0 to 1).

props.name: lava
props.doc: The heat over the pool where the scene's water is lava (`WaterPlan.lava`), as it stands after the loop was worked out.

props.name: potion
props.doc: The dye and froth over the pool where the scene's water is a potion (`WaterPlan.potion`), as they stand after the loop was worked out.

props.name: glowNow
props.doc: Each cell's glow as last laid by `set`, 0 to 1, where it is lava; a potion's dye, then its froth, a block of cells each.

props.name: swell
props.doc: How far each cell is under a bubble swelling to pop, 0 to 1, as last laid by `set`, where it is a potion.

props.name: waves
props.doc: How rough the wind makes the water, in levels (`addWind`): 0 for none.

props.name: rain
props.doc: How much of the rain from outside the scene (`addRain`) is falling: the share of its swarm out, 0 to 1.

methods.name: ride
methods.doc:
Stands each float of the scene (`WaterDoc.floats`) on the water as it is `t` seconds into the loop: its bone rises
and falls with the surface at its point and tips with the slope across its size, steepened as the surface is
drawn, on top of the pose the scene gave it. Call it after the scene's pose; it updates the skeleton.

signatures.code: ride(sk: Skeleton, t: number): void

methods.name: addRain
methods.doc:
Rain from outside the scene (weather laid over it) on the pond, in bands of its swarm: `bands` are the shares of
the swarm where each ends (ascending, the last 1), and `rain` (0 to 1, the share of the swarm out) then says how
much of each band falls. Each band's rings are worked out on their own, through the same loops: the wave
equation is linear, so the pond with them is the pond without plus their rings. Costs a run of the loop a band.

signatures.code: addRain(drops: readonly WaterDrop[], bands: readonly number[]): void

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc:
`addRain` and `addWind` worked out a little at a time, `budget` milliseconds a slice with the page let go between
(they cost about a second, which froze the page when weather was first picked). Each band of rain and the wind
join the water as each is done. Resolves when all are.

signatures.code: prepare(drops: readonly WaterDrop[], bands: readonly number[], way: readonly [number, number], budget?: number): Promise<void>

methods.name: addWind
methods.doc:
Waves the wind raises, worked out once (`way`: where it blows to, x and z), at the height of one level of
`waves`. Wind that presses on the water in long rolls running its way, a few at a time and gusting, each
repeating a whole number of times a loop and moving at the water's own speed, so they build into waves the pond
carries (and its banks throw back) and the loop still joins. Linear, as rain's rings are: `waves` levels of it is
`waves` times the field. Costs a run of the loop.

signatures.code: addWind(way?: readonly [number, number]): void

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Lays the water as it stands `t` seconds into the loop back on the pond (`water.h`), blended between the two kept moments round it.

signatures.code: set(t: number): void

methods.name: show
methods.doc:
Makes the surface's blobs ready for the scene at `t` seconds, seen from `eye`: lifted and tilted to the water,
and colored for that eye. `mirror` is a picture of what the water mirrors (`SplatMirror`), `lights` the lamps
whose glints it catches. Hand `surface` to `SplatWorld.reshape` (or `Stage.reshape`) afterward.

signatures.code: show(t: number, eye: ArrayLike<number>, options?: { mirror?: MirrorImage | null; lights?: readonly PointLight[] }): void

entries.name: shadeLava
entries.doc: Colors each blob of a lava surface by the glow of the cell it lies in (`lavaColor`), solid.

signatures.code: shadeLava(s: WaterSurface, glow: Float32Array, ramp: [Vec3, Vec3, Vec3, Vec3]): void

entries.name: shadePotion
entries.doc:
Colors each blob of a potion's surface (`potionColor`): by the dye and froth of the cell it lies in, deep in the
hollows and lit on the crests (by the surface's curvature), and paler and shinier over a bubble about to pop. Solid.

signatures.code: shadePotion(s: WaterSurface, brew: Float32Array, swell: Float32Array, p: PotionPlan): void

entries.name: Burst
entries.doc: A burst of spray: thrown at `at` seconds into the loop from (x, z), away from what was struck along (ox, oz).

props.name: x
props.doc: Where it was thrown from, on the water: x.

props.name: z
props.doc: Where it was thrown from, on the water: z.

props.name: at
props.doc: Seconds into the loop.

props.name: ox
props.doc: The way out from what was struck, a unit pair: x.

props.name: oz
props.doc: The way out from what was struck, a unit pair: z.

props.name: strength
props.doc: How hard, 0 to 1: how high its droplets go.
