entries.doc: How fast the wind crosses a fire at each of its levels, in bed radii a second.

entries.name: DIE
entries.doc: Seconds a fire takes to die down from full to out, and to catch again, and to change from one way of burning to another.

entries.name: CATCH
entries.doc: Seconds a fire takes to die down from full to out, and to catch again, and to change from one way of burning to another.

entries.name: CHANGE
entries.doc: Seconds a fire takes to die down from full to out, and to catch again, and to change from one way of burning to another.

entries.name: fuelUnder
entries.doc:
How much of its fuel a fire burns under a sky (Matt, 2026-11-22): all of it in light rain and in snow, half in rain
and in heavy snow, none in heavy rain or a thunderstorm, and none in a gale, which blows it out.

signatures.code: fuelUnder(sky: FireWeather): number

entries.name: burningAt
entries.doc:
The ways of burning that make up a fire burning `fuel` of its fuel, each with its share: the two it lies between of
burning well, burning low, dying and embers. A fire that is out is its embers, which still warm the air over them.

signatures.code: burningAt(fuel: number): { fuel: number; share: number }[]

entries.name: smokeAt
entries.doc: How much smoke a fire burning `fuel` of its fuel gives, 0 to 1: none burning well, the most burning low, a wisp off its embers.

signatures.code: smokeAt(fuel: number): number

entries.name: shapeUnder
entries.doc: A planned fire's shape under a wind of a level (a whole one) burning a share of its fuel: a harder wind throws more sparks, a lower fire fewer.

signatures.code: shapeUnder(base: FireShape, level: number, fuel: number): FireShape

entries.name: fireShape
entries.doc: What decides how a planned fire burns, wherever it is.

signatures.code: fireShape(f: FirePlan): FireShape

entries.name: SceneFire
entries.doc:
The fires of a scene written as data (`SceneDoc.fires`), played as the scene plays: from the time alone.

A scene repeats and can be shown at any moment of its loop in any order, so its fires can't be stepped along with
the clock. One whole loop of each is worked out here, once (`runFire`), and `show(t)` puts every tracer where the
loop has it at that moment. The tracers are blobs of an actor of their own beside the scene's (`actor`: glowing,
and `soft`, so they stay blobs among a Blocks scene's cubes), which the page hands the stage with the scene and
sends up again after each `show`. `shine` makes each fire's light as bright as the fire burns at that moment.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Every fire's tracers as blobs on one still bone: hand it to the stage beside the scene.

props.name: plans
props.doc: The fires it plays.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds the scene's loop lasts.

props.name: kept
props.doc: One kept loop a fire, burning in still air with nothing against it.

props.name: fuel
props.doc: How much of its fuel each fire burns just now, 1 with nothing against it and 0 when it is out (`under` moves it).

methods.name: under
methods.doc:
Sets the fires under a sky, `seconds` after the last time it was told (Infinity, or the first time: at once).
Rain and wind take the fuel they burn (`fuelUnder`) and a fire dies down over `DIE` seconds, to nothing when it is
put out, and catches again over `CATCH`; the wind's level picks a loop played in that wind, so the flame is
really blown over, in the weather's own gusts. A loop not played yet is played a little each call and the fire
burns as it did until it is there. Call it before `show`; never called, the fires burn in still air.

signatures.code: under(sky: FireWeather, seconds: number): void

methods.name: show
methods.doc:
Puts every tracer where it is `t` seconds into the loop: between the two kept moments either side, a blob as hot
as its gas, drawn longer along the way it is moving, as a lick of flame is, in the color of all the hot gas seen
through it from `eye` (with no eye, of its own heat).

signatures.code: show(t: number, eye?: ArrayLike<number>): void

methods.name: shine
methods.doc:
The scene's lights with each fire's own as bright as the fire burns `t` seconds into the loop: its strength times
the fire's power at that moment beside its mean, in place of the flicker it was written with.

signatures.code: shine(lights: PointLight[], t: number): PointLight[]

modules.title: Weather, clouds and wind as recipes
modules.doc:
Weather and cloud cover as recipes (Matt, 2026-11-21: reusable recipes applied to every scene the same way, so a
change to rain changes rain everywhere, and a thunderstorm on the campfire is one switch). Pure and tested.

A recipe is a few numbers (`SkyState`): how much rain and snow falls, how much of the sky is cloud, what the light
is multiplied by, how gray and dark the sky turns, how thick the air is, and whether lightning flashes. Nothing in
it knows a scene. What is drawn is laid over a scene, never cut into it: the rain, snow and clouds are three small
descriptions of their own (`weatherDocs`), compiled against the scene's ground so drops land on it, and the light,
sky and haze are numbers a page hands the stage each frame. So going from one weather to another is a change of
numbers, eased by `SkyEase`, and the scene is never cut again for it.

entries.name: WeatherId
entries.doc: A weather of `WEATHERS`.

entries.name: CloudId
entries.doc: A cloud cover of `CLOUD_COVERS`.

entries.name: WindId
entries.doc: A wind of `WINDS`.

entries.name: SkyState
entries.doc: What the sky is doing, as numbers that can be mixed.

props.name: rain
props.doc: How much of the rain falls, 0 to 1 (a share of `RAIN_MOST` drops).

props.name: snow
props.doc: How much of the snow falls, 0 to 1 (a share of `SNOW_MOST` flakes).

props.name: clouds
props.doc: How much of the sky is cloud, 0 to 1 (a share of `CLOUDS` clouds).

props.name: light
props.doc: What multiplies everything but the scene's own lamps and what glows (linear).

props.name: gray
props.doc: How far the sky's colors turn to an overcast gray, 0 to 1.

props.name: dark
props.doc: How much darker the sky is drawn, 0 to 1.

props.name: haze
props.doc: How thick the air is, 0 (the scene's own) to 1 (fog).

props.name: lightning
props.doc: How strong the lightning is, 0 for none.

props.name: wind
props.doc: How hard the wind blows, in levels from 0 (calm: the scene's own) to `WIND_MOST`: it slants what falls and raises waves on water.

entries.name: CLEAR
entries.doc: The sky left as the scene has it.

entries.name: CloudCover
entries.doc: A cloud cover: how much of the sky is cloud and what that does to the light and the sky's colors.

props.name: id
props.doc: The word an address or a saved scene holds.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name as a page shows it.

props.name: clouds
props.doc: The share of the clouds that are out.

props.name: light
props.doc: What it multiplies the light by (linear).

props.name: gray
props.doc: How far it turns the sky's colors to gray, 0 to 1.

props.name: dark
props.doc: How much darker it draws the sky, 0 to 1.

entries.name: CLOUD_COVERS
entries.doc: The cloud covers, from a few clouds to a sky full of them.

entries.name: WeatherRecipe
entries.doc: A weather as numbers: what falls, how thick the air is, the light, the lightning and the wind it comes with.

props.name: id
props.doc: The word an address or a saved scene holds.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name as a page shows it.

props.name: clouds
props.doc: The least cloud it comes with: rain does not fall from a clear sky.

props.name: rain
props.doc: How much of the rain falls, 0 to 1.

props.name: snow
props.doc: How much of the snow falls, 0 to 1.

props.name: haze
props.doc: How thick it makes the air, 0 to 1 (fog).

props.name: light
props.doc: What it multiplies the light by, on top of its clouds'.

props.name: dark
props.doc: How much darker again it draws the sky.

props.name: lightning
props.doc: How strong its lightning is; none when left out.

props.name: wind
props.doc: The least wind it comes with, a level of `WINDS` (Matt, 2026-11-21: water a level rougher under rain, two under heavy rain, three in a thunderstorm).

props.name: gloom
props.doc: Whether it is gloomy enough by day that lamps waiting for the dark come on.

entries.name: WEATHERS
entries.doc: The weathers every scene shares: change one here and it changes in every scene.

entries.name: weatherAsked
entries.doc: The weather a word names (from an address, say), or undefined when it names none.

entries.name: cloudsAsked
entries.doc: The cloud cover a word names, or undefined when it names none.

entries.name: skyState
entries.doc:
The sky for a weather, a cloud cover and a wind, any left out. Weather brings at least its own clouds; more cloud
than that may be asked for, less may not. It brings its own wind too, which any wind asked for replaces.

signatures.code: skyState(weather?: WeatherId, clouds?: CloudId, wind?: WindId): SkyState

entries.name: gloomy
entries.doc: Whether lamps that wait for the dark come on under this weather though it is day.

entries.name: isClear
entries.doc: Whether a sky is the scene's own, with nothing laid over it.

entries.name: mixSky
entries.doc: A sky `k` of the way from one to another.

signatures.code: mixSky(a: SkyState, b: SkyState, k: number): SkyState

entries.name: WINDS
entries.doc: How hard the wind blows: a level each, calm first. `slant` is how far sideways it carries rain for each unit it falls.
entries.type: { id: WindId; label: string; slant: number }[]

entries.name: WIND_MOST
entries.doc: The hardest wind, a level (`SkyState.wind`).

entries.name: windAsked
entries.doc: The wind a word names, or undefined when it names none.

entries.name: WIND_WAY
entries.doc: Where the wind blows, x and z (one long), the same in every scene.

entries.name: windAt
entries.doc:
The wind at `t` seconds into a loop of `loop`, for a sky: how far sideways it carries rain a unit of fall, [x, z].
Its level's slant (between levels, between their slants), in gusts a whole number of times a loop so a loop joins.

signatures.code: windAt(s: SkyState, t: number, loop: number): [number, number]

entries.name: gustAt
entries.doc: How hard the wind blows at `u` of the loop as a share of its level's own: gusts a whole number of times a loop.

entries.name: gustRun
entries.doc: `gustAt` summed from the loop's start to `u` (loops), so a thing the wind turns turns a little quicker in each gust and still joins the loop: u at 0 and 1 differ by 1 exactly.

entries.name: windLevelOf
entries.doc: The level of wind (`SkyState.wind`, 0 to `WIND_MOST`) that carries as far as `carry` does a unit of fall, gusts taken as the level's own.

signatures.code: windLevelOf(carry: number): number

entries.name: SKY_EASE
entries.doc: Seconds a change of weather takes.

entries.name: SkyEase
entries.doc:
The sky on its way from what it was to what was asked for: `set` a new one at a time (seconds on any clock) and
`at` gives the sky for a later time, there after `SKY_EASE` seconds. A change made while another is under way
starts from wherever the sky had got to.

props.name: seconds
props.doc: Seconds a change takes.

props.name: target
props.doc: The sky asked for.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: `now` of Infinity puts the sky there at once.

signatures.code: set(to: SkyState, now: number): void

methods.name: moving
methods.doc: Whether it is still changing at `now`.

signatures.code: moving(now: number): boolean

methods.name: at
methods.doc: The sky at `now`: a mix of the sky it left and the one asked for.

signatures.code: at(now: number): SkyState

entries.name: BOLT_EVERY
entries.doc: Seconds between bolts, about.

entries.name: BOLT_SECONDS
entries.doc: Seconds one bolt's light lasts.

entries.name: lightningAt
entries.doc:
How bright lightning is `t` seconds into a loop of `loop`, 0 to 1: a bolt about every `BOLT_EVERY` seconds, each
at its own moment by a hash, as a flash, a dip and a second flash that dies away. At most two flashes a bolt, so
never more than three a second. The same in every loop, so a loop joins.

signatures.code: lightningAt(t: number, loop: number): number

entries.name: FLASH_LIGHT
entries.doc: How much a full flash adds to the light, a channel: bluish white.

entries.name: FLASH_SKY
entries.doc: The sky at the top of a flash (sRGB 0 to 255).

entries.name: lightUnder
entries.doc: The light under a sky, with `flash` (0 to 1) of a bolt in it.

signatures.code: lightUnder(s: SkyState, flash?: number): Vec3

entries.name: skyUnder
entries.doc: A sky color (sRGB 0 to 255) under a sky: turned toward an overcast gray, darkened, and lit by a flash.

signatures.code: skyUnder(c: readonly number[], s: SkyState, flash?: number): Rgb

entries.name: hazeUnder
entries.doc:
The haze a sky lays on a scene seen from `distance`, in units past the view's target as a scene's own haze is
(`from` where it starts, `to` where it would be total), or none where the sky brings none. Thin for rain, a wall for fog.

signatures.code: hazeUnder(s: SkyState, distance: number): { from: number; to: number } | undefined

entries.name: RAIN_MOST
entries.doc: The most drops of rain and flakes of snow: each is a bone, and a blob names its bones in a byte.

entries.name: SNOW_MOST
entries.doc: The most drops of rain and flakes of snow: each is a bone, and a blob names its bones in a byte.

entries.name: CLOUDS
entries.doc: How many clouds there are at full cover.

entries.name: WEATHER_COLORS
entries.doc: The colors weather brings: a palette that pixel art snaps to needs them.

entries.name: CLOUD_HEIGHT
entries.doc: How high over the view's target the clouds float, as a share of the view's distance: near the top of the picture as the view starts.

entries.name: cloudBase
entries.doc: The height of the clouds' flat undersides for a view: what falls starts there, so rain comes down from under the clouds.

entries.name: fallReach
entries.doc: How far round the view's target rain and snow fall: half the side of their square.

entries.name: aboveView
entries.doc:
The height rain and snow start from with the clouds left out (Matt, 2026-11-21: clouds close over a small scene
looked strange, the koi pond's nearly touching its tree and bamboo): over the top of the picture as the view
starts, wherever in their square they come down, so they fall in from above the frame.

signatures.code: aboveView(camera: Orbit & { swing?: number }): number

entries.name: falling
entries.doc: Rain or snow over the middle of a view, falling from the clouds' height (or `top`) onto whatever stands there: one swarm, for any scene.

signatures.code: falling(kind: "snow" | "rain", camera: Orbit & { swing?: number }, count?: number, top?: number): SpeckDoc

entries.name: cloudAt
entries.doc: Where cloud `i` floats for a view: its flat underside at `cloudBase`, over the scene.

signatures.code: cloudAt(i: number, camera: Orbit & { swing?: number }): Vec3

entries.name: CloudLook
entries.doc: How a sky's clouds look: their colors from underneath up, and whether they glow to keep them. The recipe's own when left out.

props.name: colors
props.doc: The clouds' colors from underneath up.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Whether they glow, which keeps them their own color at night.

entries.name: weatherDocs
entries.doc:
The weather for a view, as three descriptions laid over any scene: the clouds, the rain and the snow. Each holds
the most there can be; `poseWeather` shows the share a sky asks for. Rain and snow start at `top` (the clouds'
undersides, or `aboveView` for a sky with its clouds left out). Compile them with the scene's `ground`, so what
falls lands on the scene.

signatures.code: weatherDocs(camera: Orbit & { swing?: number }, loop: number, look?: CloudLook, top?: number): { clouds: SceneDoc; rain: SceneDoc; snow: SceneDoc }

entries.name: shareOut
entries.doc: How much of thing `i` of `n` is out when `share` of them are: all of the first ones, none of the last, one in between.
entries.type: (i: number, n: number, share: number) => number

entries.name: WeatherBones
entries.doc: The bones of a compiled weather description that a sky shows more or fewer of.

props.name: clouds
props.doc: The clouds' bones, in the order they come out.

props.name: specks
props.doc: The bones of the drops or flakes, in the order they start to fall.

props.name: hidden
props.doc: Bones that are never shown.

entries.name: weatherBones
entries.doc: Finds a compiled weather description's bones by their names.

signatures.code: weatherBones(names: readonly string[]): WeatherBones

entries.name: showWeather
entries.doc:
After a weather description's own pose (before the bones are worked out): shows `falls` of its drops or flakes and
`clouds` of its clouds, by size, so a sky on its way from one weather to another has its rain thin out or come on
a drop at a time.

signatures.code: showWeather(size: Float32Array, bones: WeatherBones, falls: number, clouds: number): void

modules.title: Weather over a scene
modules.doc:
Weather laid over a scene (skyRecipes.ts has the recipes): the rain, snow and clouds as actors of their own beside
the scene's, shown by the numbers of a sky that may be on its way from one weather to another. The scene itself is
never cut again for the weather.

entries.name: WeatherScene
entries.doc: What the weather needs to know of the scene it is laid over.

props.name: loop
props.doc: Seconds before the scene repeats: the weather's loop too.

props.name: view
props.doc: The view the scene starts from: the clouds are laid out over it, and rain and snow fall over what it shows.

props.name: heavens
props.doc: The scene's own sky (`SceneDoc.heavens`): its clouds' colors, and how many are out whatever the weather.

props.name: ground
props.type: (x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number) => number
props.doc: Where something falling comes to rest (`CompiledScene.ground`). Left out, nothing lands and no snow lies.

props.name: lying
props.type: (x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number) => Lying
props.doc:
Where snow lies, on moving things too, with the bone that carries it (`CompiledScene.lying`), and the scene's
bones it numbers: snow lying then rides what it lies on (`SceneWeather.follow`). Left out, it lies on `ground` only.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The scene's bones, which `lying`'s bone numbers index.

props.name: water
props.doc: The scene's water, which rain rings and wind roughens.

props.name: sun
props.doc: The way to the scene's sun, which shades snow lying on faces turned from it.

props.name: lights
props.type: readonly { position: readonly number[]; color: readonly number[]; range: number }[]
props.doc: The scene's lights as it starts: snow melts round a warm one.

entries.name: SceneWeather
entries.doc: The rain, snow and clouds for one scene: made once (it finds where every drop lands), then posed by time and sky.

ctor.code: new SceneWeather(d: WeatherScene, options?: { overhead?: boolean })

props.name: actors
props.doc: The clouds, the rain, the snow, then the snow lying: drawn in the scene's world as `extras`.

props.name: ready
props.doc: Resolves once the water's rain and wind are worked out (at once for a scene with no water).

props.name: cover
props.doc: The snow lying on the scene, which builds up while snow falls (`pile`).

props.name: overhead
props.doc: Whether the clouds are drawn over the scene; without them rain and snow come in from over the top of the picture.

methods.name: follow
methods.doc:
Hands the snow lying the scene's pose, so it stays on what it lies on: call it once the scene's skeleton `sk` is
posed and updated for the frame (after the wind, the water's rocking and pokes).

signatures.code: follow(sk: Skeleton): void

methods.name: pile
methods.doc: Sets how deep the snow lying is, 0 to 1. Returns whether it changed by enough to send up again (`Stage.reshape(cover)`).

signatures.code: pile(depth: number): boolean

methods.name: shade
methods.doc:
Turns the clouds as gray and dark as the sky they are in (`skyUnder`'s gray), so a heavy cover reads as cloud, not
as a sky of a scene's own dusk-blue clouds. Returns whether they changed by enough to send up again
(`Stage.reshape(actors[0])`).

signatures.code: shade(s: SkyState): boolean

methods.name: pose
methods.doc: Poses both for `t` seconds under a sky.

signatures.code: pose(t: number, s: SkyState): void

entries.name: paletteUnder
entries.doc:
A palette for a scene under a sky: its colors as that light leaves them and the sky's own first, then the weather's
(cloud, rain, snow) and its own as they were, joined down to what a palette holds. Pixel art snaps to it.

signatures.code: paletteUnder(colors: readonly Rgb[], sky: readonly (number | readonly number[] | undefined)[], s: SkyState): Rgb[]

entries.name: TimeId
entries.doc: A time of `TIMES`.

entries.name: TimeOfDay
entries.doc: A time of day: its sky, its light, and whether it is dark.

props.name: id
props.doc: The word an address or a saved scene holds.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name as a page shows it.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky, top and bottom, as a description writes one.

props.name: light
props.doc: What multiplies everything but the scene's own lamps and what glows (linear).

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the sun or moon stands, in degrees, for a look that lights the scene itself.

props.name: dark
props.doc: Whether lamps that wait for the dark are lit.

props.name: hour
props.doc: The hour a live sun stands at for it (Scene Creator's Light mode sets its clock to this).

entries.name: TIMES
entries.doc: The times of day a scene can be set in.

entries.name: timeAsked
entries.doc: The time asked for by name (`?time=night`), or none: the scene as it is written.

entries.name: timeOf
entries.doc: The time with an id.

entries.name: under
entries.doc: A color (sRGB 0–255) as it looks under a light.

signatures.code: under(c: readonly number[], light: readonly number[]): Rgb

entries.name: paletteAt
entries.doc:
A palette for a scene at a time of day: its own colors as the time's light leaves them, the sky's two, then its own
as they were (what its lamps light and what glows keep those), joined down to what a palette holds. Pixel art snaps
to it, so a scene made for the day has its night's colors to snap to.

signatures.code: paletteAt(colors: readonly Rgb[], time: TimeOfDay): Rgb[]

modules.title: The shared sky: moon, sun, stars and clouds

entries.name: HeavensDoc
entries.doc:
The sun, the moon, the stars and a scene's own clouds as shared recipes (Matt, 2026-11-21: scenes use a reusable
sun, moon and clouds unless one calls for something of its own, an eclipse, a red sun, three moons). A description
says where its moon hangs and how big, how many stars and where, and how cloudy its sky is; what they look like is
written here once. Pure and tested.

The moon, sun and stars are cut into the scene (`withHeavens`, which `compileScene`, `litFor` and `splitScene` call
first), each on a bone of its own named with a `~` (`~moon`, `~sun`, `~star<n>`), so cloud cover can put them out by
size without the scene being cut again (`showHeavens`), and Blocks draws them as small cubes. They wait for their
time like any part: the moon and stars are `lit: 'night'`, the sun `lit: 'day'`. The clouds are not cut into the
scene: they are the weather's own clouds (skyRecipes.ts), drawn over the scene in the colors the scene asks for, so
a scene's few clouds and a storm's many are one kind of cloud.

props.name: moon
props.type: { at: Vec3; r: number; colors?: [string, string] }
props.doc: The moon: its middle and radius; `colors` its face and its craters.

props.name: sun
props.type: { at: Vec3; r: number; color?: string }
props.doc: The sun: its middle and radius, and its color.

props.name: stars
props.type: { count: number; from?: Vec3; to?: Vec3; size?: number; colors?: string[] }
props.doc:
Stars (at most `MOST_STARS`), scattered by a hash through the box `from` to `to`, or through the sky behind the
view's target when it is left out, never on the moon; `size` is a star's radius, `colors` taken in turn by a hash.

props.name: clouds
props.type: { cover: CloudId; colors?: [string, string, string]; glow?: boolean }
props.doc: How cloudy the sky is as the scene stands, and the clouds' colors from underneath up; `glow` keeps them their own color at night.

entries.name: MOST_STARS
entries.doc: The most stars a scene's sky may ask for.

entries.name: MOON_COLORS
entries.doc: The moon's own colors, its face and its craters, where a scene gives none.

entries.name: SUN_COLOR
entries.doc: The sun's own color.

entries.name: STAR_COLORS
entries.doc: The stars' own colors.

entries.name: starAt
entries.doc: Where star `i` of a scene's stars stands: in their box, or in the sky behind the view's target; off the moon.

signatures.code: starAt(doc: Pick<SceneDoc, "camera" | "heavens">, i: number): Vec3

entries.name: withHeavens
entries.doc: A scene's moon, sun and stars as parts on bones of their own, after everything else; its clouds are left to the weather.

signatures.code: withHeavens(doc: SceneDoc): SceneDoc

entries.name: ownClouds
entries.doc: The share of the weather's clouds a scene's own sky has out.

entries.name: HeavenBones
entries.doc: The bones of a compiled scene that cloud cover puts out.

props.name: moon
props.doc: The moon's bone, if the scene has one.

props.name: sun
props.doc: The sun's bone, if the scene has one.

props.name: stars
props.doc: The stars' bones, in the order cloud puts them out.

entries.name: heavenBones
entries.doc: Finds a compiled scene's moon, sun and stars by their bones' names.

signatures.code: heavenBones(names: readonly string[]): HeavenBones

entries.name: STARS_GO
entries.doc: The cover at which stars start to go, and at which the last is gone; the moon and sun go between `BODIES_GO` and 1.

entries.name: BODIES_GO
entries.doc: The cover at which the moon and sun start to go; they are gone at 1.

entries.name: showHeavens
entries.doc:
After a scene's own pose: with `cover` of the sky cloud (0 to 1), puts out the stars one at a time (all of them by a
cloudy sky) and the moon and sun under heavy cloud, by size, so a sky clouding over puts them out as it comes.

signatures.code: showHeavens(size: Float32Array, bones: HeavenBones, cover: number): void

modules.title: Snow that lies
modules.doc:
Snow that lies and builds up (Matt, 2026-11-21: snow and heavy snow should pile up over time and cover the ground).

A layer of flat white blobs laid once over whatever stays put under a stretch of sky, found the way falling snow
finds where it lands (`ground`, a scene's `CompiledScene.ground`): the tops of the land, roofs, walls and rocks, on
faces no steeper than `STEEPEST`. Every blob has its turn to come (`rank`): flat, open ground first and in clumps
(value noise over a few cells), so snow starts as patches that spread and join. `pileSnow(cover, depth)` sets the
layer for a depth from 0 (none) to 1 (all of it lying, a little deeper than a blob is thick): a blob whose turn has
come grows from nothing, and the whole layer rises as it deepens. How deep it is, is the page's: snow builds up
over the time it falls (`pileStep`), which no scene's loop knows.

Snow stays on what it lies on (Matt, 2026-11-24): given a scene's bones and a ground that says which bone carries
each spot (`CompiledScene.lying`), every blob rides its bone, so snow on a swaying crown, a turning sail, a boat on
the waves or anything that walks goes with it. `followSnow` hands the layer each frame's pose; snow on a thing turned
past `SLIDE_FROM` from upright slides off it (shrinks onto its bone) and settles again as it comes back up.

entries.name: STEEPEST
entries.doc: The steepest face snow lies on: the up part of its normal.

entries.name: SnowCover
entries.doc: A layer of snow lying on a scene: an actor of flat white blobs, with what `pileSnow` needs to deepen it.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The layer's blobs, one a spot snow can lie on.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Every blob on the one still bone.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The scene's bones (one still bone when it gave none), posed by `followSnow`.

props.name: soft
props.doc: Drawn as blobs while the stage draws blocks, beside the weather.

props.name: weather
props.doc: It is weather, which the Blocks look draws as cubes or leaves as blobs.

props.name: lies
props.doc: It lies on things: among blocks it is raised onto the cubes' tops.

props.name: rank
props.doc: When each blob comes, 0 to 1: at depth `rank · (1 − GROW)` it starts to grow.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where each blob lies on the surface, x y z, and the surface's normal there.

props.name: normal
props.doc: The surface's normal under each blob, x y z.

props.name: size
props.doc: Each blob's full radius.

props.name: depth
props.doc: The depth the layer was last set for.

props.name: follows
props.doc: For each bone of the layer, its index in the skeleton `followSnow` was last given (-1: none), and that skeleton.

entries.name: Lying
entries.doc: Where a spot of snow lies: the height, and the bone of the scene's that carries it.

entries.name: makeSnowCover
entries.doc:
Lays the layer over a disc of `radius` round (`x`, `z`) at `spacing` between blobs. `ground(x, z, top, bottom)` is
where something falling from `top` comes to rest (`bottom` where it meets nothing); `dry(x, y, z)` leaves out a
spot (water: snow falling on it melts). `sun` (toward the light) shades faces turned away a little blue.

signatures.code: makeSnowCover(ground: (x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number) => number | Lying, options: { x: number; z: number; radius: number; top: number; bottom: number; spacing: number; bones?: readonly Bone[]; sun?: readonly number[]; dry?: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => boolean; warm?: readonly { at: readonly number[]; reach: number }[] }): SnowCover

entries.name: pileSnow
entries.doc: Sets the layer for a depth from 0 to 1. Returns whether anything changed (then hand it to `Stage.reshape`).

signatures.code: pileSnow(cover: SnowCover, depth: number): boolean

entries.name: SLIDE_FROM
entries.doc: Snow slides off a thing turned so its up is no more than this far up (the y of its turned up): gone by level, whole from here.

entries.name: followSnow
entries.doc:
Poses the layer as the scene's skeleton `sk` stands (posed and updated: call it after everything that moves the
scene's bones). Each of the layer's bones takes the skin of the scene's bone of its name, so snow rides what it lies
on; on a bone turned past `SLIDE_FROM` its snow shrinks onto the bone's head. Bones the scene lacks stay at rest.

signatures.code: followSnow(cover: SnowCover, sk: Skeleton): void

entries.name: MELT_SHARE
entries.doc: How far round a light snow melts, as a share of its range at a strength of one: a campfire clears the ground round it, a lamp its own cap.

entries.name: warmthOf
entries.doc: The places a scene's lights keep clear of snow: warm ones only (more red than blue), by how strong they are.

signatures.code: warmthOf(lights: readonly { position: readonly number[]; color: readonly number[]; range: number }[]): { at: readonly number[]; reach: number }[]

entries.name: PILE_SECONDS
entries.doc: How fast the snow lying builds up: a whole cover in about this many seconds of heavy snow.

entries.name: MELT_SECONDS
entries.doc: How many seconds snow takes to melt away once none falls.

entries.name: pileMost
entries.doc:
The most a snowfall of `snow` (0 to 1) lays: heavy snow covers everything, a lighter fall only dusts
(Matt, 2026-11-21: light snow covered too quickly).

entries.name: pileStep
entries.doc:
The depth after `dt` seconds more of `snow` (the share of the swarm falling, 0 to 1): it builds by the square of
how much falls, so light snow (0.4) lays about a sixth as fast as heavy, up to `pileMost`; above that, and when
none falls, it melts.

signatures.code: pileStep(depth: number, snow: number, dt: number): number

entries.name: Shape
entries.doc:
A voxel builder for pixel-art scenes: shapes given as distance functions are
cut into a grid, and every grid cell on a shape's surface becomes one small,
nearly solid blob, a disc lying flat on the surface. Drawn small and snapped to a palette (pixelPass.ts)
a scene of these reads as chunky pixel art with real depth.

Where body.ts scatters flat blobs over a creature's skin and blends them
between bones, this fills a regular grid and hangs each part on one bone, so
parts move rigidly (a lamp turns, a boat bobs) and the grid stays crisp.

Light is baked into the colors: one sun, an ambient floor, and shadows cast
by every part on every other, found by marching from each blob toward the
sun through the scene's shapes in the rest pose. `glow` parts keep their
color and cast no shadow. Three optional touches a pixel artist would paint
(all off unless the light asks): `ramp` turns shade cool and light warm
instead of only darker, `crevice` darkens what is shut in by other surfaces,
and `wear` lightens edges. A part's `grime` collects where it is shut in.

props.name: sdf
props.type: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => number
props.doc: Distance to the surface: negative inside.

props.name: min
props.doc: A box that holds the whole shape.

props.name: max
props.doc: The far corner of a box that holds it.

props.name: pieceAt
props.doc:
For a shape made of many pieces (the bricks of a wall, the posts of a fence, the columns of a basalt
causeway): which piece a surface point belongs to, as a whole number 0 or more, or -1 for what lies between
them (mortar). The `pieces` paint gives every piece a color of its own.

entries.name: VoxelPart
entries.doc: One part of a voxel scene: a shape, its paint and the bone that carries it.

props.name: shape
props.doc: The part's shape, as a distance function.

props.name: color
props.doc: Color (0–1, sRGB) or color at a surface point given its outward normal.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it.

props.name: glow
props.doc: Unlit and casting no shadow: lamps, windows, beams of light.

props.name: laid
props.doc: Laid on other parts (a pane on its frame): none of its cells is left out for lying inside a neighbor, so its face is whole and the face under it is what goes.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: How solid its blobs are, 0–1.

props.name: noShadow
props.doc: Casts no shadow on other parts (thin things far from the ground, like birds).

props.name: grime
props.doc: A color (sRGB, 0–1) that gathers in its hollows and creases, as moss or dirt does. Needs the light's `crevice` to find them.

props.name: bare
props.doc: Takes none of the scene's `cover`: water, glass, anything that moves through it or was just made.

props.name: ink
props.doc: Little drawn marks over the surface: see Ink.

props.name: glass
props.doc: Water, ice or glass: see Glass. Needs the spec's `eye`.

props.name: strokes
props.doc:
Dabs that follow the form: 0 leaves each cell a round disc; up to 1 draws it as a stroke along the level line
round the shape, as a painter's brush goes round a pot or a trunk. Seen as blobs it reads as brushwork; in pixel
mode it barely shows.

entries.name: Glass
entries.doc:
A surface you see into and that mirrors what is over it, baked for one place to look from (the spec's `eye`, the
scene's camera): pixel mode cuts anything faint, so instead of being drawn see-through, each cell takes the color
of what lies behind it on the line from the eye (`see`) and of what its mirror line meets (`mirror`, stronger at a
glancing look, as on real water). Seen from far off the scene's own view it is a painting of glass, not glass.

props.name: see
props.doc: How much of what is behind shows through: 0 to 1.

props.name: mirror
props.doc: How much it mirrors, looked at straight on; more at a glancing look. 0 to 1.

props.name: top
props.doc: Only its upturned faces: a pond cut as one slab whose sides are earth.

entries.name: Ink
entries.doc:
Inked detail: the surface is taken in blocks of 4×4 cells (one picture pixel each in pixel mode), and a share of
the blocks (`amount`) each carry one small mark of the kind, picked, turned and flipped at random per block and with
the blocks of each row shifted, so a big wall never shows a repeat. `color` is the ink; left out, a darker step of
the paint under it.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which marks.

props.name: amount
props.doc: The share of blocks that take a mark, 0–1.

props.name: color
props.doc: The marks' color (sRGB, 0–1); left out, a much darker step of the paint.

entries.name: InkKind
entries.doc: The kinds of mark a part's `ink` can draw on it.

entries.name: INK_MARKS
entries.doc: The marks of each kind, 4×4, top row first. Kinds in UPRIGHT only ever flip side to side: grass grows up, wood grain runs along.

entries.name: inkedAt
entries.doc: Whether the cell at grid (gx, gy, gz) with normal `n` carries ink of this kind: see Ink. `seed` keeps parts apart.

signatures.code: inkedAt(ink: Ink, gx: number, gy: number, gz: number, n: Vec3, seed: number): boolean

entries.name: inkOf
entries.doc: The ink a color takes by default: a darker, slightly richer step of it.

signatures.code: inkOf(c: Vec3): Vec3

entries.name: Cover
entries.doc:
Something laid over the whole scene once it is cut: `snow` settles on tops that the sky can reach, `moss` creeps
over shut-in and up-turned faces in patches, `dust` lies thin on every upturned face, under cover or not.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What lies on the scene.

props.name: color
props.doc: sRGB, 0–1.

props.name: amount
props.doc: 0–1: how much of the scene it takes, from a dusting to most of what faces up.

entries.name: LooseBlob
entries.doc:
A blob placed as it is, not cut from a shape: soft, faint things in the air such as mist or a beam of light. Kept
under LOOSE_MAX opacity, so pixel mode's map of parts never takes one for a surface.

props.name: center
props.doc: Where it is.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Its radii along x, y and z.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color (sRGB, 0–1).

props.name: opacity
props.doc: How solid it is, 0–1.

props.name: bone
props.doc: The bone that carries it.

entries.name: Beam
entries.doc:
A beam of light falling through the scene, as from a window or a gap in the leaves: surfaces inside it that face
back up it are lit by its color, on top of the sun, so the beam shows where it lands.

props.name: from
props.doc: Where it starts.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it lands.

props.name: r
props.doc: Its radius.

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color (sRGB, 0–1).

entries.name: LOOSE_MAX
entries.doc: The most a loose blob may cover: under the engine's PART_CUT, so it never shows in the map of parts.

entries.name: VoxelLight
entries.doc: The light baked into a voxel scene's colors: the sun, the ambient light, cast shadows and the painted touches.

props.name: dir
props.doc: Direction toward the sun.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: Light that reaches everywhere, 0–1.

props.name: shadow
props.doc: How dark a cast shadow is: 0 leaves no shadow, 1 leaves only the ambient light.

props.name: ramp
props.doc: How far shade turns its hue toward cool violet and full sun toward warm yellow, as a painter's ramp does: 0 only darkens.

props.name: crevice
props.doc: How much surfaces shut in by others (corners, cracks, the foot of a wall) darken: 0 to 1.

props.name: wear
props.doc: How much sharp outer edges lighten, as worn stone and wood do: 0 to 1.

props.name: bounce
props.doc: How much color surfaces throw onto what faces them, as a red wall warms the floor beside it: 0 to 1.

props.name: steps
props.doc:
Painted in steps: once a blob's light is worked out, its color is moved onto one color of `palette` (sRGB, 0–1), a
step of its own paint's ramp (the palette colors that paint passes through from deep shade to full sun), so shade
falls in flat bands a pixel pass has nothing left to guess at. `mottle` (0–1, `MOTTLE` when left out) nudges small
patches a little lighter or darker first, so a band's edge is ragged as a brush leaves it, not ruled. Parts that
`glow` keep their color.

entries.name: STEP_L
entries.doc: How much a difference in lightness counts beside one in hue when a blob picks its step (`stepper`): under 1, so hue is kept first.

entries.name: MOTTLE
entries.doc: How ragged the edge between two steps is, where a scene doesn't say (`VoxelLight.steps`).

entries.name: HUE_KEEP
entries.doc:
How far round the hue circle (degrees, in OKLab) a palette color may sit from a paint's own and still be a step of its
ramp (`stepper`), where both have color enough to have a hue (`HUE_FROM`). A red that has no darker red in the palette
stays its own darkest red in shade rather than turning brown or orange, as a hand-made ramp would.

entries.name: HUE_FROM
entries.doc: The chroma (OKLab) under which a color counts as a gray for `HUE_KEEP`: a gray is a step of any paint's ramp.

entries.name: GRAY_TURN
entries.doc:
How far round the hue circle (degrees) a near-gray palette color may sit from the way a gray paint's light tints it
(cool in shade, warm in sun) or from the paint's own faint hue, and still be a step of its ramp (`stepper`). White
sails in shade took the sky's palest blue, which read as holes through to the sky.

entries.name: ESCAPE
entries.doc: How many times closer a palette color off a paint's ramp must be before a blob takes it (`stepper`): only light of another color carries a blob that far.

entries.name: VoxelSpec
entries.doc: A voxel scene for `buildVoxels`: its bones, its parts and the grid's cell size.

props.name: bones
props.doc: The scene's bones.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts, all cut into one shared grid.

props.name: spacing
props.doc: Grid cell size in world units: one blob per surface cell.

props.name: light
props.doc: The baked light; what is left out comes from `DEFAULT_LIGHT`.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: Skip blocks of cells far from a surface: much quicker for big smooth shapes, sound only for honest distance functions (sculpt.ts).

props.name: trueShell
props.doc:
Keep the outermost layer one cell thick in true distance, not in the shape's own units. A shape pushed in and
out (`displace`) can have a distance that changes faster than one unit per unit; read raw, its layer comes out
thinner than a cell and leaves holes you see the far side through. Creatures (sculpt.ts) turn this on.

props.name: keepBuried
props.doc: How deep (world units) a cell may sit inside a neighbor on its bone and still be made: a skirt that keeps a joint closed as parts move.

props.name: disc
props.doc:
A disc's radius (its blob's scale across the surface) as a share of `spacing`. The default leaves the grid
crisp for pixel mode, which cuts alpha; drawn smooth, discs that small let about a tenth of what lies behind
show between them, so a creature seen as blobs wants them wider.

props.name: loose
props.doc: Blobs placed as they are, after the cut ones: see LooseBlob.

props.name: beams
props.doc: Beams of light that fall through the scene.

props.name: cover
props.doc: Snow, moss or dust over every part that isn't `bare` or `glow`: see Cover.

props.name: focus
props.doc:
Where the eye goes: within `r` of `at` the grid is as fine as `spacing`; further out it is twice as coarse, with
discs twice the size, so the subject keeps its detail and the rest is painted broadly in a quarter of the blobs. Only parts at least
eight cells across every way go coarse: a thinner one could miss every coarse cell.

props.name: eye
props.doc: Where `glass` parts are looked at from: the scene's camera.

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky a `glass` part mirrors where its mirror line meets nothing: [overhead, at the horizon]. Dark when left out.

props.name: lamps
props.doc:
Lamps whose shadows are baked, in the order of the live lights they stand for (at most four; a gap is a light
that casts none): for each blob, how much of lamp k it can see goes in byte k of `seen`, and the engine's live
light pass scales that light by it, so a lamp's shadows flicker with it and cost nothing a frame.

entries.name: Lamp
entries.doc: A light that stays put, whose shadows `buildVoxels` works out once for each blob.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it is.

props.name: reach
props.doc: How far its light reaches: blobs further off are not looked at (their byte stays full).

props.name: clear
props.doc:
How far short of it the look toward it stops, so its own housing doesn't shade everything: `LAMP_CLEAR` where
left out. Blobs nearer than this are always lit. Set it to the room round a lamp that sits in a small hollow,
or the hollow's own walls and roof let its light through.

entries.name: MAX_LAMPS
entries.doc: How many lamps' shadows a blob carries, one byte each.

entries.name: LIT_MAX
entries.doc:
The brightest the baked sun makes a surface, as a share of its color. Only
`glow` parts are built brighter, so pixel mode can tell a lamp from a white
wall in the sun (GLOW_FROM in splat-core/pixel.ts sits just over it). Live
lights add on top: a surface under a strong one does pass the line and glow.

entries.name: PAINTED
entries.doc: The painted touches pixel scenes use unless they say otherwise: hue-turning shade, dark crevices, worn edges.
entries.type: { ramp: number; crevice: number; wear: number }

entries.name: DEFAULT_LIGHT
entries.doc: The light a voxel scene gets where it sets none of its own.

entries.name: sphere
entries.doc: A ball of radius `r` about `c`.

signatures.code: sphere(c: Vec3, r: number): Shape

entries.name: ellipsoid
entries.doc: An ellipsoid with radii along x, y and z (the distance is approximate, exact on the surface).

signatures.code: ellipsoid(c: Vec3, r: Vec3): Shape

entries.name: box
entries.doc: A box with half sizes `h`, its edges rounded by `round`.

signatures.code: box(c: Vec3, h: Vec3, round?: number): Shape

entries.name: cone
entries.doc: A rounded cone from a (radius ra) to b (radius rb); equal radii make a capsule.

signatures.code: cone(a: Vec3, b: Vec3, ra: number, rb?: number): Shape

entries.name: cylinder
entries.doc: A upright cylinder with flat ends, from y0 to y1; `r1` tapers it.

signatures.code: cylinder(c: [x: number, z: number], y0: number, y1: number, r0: number, r1?: number): Shape

entries.name: torus
entries.doc: A ring lying flat (about the y axis): `R` to the middle of the tube, `r` the tube's radius.

signatures.code: torus(c: Vec3, R: number, r: number): Shape

entries.name: roof
entries.doc: A roof: a ridge along x at `top`, sloping down to `y0` at `hz` either side.

signatures.code: roof(c: [x: number, z: number], y0: number, top: number, hx: number, hz: number): Shape

entries.name: union
entries.doc: Several shapes as one: a point inside any of them is inside.

signatures.code: union(...s: Shape[]): Shape

entries.name: tighten
entries.doc:
A shape whose distance can overstate by up to 1/k − 1 of itself (a ragged edge, an overhang the side distance
doesn't see) made honest for the sun march: exact within `near` of the surface, where cells are placed, and
scaled by k beyond it, so a step never passes through.

signatures.code: tighten(s: Shape, k: number, near?: number): Shape

entries.name: many
entries.doc:
A union of many scattered shapes, sorted into buckets so a point asks only the shapes near it: quick for fences,
fallen bricks and twigs.

signatures.code: many(shapes: Shape[]): Shape

entries.name: orientedBox
entries.doc:
A box turned any way: `axes` are its three edge directions (unit length, square to each other) and `half` its half
size along each. Fallen bricks, leaning posts, rails between them.

signatures.code: orientedBox(c: Vec3, axes: [Vec3, Vec3, Vec3], h: Vec3, round?: number): Shape

entries.name: BlendKind
entries.doc: How a `blend` meets where its shapes touch: a rounded fillet, a flat bevel, or a run of little steps.

entries.name: blend
entries.doc: Shapes joined so the seam between them is filled in: `r` is how far the fillet, bevel or stairs reach.

signatures.code: blend(kind: BlendKind, r: number, shapes: Shape[], steps?: number): Shape

entries.name: lathe
entries.doc:
A turned shape, as from a lathe: `profile` is [radius, height] pairs from the bottom up, standing on `c`, and the
outline is spun about the upright axis through it. Vases, bells, bottles, chess pieces, lamp posts.

signatures.code: lathe(c: Vec3, profile: [number, number][]): Shape

entries.name: sweep
entries.doc: A tube along a path of points, `r0` thick at the start and `r1` at the end: vines, pipes, rails, a dragon's tail.

signatures.code: sweep(path: Vec3[], r0: number, r1?: number): Shape

entries.name: LETTERS
entries.doc: The 3×5 letters `pixelText` knows, top row first.

entries.name: pixelText
entries.doc:
Words in blocky 3×5 letters (`LETTERS`; lower case is read as upper), `size` tall and `depth` thick, centered on
`at` and reading along +x, or along -z when `facing` is 'x'. A letter needs about five grid cells of height to read.

signatures.code: pixelText(at: Vec3, text: string, size: number, depth: number, facing?: "z" | "x"): Shape

entries.name: letterGrid
entries.doc:
A model drawn as letters: `layers` from the bottom up, each a list of rows from the back (-z) to the front, each
row a string read along +x; any character but '.' or a space fills a cube `size` across. Standing on `at`, centered
on it across. `letterAt` says which letter a point is in, so a paint can color the model by letter.

signatures.code: letterGrid(at: Vec3, size: number, layers: string[][]): Shape & { letterAt: (p: Vec3, n: Vec3) => string | undefined }

entries.name: cut
entries.doc: `a` with `b` cut out of it.

signatures.code: cut(a: Shape, b: Shape): Shape

entries.name: displace
entries.doc: A shape pushed in or out by `f(x, y, z)` world units: ripples, rough rock. `reach` is the most it moves.

signatures.code: displace(s: Shape, f: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => number, reach: number): Shape

entries.name: coverAt
entries.doc:
How much of a cover lies on a surface point, 0–1. `open` is its openness (moss wants it low) and `sky` how much
of the sky straight up it sees (snow wants it high); each is only asked for when the kind needs it.

signatures.code: coverAt(cover: Cover, p: Vec3, n: Vec3, spacing: number, open: () => number, sky: () => number): number

entries.name: bakedColor
entries.doc:
A surface color under the baked light. `shade` is how bright (0 to LIT_MAX), `lit` how much straight sun it takes
(0–1). With `ramp` the color doesn't only darken: shade turns its hue toward violet and gains a little chroma in the
middle tones, full sun leans warm, and even a gray goes cool in shadow, so a palette's cool darks get picked over its
browns. `lift` lightens it (a worn edge). Never brighter than LIT_MAX, which keeps it under pixel mode's glow line.

signatures.code: bakedColor(base: Vec3, shade: number, lit: number, ramp: number, lift?: number): Vec3

entries.name: stepper
entries.doc:
Painting in steps (`VoxelLight.steps`): gives the function that moves a blob's finished color onto its paint's ramp.
A paint's ramp is the palette colors it passes through as its light goes from a deep corner to full sun (found once
per paint, to 1/64 a channel); a finished color takes the nearest of them, after `mottle` has pushed its lightness up
or down by patch. Light of another color (a beam, a bounce, a mirror) can carry a blob well off its ramp: when a
palette color outside it is `ESCAPE` times as close or more, that one is taken. A ramp keeps to its paint's own hue (`HUE_KEEP`). Palette colors over `LIT_MAX` are held at
it, as every lit color is, so nothing painted starts to glow.

signatures.code: stepper(steps: { palette: Vec3[]; mottle?: number }, light: VoxelLight): (base: Vec3, color: Vec3, i: number, j: number, k: number) => Vec3

entries.name: unlit
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it leaving the light out: each blob keeps its paint (with its ink, cover
and grime, which are paint), and no sun, shade, cast shadow, ramp, crevice, wear, bounce or beam is baked into it.
For a look that lights the blobs itself, such as cel shading (`Stage.setCel`), which would otherwise shade a shadow
twice. It reaches builders that take no light of their own to set, such as a creature's `make`.

signatures.code: unlit<T>(make: () => T): T

entries.name: within
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it cutting only the grid points within a box (in the spec's own units,
the rest pose): a finer cut of the ground round one place of a scene too big to cut fine whole.

signatures.code: within<T>(box: { min: Vec3; max: Vec3 }, make: () => T): T

entries.name: banded
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it lighting each blob as one texel in `n` flat bands: the sun's share that
reaches a blob (its facing times its cast shadow) is moved onto the nearest of `n` steps from none to full before its
color is worked out, so light and shade fall in whole blobs, crisp along the surface, while each blob keeps its own
paint (bricks, planks, ripples). The ambient share is left as it is. 0 or 1 leaves the light smooth.

signatures.code: banded<T>(n: number, make: () => T): T

entries.name: hugged
entries.doc:
Runs `make` with every `buildVoxels` inside it fitting the discs along a shape's outer edges to the edge: a disc whose
surface ends within its reach (the shape falls away from the disc's own plane, as past the top of a fence rail or the
rim of a pond) is moved in and squeezed across the edge, long along it, so the row of discs ends in a straight line
where the shape does instead of a row of round bumps standing past it. Inner corners are left alone: what meets them
covers them. See `edgeFit`.

signatures.code: hugged<T>(make: () => T): T

entries.name: edgeFit
entries.doc:
Where the surface of a shape ends within a disc's reach, in the disc's own plane: the way out to the nearest outer edge
(a unit vector in the plane) and how far from the disc's middle the edge lies, or undefined when the surface carries on
all round. `past(q)` is how far the shape lies off the disc's plane at `q`, counted as off past `least`; it is asked at
three distances along `EDGE_WAYS` ways, the nearer ones only where the farthest finds an edge.

signatures.code: edgeFit(p: Vec3, n: Vec3, reach: number, past: (q: Vec3) => number, least: number): { out: Vec3; at: number } | undefined

entries.name: bandOf
entries.doc: Moves a sun share (0 to 1) onto the nearest of `n` steps (`banded`).

signatures.code: bandOf(direct: number, n: number): number

entries.name: buildVoxels
entries.doc:
Builds the scene's blobs, skin and skeleton. Cells sit on one grid shared by
every part (multiples of `spacing` from the origin), so parts line up, and
the same spec always gives the same blobs.

signatures.code: buildVoxels(spec: VoxelSpec): Built

modules.title: Built things: walls, steps, fences, arcades
modules.doc:
Built things: walls of real bricks, flights of worn steps, fences along a path and arcades cut into
equal bays, each one shape however many pieces it has. Pure numbers and distance functions, so the scene builder
cuts them like any other shape, and each shape's `pieceAt` says which brick, block, post or stone a point is on,
for the `pieces` paint.

Every piece is placed by a rule from the shape's own sizes and a seed (the same seed, the same ruin), and sizes are
fitted so the pieces come out whole: a wall's length is a whole number of bricks (half bricks at the ends of every
other course), a span a whole number of bays, so pillars and posts land exactly at its ends.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio built-things kit; this is our own code.

entries.name: hash
entries.doc: A repeatable number in 0..1 from a seed and up to three whole numbers.

signatures.code: hash(seed: number, a: number, b?: number, c?: number): number

entries.name: noise1
entries.doc: Smooth 1D noise in 0..1 with bumps about `size` apart.

signatures.code: noise1(seed: number, u: number, size: number): number

entries.name: WallSpec

entries.name: arcade

modules.title: Formations: crystals, columns, drips
modules.doc:
Formations: shapes that come from a rule rather than placing each one by hand. A faceted crystal and
clusters of them from one root, a geode broken open, basalt columns on a hex grid, stalactites and stalagmites that
join into columns, flowstone down a wall, and icicles under every downward edge of another shape. Pure distance
functions, each with a `pieceAt` for the `pieces` paint.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio formations kit; this is our own code.

entries.name: CrystalSpec
entries.doc: One crystal for `crystal`.

props.name: at
props.doc: Its foot, where it grows out of the rock.

props.name: dir

props.name: length

props.name: r
props.doc: Its radius, corner to middle.

props.name: chips
props.doc: How many chips are knocked off its faces, 0 to 6.

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: crystal
entries.doc: A sided crystal with a pointed end, chipped here and there.

signatures.code: crystal(s: CrystalSpec): Shape

entries.doc: A cluster of crystals growing from one root, for `cluster`.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where they grow from.

props.name: count

props.name: size
props.doc: The longest, in the middle.

props.name: r
props.doc: The radius of the biggest.

props.name: spread
props.doc: How far the outer ones lean, in degrees (50 when left out).

props.name: sides

props.name: chips

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: clusterCrystals

entries.doc:
Icicles under every downward edge of `host`: its box is looked at from below in columns `every` apart, and where a
column meets the underside of the shape but the column beside it doesn't (or meets it much higher up), an icicle
hangs from that edge. Only the icicles are drawn: give the host its own part.

modules.title: Living forms: trees, cacti, shells
modules.doc:
Living forms: trees grown by space colonization, ribbed cacti, succulent rosettes, bracket fungi,
brain coral, shells wound on a log spiral, horns that curl, antlers with tines and a spine of ribs. Pure numbers and
distance functions: each lights, shadows, grows (on a bone with a `sprout` move) and rigs like any other part.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio living-forms kit; this is our own code.

entries.name: TreeSpec
entries.doc: A tree for `tree`, grown by space colonization.

props.name: at
props.doc: The foot of the trunk.

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the trunk rises before the crown.

props.name: crown
props.doc: The crown's radii: the space its branches grow to fill.

props.name: r
props.doc: The trunk's radius at its foot; every limb is as thick as what it carries.

props.name: points
props.doc: Points scattered through the crown that the branches grow toward (160). More makes a finer tree.

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: TreeNode
entries.doc: One joint of a grown tree: its place, the joint it grew from and the limb's radius there.

props.name: p
props.doc: Where the joint is.

props.name: parent
props.doc: The joint it grew from, or -1 for the foot.

props.name: r
props.doc: The limb's radius here.

entries.name: colonize
entries.doc:
Grows a tree by space colonization: points are scattered through the crown, and every point pulls the nearest
branch tip toward it until a branch reaches it. Then each limb is made as thick as what it carries (the pipe rule:
a limb's radius to the 2.5 is the sum of its children's), scaled so the trunk's foot is `r`.

signatures.code: colonize(s: TreeSpec): { nodes: TreeNode[]; ends: number[] }

entries.name: tree
entries.doc: A tree grown by space colonization (see colonize): its limbs, and if `leaves` is set a ball that size at each end.

signatures.code: tree(s: TreeSpec & { leaves?: number; only?: "limbs" | "leaves" }, thin?: number): Shape

modules.title: Worn land
modules.doc:
Worn land and layered rock: a height field worn by water and slumping (droplets carve gullies and drop
what they carry in fans; slopes too steep for their rock slide to scree), rock laid down in beds where soft beds wear
back further than hard ones, so ledges, benches and overhangs come by themselves, with hoodoos and natural arches as
presets; cracked mud whose plates curl at their edges; and pebbles along a stream bed, bigger where it runs fastest.

Everything runs once, when the scene is built, from its numbers and a seed: the same seed, the same land. Erosion
has a budget (`MAX_DROPS`, a grid of at most `MAX_GRID` cells a side) so a build stays within a second or so.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio erosion kit; this is our own code.

entries.name: Bed
entries.doc: A bed of rock: how thick it is and how hard (0 soft, worn back far, to 1 hard, standing out as a ledge).

props.name: thick
props.doc: How thick the bed is.

props.name: hard
props.doc: How hard: 0 is soft and wears back far, 1 is hard and stands out as a ledge.

entries.name: BEDS
entries.doc: Beds when none are given: soft and hard by turns, a hard one on top.

entries.name: bedAt
entries.doc: Which bed a height above the base is in, the beds repeating upward.

signatures.code: bedAt(beds: Bed[], y: number): number

entries.name: LandSpec
entries.doc: Land worn by water, for `land` and `wornLand`.

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of its foot.

props.name: half
props.doc: Half its size along x and z.

props.name: peaks
props.type: { at: [number, number]; h: number; r: number }[]

props.name: noise
props.doc: Rough ground over the hills, as a height.

props.name: drops

props.name: slump
props.doc: How far slopes slump to scree, 0 to 1.

props.name: beds
props.doc: Beds of rock, from the bottom up, repeating: soft ones wear faster. Left out, all one rock.

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: MAX_DROPS
entries.doc: The most water drops a `LandSpec` may ask for.

entries.name: MAX_GRID
entries.doc: The most cells along a side of a land's height grid.

entries.name: Land
entries.doc: Worn land as a grid of heights, from `wornLand`.

props.name: nx
props.doc: Grid points along x.

props.name: nz
props.doc: Grid points along z.

props.name: cell

props.name: x0
props.doc: The grid's first x.

props.name: z0
props.doc: The grid's first z.

props.name: height

props.name: flow

props.name: laid

props.name: thick

methods.name: at

entries.name: wornLand

entries.name: terrace
entries.doc:
Heights remapped into steps by the beds they fall in: going up a slope, a hard bed rises as a cliff (most of its
height over little ground) and then holds level for a bench, while a soft bed rises evenly as a slope.

signatures.code: terrace(beds: Bed[], h: number): number

entries.name: land
entries.doc: Worn land as a shape: its surface from the height field, sides cut straight down, its foot `base` deep. Pieces: the bed a point is in, or -1 where something was laid down (fans and scree).

signatures.code: land(s: LandSpec & { base?: number }): Shape

entries.name: ButteSpec

props.name: at

props.name: height

modules.title: Growers
modules.doc:
Growers: a tree, a coral or a cluster of crystals grown by a branching rule from a seed, so the same
seed always gives the same plant. Pure numbers: `grow` gives the twigs (round-ended sticks, thick to thin) and the
tips, which the scene builder turns into shapes. Each style is a rule: how many branches split from each end, how
far they lean out, how much shorter and thinner each step is, and how hard they pull back toward the sky.

entries.name: GrowStyle
entries.doc: What a grower grows as.

entries.name: GROW_STYLES
entries.doc: Every `GrowStyle`.

entries.name: Grower
entries.doc: A tree, a coral or a cluster of crystals to grow from a seed, for `grow`.

props.name: style
props.doc: What it grows as.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it stands.

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

props.name: size
props.doc: The trunk's length (a crystal's longest spike).

props.name: r
props.doc: The trunk's radius at the foot.

props.name: depth
props.doc: Times it splits; left out, what suits the style.

props.name: branches
props.doc: Branches from each split; left out, what suits the style.

entries.name: Twig
entries.doc: One branch of a grower: a cone from `from`, where its radius is `r`, to `to`, where it is `rTo`.

props.name: from
props.doc: Where it starts.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it ends.

props.name: r
props.doc: Its radius at the start.

props.name: rTo
props.doc: Its radius at the end.

entries.name: MAX_TWIGS
entries.doc: No grower makes more twigs than this, whatever its depth and branches.

entries.name: grow
entries.doc: Grows it: twigs from the foot out, and the tips where the last twigs end.

signatures.code: growBounds(g: Grower): { mid: Vec3; half: Vec3 }

modules.title: Weather that lands
modules.doc:
Weather that lands: what falls finds the ground actually under it, snow lies in drifts shaped by the
wind and what stands in its way, and frost grows across a pane a branch at a time. Pure and tested.

The idea comes from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio weather kit; this is our own code.

entries.name: groundUnder
entries.doc:
The height of the first surface met going straight down from `top` at (x, z), or `bottom` if nothing is met. The
shapes' distances are lower bounds, so each step down is as long as the distance says and never steps through.

signatures.code: groundUnder(shapes: Shape[], x: number, z: number, top: number, bottom: number): number

entries.name: Falling
entries.doc: The kinds of thing that fall and land.

entries.name: fallAt
entries.doc:
Where a falling thing is in its life (0 to 1, starting again each time it falls): `drop`, the share of its fall
done (0 at the top, 1 landed); `lying`, whether it has landed; `size`, from nothing as it appears to nothing as it
goes (snow melts, a leaf fades, rain splashes away quickly). Size is 0 at both ends, so a loop joins up.

signatures.code: fallAt(kind: Falling, life: number): { drop: number; lying: boolean; size: number }

entries.name: fallShare
entries.doc: The share of a life spent falling: what a speck's sway is frozen at once it lands.

entries.name: DriftSpec
entries.doc: A field of drifted snow, for `drift` and `driftField`.

props.name: at
props.doc: The middle of the snow field, at about ground height.

props.name: half
props.doc: Half its size along x and z.

props.name: depth
props.doc: How deep snow lies on open, level ground.

props.name: wind
props.doc: Which way the wind blows, [x, z]; the drift piles downwind of what stands in its way.

props.name: pile
props.doc: The most it piles up against something (3 × depth).

props.name: reach
props.doc: How far downwind a wall still shelters, in multiples of its height (4).

props.name: path
props.doc: A path trodden through it, where it lies thin.

props.name: pathWidth
props.doc: How wide the trodden path is (0.2 when left out).

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: Drift
entries.doc: Drifted snow as a grid, from `driftField`.

props.name: nx
props.doc: Grid points along x.

props.name: nz
props.doc: Grid points along z.

props.name: cell
props.doc: The distance between grid points.

props.name: x0
props.doc: The grid's first x.

props.name: z0
props.doc: The grid's first z.

props.name: ground
props.doc: The ground under the snow.

props.name: depth
props.doc: How deep the snow is on it.

entries.name: DRIFT_GRID
entries.doc: The most cells along a side of a drift's grid.

entries.name: driftField
entries.doc:
How deep snow lies over the ground `under` gives, in a grid: deep where something upwind shelters it (a wall, a
rock, a bank), thin where the wind scours (anything higher than the ground upwind, and steep slopes), thinner on a
path, then smoothed so it lies in soft drifts.

signatures.code: driftField(s: DriftSpec, under: (x: number, z: number) => number): Drift

entries.name: FrostSpec
entries.doc: A frost fern for `frost`.

props.name: at
props.doc: Where it starts, on the surface.

props.name: facing
props.doc: The way the surface faces.

props.name: r
props.doc: How far it spreads.

props.name: arms
props.doc: Main branches out from the start (5).

props.name: stage
props.doc: Which share of its growth to show, [from, to] in 0..1 (all of it): split one fern over parts that sprout in turn and it grows a branch at a time.

props.name: seed
props.doc: The same seed gives the same result.

entries.name: FrostBranch
entries.doc:
One stroke of a frost fern: its ends, its radius, which generation of branch it is, and `t`, when it grows (0 at
the start to 1 at the last tip).

props.name: from
props.doc: Where the stroke starts.

props.name: to
props.doc: Where it ends.

props.name: r
props.doc: Its radius.

props.name: gen
props.doc: Which generation of branch it is: 0 for a main branch.

props.name: t
props.doc: When it grows: 0 at the start to 1 at the last tip.

entries.name: frostPlan
entries.doc:
A frost fern as straight strokes in the surface's plane: main branches curve out from the start, each throwing
side branches at about 60 degrees, every other step on alternate sides, which do the same, smaller, up to three
generations. `t` is when a stroke grows, 0 at the start to 1 at the last tip, by how far along it is.

signatures.code: frostPlan(s: FrostSpec): FrostBranch[]

entries.name: frost
entries.doc: A frost fern lying on a surface (see frostPlan), each stroke standing a little proud of it; pieces are the generations, 0 the main branches.

signatures.code: frost(s: FrostSpec, thin?: number): Shape

entries.name: drift
entries.doc:
Drifted snow as a shape: deep behind whatever stands in the wind, gone from steep faces, thin on a trodden path.
`under` gives the height of the ground at a place.
entries.type: (s: DriftSpec, under: (x: number, z: number) => number, thin?: number) => Shape

modules.title: The sky through a day
modules.doc:
The sky over a scene through a day: where the sun and the moon stand for a time, a latitude and a day of the year,
and the light that follows from it, ready for `setLights`. The sun's path is the real one (declination by the day,
hour angle by the clock); its color comes from how much air its light crosses (red and dim at the horizon, white
overhead); the sky's own light, the sky's colors and the stars follow the sun's height. The moon is kept simple: it
trails the sun by its age, a full one rides high in winter and low in summer, and it gives light by how much of it
is lit. Pure numbers, so a page, a test and a recording get the same sky.

Directions are in the scene's frame: +x east, +y up, +z south. Strengths are set for a picture, not for a light
meter: real moonlight is a millionth of sunlight, and an eye (or a camera) opens up at night, so here the night is
dim, not black.

entries.name: SkyPlace
entries.doc: Where and when the sky is: what `daylight` needs besides the hour.

props.name: latitude
props.doc: Degrees north of the equator (south is negative).

props.name: day
props.doc: The day of the year, 1 to 365: 80 is the March equinox, 172 the June solstice.

props.name: moon
props.doc: The moon's age: 0 new, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 last quarter.

entries.name: DEFAULT_PLACE
entries.doc: A temperate place at midsummer under a full moon: what `daylight` uses where none is given.

entries.name: Daylight
entries.doc: The sky at one moment, from `daylight`. Colors are linear RGB; a light's color already holds its strength.

props.name: sun
props.doc: The way toward the sun (a unit vector), below the horizon too.

props.name: sunHeight
props.doc: The sun's height over the horizon, in degrees (negative when it is down).

props.name: sunColor
props.doc: The sun's light: white overhead, redder and weaker toward the horizon, nothing once it is down.

props.name: moon
props.doc: The way toward the moon (a unit vector).

props.name: moonHeight
props.doc: The moon's height over the horizon, in degrees.

props.name: moonColor
props.doc: The moon's light, by how much of it is lit and how dark the sky is: nothing by day.

props.name: moonLit
props.doc: How much of the moon's face is lit, 0 (new) to 1 (full).

props.name: ambient
props.doc: Light from the whole sky, which reaches into shade: blue by day, warm at dusk, dim and blue at night.

props.name: zenith
props.doc: The sky's color straight up.

props.name: horizon
props.doc: The sky's color at the horizon, away from the sun.

props.name: sunGlow
props.doc: The warm glow low in the sky round the sun as it rises and sets: nothing while it is high or well down.

props.name: stars
props.doc: How clearly the stars show, 0 by day to 1 in full night (less under a bright moon).

props.name: dark
props.doc: How dark it has grown, 0 in daylight to 1 once the sun is well down: when lamps come on.

entries.name: skyWay
entries.doc:
The way toward a point of the sky (a unit vector: +x east, +y up, +z south) from its hour angle (degrees west of
due south, 15 an hour), its declination (degrees north of the sky's equator) and the latitude it is seen from.

signatures.code: skyWay(hourAngle: number, declination: number, latitude: number): Vec3

entries.name: sunDeclination
entries.doc: How far north of the sky's equator the sun is on a day of the year, in degrees: 23.44 at the June solstice.

signatures.code: sunDeclination(day: number): number

entries.name: sunWay
entries.doc: The way toward the sun at an hour of the day (0 to 24 by the sun: 12 is when it is highest).

signatures.code: sunWay(hour: number, place?: SkyPlace): Vec3

entries.name: moonWay
entries.doc:
The way toward the moon at an hour of the day. It trails the sun across the sky by its age (a full moon is opposite
the sun, so it rises as the sun sets), and its declination is the sun's turned by its age, so a full moon is high in
winter and low in summer.

signatures.code: moonWay(hour: number, place?: SkyPlace): Vec3

entries.name: moonLit
entries.doc: How much of the moon's face is lit at an age: 0 new, 1 full.

signatures.code: moonLit(age: number): number

entries.name: sunTimes
entries.doc:
When the sun rises and sets, in hours by the sun, from where its center crosses the horizon. Where it never sets
(a polar summer) `rise` is 0 and `set` 24; where it never rises, both are 12.

signatures.code: sunTimes(place?: SkyPlace): { rise: number; set: number }

entries.name: airMass
entries.doc:
How much air light crosses on its way down from a height over the horizon (degrees), as a multiple of the air
straight overhead: 1 at the zenith, about 38 at the horizon (Kasten and Young's fit).

signatures.code: airMass(height: number): number

entries.name: daylight
entries.doc:
The sky and its light at an hour of the day (0 to 24 by the sun; any number wraps) at a place: where the sun and
moon stand, their light, the sky's own light and colors, how clearly stars show and how dark it has grown. Every
value changes smoothly through the day, so an hour hand dragged across it never jumps.

signatures.code: daylight(hour: number, place?: SkyPlace): Daylight

entries.name: skyLights
entries.doc:
The lights a sky gives a scene, for `setLights`: the sun and the moon as lights from a direction (each only while
it gives light, so a march for shadows is never spent on a light that is down), casting shadows if asked, and the
sky's own light as the ambient color.

signatures.code: skyLights(sky: Daylight, shadows?: boolean): { lights: { direction: Vec3; color: Vec3; shadow: boolean }[]; ambient: Vec3 }

entries.name: PixelPass
entries.doc:
Pixel mode: the scene is drawn small into a target, and one full-screen pass
turns it into pixel art and scales it up in whole pixels, with no smoothing.

The pass is the GPU twin of `pixelArt` in splat-core/pixel.ts (change one,
change both): alpha cut, glow from bright pixels, nearest palette color in
OKLab with a Bayer dither, edge lines inside the scene, an outline on the
empty pixels that touch it, and a sky behind. It runs once per art pixel,
into `art`, which keeps display (sRGB) color so a palette color is stored
exactly; the screen then gets a plain copy, scaled up. The art of the frame
before is kept too: a look with `steady` reads it so a pixel between two
palette colors does not flip from frame to frame.

A look with `fine` draws the scene and its map of parts at twice the art's
size first, and a step before the pass settles each art pixel from its four
samples into `small` and `ids` (`resolveFine` in pixel.ts is its twin), so
everything after it is the same either way.

props.name: small
props.doc: The scene, drawn small. Linear and premultiplied, as any render target.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The scene's parts, drawn small (`SplatWorld.parts`): where the color changes, one part ends and another begins. Only drawn for a look with `parts`.

props.name: ranks
props.doc: Each art pixel's step of the dither pattern, from the blob there (red, a byte), for a look with `surface`.

props.name: fineSmall
props.doc: The scene and its map of parts at twice the art's size, for a look with `fine`: what `small` and `ids` are settled from.

props.name: fineIds
props.doc:
The map of parts at twice the art's size, which four samples a pixel settles from (its first texture), and in the
same draw the picture with every blob a hard disc in its own color, as the map cuts it (its second, read with
`PixelLook.solid`): one draw of every blob for both, which on a phone is most of what either costs.

props.name: art
props.doc: The finished art at its own size, in display color, for reading back (tests, saving) and for the screen.

props.name: before
props.doc: The art of the frame before, when this frame was drawn against it (a look with `steady`): what `pixelArt` needs to give the same answer.

props.name: look
props.doc: The look in use.

props.name: drawnAt
props.doc: The time the last frame was drawn for (`setTime`): what `pixelArt` needs as its `time`.

props.name: width
props.doc: The art's width, in art pixels.

props.name: height
props.doc: The art's height, in art pixels.

props.name: anchor
props.doc:
The world point `snap` lands on the art's grid: the point the view turns about (the stage sets its orbit's target).
It must stay put on the screen as the view turns, or its place crosses half an art pixel now and then and the
whole picture jumps a pixel at once (Matt saw it as a Diorama scene rocked, 2026-11-23, snapped at the world's origin).

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Forgets the frame before: for when what is being drawn is swapped for something else.

signatures.code: reset(): void

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: Changes the look: palette, dither, glow, lines.

signatures.code: setLook(look: PixelLook): void

methods.name: setTime
methods.doc: The scene's time for this frame: what heat haze's waves and color cycling step by (`pixelArt`'s `time`).

signatures.code: setTime(t: number): void

methods.name: setGlitch
methods.doc:
This frame's glitch, laid on as the art goes to the screen (the art itself, `art`, stays clean: `glitchArt` lays
the same on a frame read back). Left out, none.

signatures.code: setGlitch(g?: GlitchState): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: The art's size in pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
Draws `scene` as pixel art. With `screen` (the output's size in device
pixels and how many of them make one art pixel) it goes to the renderer's
current output; without, into `art` at one to one.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, screen?: { width: number; height: number; scale: number }): void

methods.name: dispose
