methods.doc: Frees its render targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Pixel art
modules.doc:
The 2D half of Splat to Sprite: everything that happens after the splat has
been rendered. Pure functions on RGBA byte arrays so they can be unit tested
without a GPU.

Pipeline per frame:
  supersampled render → box downsample → alpha cut → palette (+dither) →
  stray-pixel cleanup → outline

entries.name: Rgb
entries.doc: A color as three numbers: red, green and blue, 0 to 255 in a palette.

entries.name: Frame
entries.doc: A picture as RGBA bytes.

props.name: width
props.doc: Pixels across.

props.name: height
props.doc: Pixels down.

props.name: data
props.doc: RGBA, row 0 at the top, straight (not premultiplied) alpha.

entries.name: PixelLook
entries.doc: How a scene is turned into pixel art, live (splat-engine/pixelPass.ts) or here on the CPU.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The colors every pixel snaps to; empty keeps the scene's own colors.

props.name: base
props.doc:
How many of `palette`'s colors are the palette's own, the rest being its ramp (`rampPalette`): the sky snaps to
these only, so its gradient dithers between the colors it was painted with. All of them when left out.

props.name: dither
props.doc: 0..1, as for `quantize`.

props.name: outline
props.doc: A 1-pixel line round the scene's silhouette, or none.

props.name: own
props.doc:
The outline in a darker tone of whatever it goes round, not one color for the whole scene: each outline pixel takes
the palette color nearest a darker step of the scene pixel beside it (`outline`'s own color where the palette has
nothing darker). Needs `outline`.

props.name: fine
props.doc:
Four samples a pixel: the scene is drawn at twice the art's size and each art pixel is settled from its 2×2 samples
(`resolveFine`) before anything else happens, so a pixel on the edge of a thing shows one thing or the other, never
a mix. The live pass does it itself; `pixelArt` is given the settled frame.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How far bright pixels spill light onto their neighbors: 0 is none.

props.name: edges
props.doc: Lines inside the scene, where one color meets a much lighter one: 0 (or left out) is none, 1 the darkest line.

props.name: parts
props.doc:
A line where one part of the scene meets another whose color is too close for `edges` to draw one (two things of one color, one in front of the other), at `edges`' strength or full strength without it.
Needs a map of the parts drawn beside the scene (`pixelArt`'s `parts`; the live pass draws its own).

props.name: across
props.doc:
Lines inside the scene only where one thing meets another: with a map of parts (`parts`, or `fine`, which draws one),
a jump in color within one part is its paint (grass, stonework) and takes no line, as a pixel artist outlines things
and not their texture. Without a map it does nothing.

props.name: solid
props.doc:
The scene's picture drawn with every blob a hard disc in its own color, cut where the map of parts cuts it, so a
thing's edge never shows a little of what is behind it (the stage draws it; the picture handed in is already so).

props.name: sky
props.doc:
A backdrop behind the scene: its color at the top and at the bottom of the picture, blended between and dithered into the palette.
`reach` is how far down the picture the blend runs before it is all the bottom color (above 0, up to 1; the whole way when left out or not a sound number: `skyReach`).
Left out, empty pixels stay clear.

props.name: steady
props.doc:
Steady pixels: a pixel keeps the palette color it had in the frame before unless another is closer by more than this (an OKLab distance; 0 or left out is off).
Without it, a pixel that sits between two colors flips back and forth as lights flicker and the view turns.

props.name: tidy
props.doc:
Lone-pixel cleanup, as a pixel artist does it: a scene pixel whose color none of its eight neighbors shares, while
six or more of them share one other color, takes that color. With a map of parts, only a pixel inside its own
part (four or more neighbors of its part) is touched, so a speck, an eye or a firefly in front of something stays.
A checkerboard dither keeps its pixels: each has its own color on the diagonals.

props.name: calm
props.doc:
Calmer pixels, in place of `tidy` (an idea from Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio, whose cleanup pass this follows in
part): a pixel art piece is flat patches of color with dither only where one gives way to the next, while a scene
of small blobs comes out speckled. So, reading only the art as drawn: a scene pixel takes the color `CALM_MOST` or
more of its eight neighbors share when fewer share its own (with a map of parts, only neighbors of its own part
count, so one thing never bleeds into another); a scene pixel with the empty backdrop on three or four sides (a
one-pixel bump on a silhouette) takes the backdrop's color beside it, and an empty pixel with the scene on three or
four sides (a notch) takes the scene's, so an outline runs clean; and lines are cleaned (`lineFix`: one-pixel kinks off
straight edges, doubled pixels off the corners of dark lines); and a patch of one or two pixels joins its
neighbors' color unless it is a highlight or a detail (`SPECK_MOST`, `SPECK_KEEP`). `calmArt` is the CPU twin of the pass.

props.name: flat
props.doc:
Dither only where a pixel artist puts it: the sky's blend and the light a glow spills onto the scene keep `dither`,
while the scene's own surfaces are drawn flat, each pixel its nearest palette color, so shade falls in bands. A
pixel a glow lights snaps only to a color of its own hue, the light's, or a gray (`keptNearest`).

props.name: rim
shine
props.doc: A highlight on the peak of each smooth lit form (`peakAt`): that pixel one step lighter in its own hue.

props.name: surface
props.doc:
Dither that stays on the things it falls on: each blob takes one step of the Bayer pattern from where it sits in
its own rest pose (`ditherRank`), not from the pixel it lands on, so the pattern rides with a turning view or a
moving creature instead of standing still on the screen while they slide under it. Needs a map of each pixel's
step drawn beside the scene (`pixelArt`'s `ranks`; the live pass draws its own). The sky keeps the screen's pattern.
Left out with `flat`: there only a glow's spill is dithered, and the map cost a whole extra draw of every blob.
After Silicon Jungle's Ink Studio (object-space dither, MIT), with their agreement.

props.name: snap
props.doc:
Holds the picture on the art's grid: one world point (`PixelPass.anchor`, where `snapAnchor` in orbit.ts puts it)
always lands on a whole art pixel, so when the view slides (a pan, a camera that follows) the scene moves by whole
pixels instead of smearing across them, and while it turns about its target nothing jumps. The live pass only
(`snapShift`). After Ink Studio's camera snap, which does it for a flat view; here it holds for a perspective view
at the anchor's depth.

props.name: bands
props.doc:
Glow in bands (1 or 2): in place of the soft spill round bright pixels, each pixel within `HALO_R` art pixels of a
glowing one takes a flat share of its light by how far it is, in rings, as hand-drawn pixel art lights a lamp.
After Ink Studio's banded glow (MIT), with their agreement.

props.name: heat
props.doc:
Heat haze: pixels above anything glowing (within `HEAT_R` across and up to `HEAT_UP` more above) are drawn from a
pixel or so to one side, the shift running in waves that change `pace` times a second (a whole number a loop, so a
recording joins). `pixels` is the most a pixel moves, 1 to 3. After Ink Studio's heat effect (MIT).

props.name: cycle
props.doc:
Color cycling: scene pixels whose palette color is one of `colors` step along the list `pace` times a second, as
old games ran water and fire. Each color is taken to its nearest in the palette, so a visitor's own palette still
cycles. Steady pixels leave these colors alone. After Ink Studio's palette cycles (MIT).

props.name: selout
props.doc:
Lighter outlines on lit sides ("selout"): an outline beside a scene pixel lighter than `SELOUT_FROM` takes a shade
just under that pixel's own color instead of the outline, so the line shows only where the thing is in shade. Needs
`outline`. After Ink Studio's lit and shadow line colors (MIT).

entries.name: pixelArt
entries.doc:
One frame of a scene to pixel art, the CPU twin of the live pixel pass
(change one, change both). `f` is the scene drawn small: straight sRGB.

  alpha cut → glow (bright pixels light their neighbors, and empty pixels
  beside them) → edge lines (the darker side of a jump in color) →
  palette + dither → outline on the empty pixels that touch the scene →
  sky on the rest, if the look has one

`before` is the art of the frame before, for a look with `steady`: where it
holds a palette color that is nearly as close as the best one, that pixel
keeps it. `parts` is the scene's map of parts for a look with `parts`: the
same view with every part in its own flat color (alpha 0 where there is none).

signatures.code: pixelArt(f: Frame, look: PixelLook, before?: Frame, parts?: Frame, ranks?: Frame, time?: number): Frame

modules.title: Brush and ink marks
modules.doc:
Marks: every blob drawn as a brush mark or an ink stroke in place of a soft dot, so a scene reads as a painting or
a drawing from any side. A mark is a function of where a pixel is on its own blob (along the blob's long and short
axes on screen, in standard deviations) and of the blob's seed, and of nothing on the screen: marks belong to their
blobs, so they stay put as the view moves, where a filter laid over the finished picture slides across it.

This file is the CPU twin of the engine's draw (`markOf` in splat-engine/engine.ts): change one, change both.

entries.name: MarkKind
entries.doc:
The kinds of mark: flat opaque dabs with bristle streaks, thicker dabs with ridges that catch light, a wash with a
pen stroke along each blob, hatching that is denser where it is darker, or a whole disc of the blob's own color with
no brushwork at all (`flat`: the fill under cel shading, where the discs of one surface close up into one color),
or stippling: pen dots on bare paper, more of them and bigger where it is darker.

entries.name: MARK_KINDS
entries.doc: The kinds, in the order the GPU numbers them (from 1; 0 is no marks).

entries.name: MarkLook
entries.doc: How the blobs are drawn as marks.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which mark.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big a mark is beside its blob: 1 reaches 1.5 standard deviations along the blob (default 1).

props.name: ink
props.doc: Ink, hatch and stipple: the pen's color, sRGB 0–1 (default a blue-black).

props.name: paper
props.doc: Ink, hatch and stipple: the paper's color, sRGB 0–1 (default a warm white). Set the page behind the view to it too.

props.name: soft
props.doc:
Lay the marks one over another from far to near, with soft edges, as soft blobs are drawn. Without it (the
default) each pixel shows the mark nearest to it, so the marks on a thing keep their places as it turns: right
for anything cut as discs on a surface. A scan's blobs overlap far more and build a surface between them, and
look better laid softly.

entries.name: lineWeight
entries.doc:
How strong a drawn outline is, 0–1: heavier round dark things than light ones, swelling and thinning along its
length (`swell`, 0–1, smooth noise), and broken off here and there round the lightest. `dark` is 1 less the root of
the thing's luminance.

signatures.code: lineWeight(dark: number, swell: number): number

entries.name: OutlinePen
entries.doc: A pen for drawn outlines (`Stage.setOutline`).

props.name: width
props.doc: The line's width in CSS pixels (default 1.5).

props.name: ink
props.doc: Its color, sRGB 0–1 (default the same blue-black as `MarkLook.ink`).

entries.name: MarkSample
entries.doc: What a mark is at one pixel.

props.name: cover
props.doc: How much of the pixel the mark covers, 0–1. Marks are paint: its alpha is this times the blob's opacity times `MARK_SOLID`, at most 1.

props.name: color
props.doc: The mark's color there, linear RGB.

entries.name: markAt
entries.doc:
A mark at (u, v): u along the blob's long axis on screen and v across it, in standard deviations. `rgb` is the
blob's color (linear) and `seed` its own number, 0–1. `ink` and `paper` are linear too.

signatures.code: markAt(kind: MarkKind, u: number, v: number, seed: number, rgb: ArrayLike<number>, size?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>, paper?: ArrayLike<number>): MarkSample

entries.name: InkLines
entries.doc:
Drawn outlines, as a pen would put them down: round the subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and
between its parts. Marks (`setMarks`) lay each blob down as a stroke, which shades a picture but never draws its
edges; a pen and wash drawing is the other way round, contours first.

The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs: the picture, a map of depth (`SplatDepth`) and
a map of parts (`SplatWorld.parts`). One pass then inks a pixel when, a line's width away, the picture ends, or
something is clearly nearer, or another part begins. The line is not even: its weight swells and thins along its
length and is heavier against dark things than light ones, where it may break off (`lineWeight` in marks.ts, the
CPU twin of the weight); and it wobbles a little, as a hand does.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the stage draws it without lines.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lines between parts come from.

methods.name: setPen
methods.doc: The pen: its color (linear RGB) and how wide its line is, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setPen(ink: readonly number[], width: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene with its lines into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Characters
modules.doc:
Characters: the picture drawn as text, a grid of cells over the view with one character in each. A cell's character
is picked by how much of the cell there is to show (its tone: more ink for more of it), or, where an edge runs
through the cell, by which way the edge runs: `|`, `-`, `/` or `\`. The grid is fixed on the screen, so the
characters stand in rows and columns and never slide; and a cell keeps the character it had unless another has
become clearly closer, so a cell whose tone sits between two characters does not flip back and forth as lights
flicker and the view turns.

This file is the CPU twin of the engine's pass (`GlyphPass` in splat-engine/glyphPass.ts): change one, change both.

entries.name: RAMP
entries.doc: The characters that show tone, from none to the most ink.

entries.name: STROKES
entries.doc: The characters that show an edge: upright, level (drawn as a dash the width of the cell), rising and falling.

entries.name: GLYPHS
entries.doc: Every character, in the order the engine numbers them.

entries.name: glyphBit
entries.doc: Whether a character has ink at a pixel of its cell (`x` from the left, `y` from the top).

signatures.code: glyphBit(glyph: number, x: number, y: number): boolean

entries.name: RAMP_INK
entries.doc: How much ink each character of the ramp lays down, as a share of the heaviest one's: what its tone is.

entries.name: glyphAtlas
entries.doc: The font as one strip of bytes, a character after another from the left, 255 where there is ink: what the engine samples.

signatures.code: glyphAtlas(): { width: number; height: number; data: Uint8Array }

entries.name: GlyphLook
entries.doc: How the picture is drawn as characters (`Stage.setGlyphs`).

props.name: size
props.doc: How tall a cell is in CSS pixels (default 12; a cell is three quarters as wide). It is rounded so every pixel of the font is a whole number of device pixels.

props.name: ink
props.doc: The characters' color, sRGB 0–1. Left out, each takes the color of what it stands for.

props.name: light
props.doc: For a light ground: darker things get the heavier characters. Without it (a dark ground) lighter things do.

props.name: edges
props.doc: Draw a stroke where an edge runs through a cell: where the picture ends, one thing stands in front of another, two parts meet, or the tone changes sharply (default true).

props.name: strands
props.doc:
Draw a stroke along what is long and thin on the screen, such as strands of fur and blades of grass, where a cell
is mostly that (default true). The stroke is the one of `|`, `_`, `/` and `` nearest the way they run.

props.name: steady
props.doc: How much closer another character's tone has to be before a cell gives up the one it has, 0–0.5 of the whole range (default `STICK`; 0 never keeps one).

props.name: gain
props.doc: Tones are multiplied by this before a character is picked (default 1): over 1 for a dim scene.

props.name: set
props.doc:
Which characters (default 'ascii'): 'braille' draws each cell as the braille character whose eight dots are on
where that eighth of the cell is heavy enough, and 'blocks' as the quarter blocks (▘ ▚ ▙ and so on) or, where a
cell is even, one of the shades ░ ▒ ▓. Both show shapes within a cell, so `edges` and `strands` are not used.
'lines' draws only the edges, in box-drawing characters (─ │ ┌ ┼ and so on) that join from cell to cell, with a
dot for tone; 'words' writes `words` over and over through the picture, each letter as bright as its cell; and
'typed' is a typewriter's: keys struck once or twice over one another by tone, each strike a little out of line.

props.name: words
props.doc: The text 'words' writes, in capitals (letters, digits and `EXTRA`'s signs; anything else is a space).

entries.name: GlyphSet
entries.doc: The kinds of characters a picture can be drawn in (`GlyphLook.set`).

entries.name: toneOf
entries.doc:
A cell's tone, 0–1: how heavy a character it wants. `rgb` is the mean of the picture over the cell, linear and
premultiplied, `cover` its mean alpha: a cell the subject only half fills gets a lighter character, which softens
the outline.

signatures.code: toneOf(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, look?: GlyphLook): number

entries.name: rampFor
entries.doc:
The ramp character for a tone: the one whose ink is nearest, unless the cell had a ramp character the frame before
(`before`, its number) that is no more than `steady` further off.

signatures.code: rampFor(tone: number, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: Probe
entries.doc: What the picture is at one of a cell's probes.

props.name: shown
props.doc: Whether anything is drawn there.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Its tone there (`toneOf` of that one point).

props.name: depth
props.doc: How far in front of the camera it is.

props.name: part
props.doc: Which part it is, as any number that differs between parts.

entries.name: strokeFor
entries.doc:
The stroke for a cell, as a number in `GLYPHS`, or -1 for none. The probes are left, right, above, below, then
above left, above right, below left and below right of the cell's middle. An edge runs along the one way in which
both ends are on the same side while the way across it is not: upright and level are tried first.

signatures.code: strokeFor(p: readonly Probe[]): number

entries.name: GlyphCell
entries.doc: A cell as drawn: its character and that character's color.

props.name: glyph
props.doc: The character's number in `GLYPHS` (0 is a space).

props.name: color
props.doc: Its color, linear RGB.

entries.name: glyphCell
entries.doc:
One cell: its character and color from the picture's mean over the cell (`rgb` linear and premultiplied, `cover`
its alpha), the two rings of probes when edges are wanted (the inner eight, then the outer eight), and the character
it had the frame before (-1 for none). `ink` here is linear. `lie` is the cell's mean lie (`strandFor`) when strands
are wanted: a cell of strands takes their stroke, lit by its tone, before any edge is looked for.

signatures.code: glyphCell(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, probes: readonly Probe[] | undefined, look?: GlyphLook, before?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>, lie?: ArrayLike<number>): GlyphCell

entries.name: brailleFor
entries.doc:
A braille cell's dots from the tones of its eight parts (two across, four down, a row after another from the top):
as bits from U+2800. A dot is on where its part's tone reaches its `DOT_STEP`; one that was on the frame before
(`before`, the same bits, or -1) stays on down to `steady` under it, so a dot at its step does not blink.

signatures.code: brailleFor(tones: ArrayLike<number>, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: QUADS
entries.doc: The quarter blocks, by their bits: above left 1, above right 2, below left 4, below right 8.

entries.name: SHADES
entries.doc: The shades, light to dark, numbered after the quarter blocks.

entries.name: blockFor
entries.doc:
A blocks cell from the tones of its four quarters (above left, above right, below left, below right): an even cell
is the shade nearest its mean (kept, like a ramp character, unless another is `steady` closer), and an uneven one is
the quarter block with the quarters over the middle of its tones (kept while no quarter is clearly on the other side).

signatures.code: blockFor(q: ArrayLike<number>, before?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: shapeCell
entries.doc:
One cell drawn in braille or blocks (`GlyphLook.set`): `parts` are the tones of its eighths or quarters (`toneOf` of
each), the rest as for `glyphCell`. The color is the cell's own at the level its heaviest part asks for.

signatures.code: shapeCell(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, cover: number, parts: ArrayLike<number>, look?: GlyphLook, before?: number, ink?: ArrayLike<number>): GlyphCell

entries.name: setBit
entries.doc: Whether a character of a set has ink at a pixel of its 6 × 8 cell (`x` from the left, `y` from the top): what the engine draws. The typewriter's also needs the cell's column and row (`cx`, `cy`).

signatures.code: setBit(set: GlyphSet, glyph: number, x: number, y: number, cx?: number, cy?: number): boolean

entries.name: charOf
entries.doc: A character of a set as text.

signatures.code: charOf(set: GlyphSet, glyph: number): string

entries.name: glyphText
entries.doc: A grid of characters (their numbers in `GLYPHS`, or a set's own numbers, a row after another from the top) as lines of text, with spaces at line ends dropped.

signatures.code: glyphText(glyphs: ArrayLike<number>, columns: number, set?: GlyphSet): string

entries.name: glyphScale
entries.doc: How many device pixels one pixel of the font is, for a cell `size` CSS pixels tall: whole, and at least 1.

signatures.code: glyphScale(size: number, pixelRatio: number): number

entries.name: GlyphPass
entries.doc:
The picture as characters (splat-core/glyphs.ts is the CPU twin: change one, change both). The frame is drawn three
times with the same moved and sorted blobs, as for drawn outlines: the picture, a map of depth and a map of parts.
One small pass then decides every cell of the grid (its character and that character's color, kept in a target a
cell a pixel, beside the one from the frame before so a cell can keep its character), and a second draws the
characters from the font, each of the font's pixels a whole number of device pixels.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the stage draws it without characters.

props.name: grid
props.doc: The grid of the frame just drawn: a pixel a cell, the character's number in alpha.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look; `ink` is linear RGB here, or left out for each character to take its own color.

signatures.code: setLook(look: GlyphLook, ink?: readonly number[]): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass for a picture in device pixels, with `scale` of them to one pixel of the font.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number, scale: number): void

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Forgets the frame before: for when what is being drawn is swapped for something else.

signatures.code: forget(): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene as characters into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

entries.name: CelPass
entries.doc:
Cel shading (splat-core/cel.ts). The frame is drawn four times with the same moved and sorted blobs: the picture in
the blobs' own flat colors, a map of depth, a map of parts and a map of tones (how each blob faces the light). The
scene is also drawn once as the light sees it, as a map of depth (a shadow map), whenever the blobs or the light
have moved. One pass then finds, for each pixel, whether the light sees it; a second smooths that and the facing
over each surface, cuts them into light and shade, paints the picture with them and draws an even line round the
subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and between its parts.

The world must be drawing for it: flat marks, `cel` on, and its first light the one to shade by (`Stage.setCel` sets
all three). The frame's camera must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lines between parts come from.

props.name: tones
props.doc: The map of tones (`SplatWorld.tones`).

props.name: shadow
props.doc: The scene's depth as the light sees it, counted from the near side of the scene.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is.

signatures.code: setLook(look: CelLook, ratio: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene cel shaded into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Cel shading: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Cel shading: the light on a picture cut into a few flat tones with clean edges, as an animation cel is painted, in
place of light that fades smoothly round a form.

Nothing is faked on the finished picture. Each blob is drawn flat in its own color (the `flat` mark), and the engine
works out, for each blob, how it faces the light and how much of the light gets to it past what stands in the way
(`toneAt` in splat-engine/light.ts and its shader twin). Those two numbers are drawn as a picture of their own, and
smoothed a little over the surface they lie on before they are cut into tones: a blob is a disc some pixels across,
and cutting first would leave every shadow with an edge of discs.

This file is the arithmetic of the cut, the CPU twin of the engine's pass (`CelPass` in splat-engine/celPass.ts):
change one, change both.

entries.name: CelLook
entries.doc: How a picture is cel shaded (`Stage.setCel`).

props.name: from
props.doc: The way to the light, in the world (it needs no length). Default up, to the right and toward the front.

props.name: tones
props.doc: How many tones the light is cut into: 2 is light and shade, 3 adds a brighter tone where a surface faces the light squarely (default 2).

props.name: shade
props.doc: What shade multiplies a color by, sRGB 0–1: a cool violet gray by default, as shadows are painted on a cel.

props.name: bright
props.doc: How far the brightest of three tones goes toward white, 0–1 (default 0.2).

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether things cast shadows on one another (default true). Without them a surface is only lit by how it faces the light.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: How far the light is smoothed over a surface before it is cut into tones, in CSS pixels (default 8): more gives rounder, simpler shadow shapes.

props.name: soft
props.doc: How soft the edge between two tones is, 0–1 (default 0: as crisp as the screen's pixels allow).

props.name: line
props.doc: The outline's width in CSS pixels (default 1.5); 0 draws none.

props.name: ink
props.doc: The outline's color, sRGB 0–1 (default near black).

props.name: shadowSize
props.doc: How many pixels a side the light's view of the scene is, which cast shadows are read from (default and most 2048): fewer is cheaper to draw and gives softer shadow edges.

props.name: shadowEvery
props.doc: The light's view is drawn again at most every this many frames (default 1, every frame something moves): 2 halves its cost and leaves cast shadows a frame behind.

props.name: lamps
props.doc:
What the scene's own lights add to a color where they reach it (linear, added to what the tone multiplies it by).
Left out, a `Stage` works it out from the lights set on it (`lampTint`); black takes the lamps away.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: What both tones are multiplied by (linear), such as a night's dim blue. On a `Stage` its ambient light multiplies them too, so a scene that dims dims here.

entries.name: CEL_FROM
entries.doc: The default way to the light.

entries.name: CEL_SHADE
entries.doc: The default shade.

entries.name: CEL_INK
entries.doc: The default outline color.

entries.name: CEL_TURN
entries.doc:
A surface is in the light when it faces the light by more than this: its `facing` is half the cosine of the angle
between its normal and the way to the light, plus a half, so 0.5 is edge on. A little past edge on, as it is drawn by
hand: a surface the light only grazes reads as shade.

entries.name: CEL_BRIGHT
entries.doc: With three tones, a surface facing the light by this much or more takes the brightest.

entries.name: CEL_CAST
entries.doc: A blob is in a cast shadow when less than this share of the light gets to it.

entries.name: CEL_LAMP
entries.doc: A surface is in a lamp's light when the scene's lamps reach it by this much or more (`toneAt`'s `lamps` in splat-engine/light.ts).

entries.name: CEL_GLOWS
entries.doc: From this much, what reaches a surface is its own light (a flame, a lit pane): it is never darker than its own color.

entries.name: LAMP_ADD
entries.doc: How strong the color lamps add is, where the lights set no more: the brightest channel of `lampTint`.

entries.name: CEL_EDGE
entries.doc: The least width of a tone's edge, in the units of what is cut (facing and share of light, both 0–1), so the edge is not stepped.

entries.name: CEL_UNSURE
entries.doc: A blob with no flat side has no facing of its own; where nothing round a pixel has one, it is taken to face the light this much.

entries.name: celTones
entries.doc:
The tones at a point: `lit` is 0 in shade and 1 in the light, `bright` 1 where the third tone is. `facing` is how
the surface faces the light (0 away, 0.5 edge on, 1 toward) and `through` the share of the light that reaches it.

signatures.code: celTones(facing: number, through: number, look?: CelLook): { lit: number; bright: number }

entries.name: celColor
entries.doc:
A color (linear RGB) under the tones `celTones` gives: `shade` (linear) multiplies it in shade, and the brightest
tone goes toward white. `by` is the scene's own light: `ambient` multiplies both tones, `lamps` is added where the
scene's lamps reach (`reach`, from `toneAt`: one more tone, cut at `CEL_LAMP`), and from `CEL_GLOWS` the color is
never darker than itself.

signatures.code: celColor(rgb: ArrayLike<number>, tones: { lit: number; bright: number }, shade: ArrayLike<number>, bright?: number, by?: { reach: number; lamps?: ArrayLike<number>; ambient?: ArrayLike<number> }): [number, number, number]

entries.name: lampTint
entries.doc:
The color the scene's lamps add in cel shading (linear): the color of its point lights taken together, each by its
brightness, with its strongest channel at `LAMP_ADD`. Black where there are none.

signatures.code: lampTint(lights: readonly { color: ArrayLike<number>; position?: unknown }[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: SHADOW_FAR
entries.doc: How many times the scene's size away the light's view of it is taken from: far enough that its shadows fall nearly side by side.

entries.name: shadowView
entries.doc:
Where to stand to see the scene as the light does, for a map of what the light reaches: a narrow view from
`SHADOW_FAR` sizes away along the way to the light, round a ball that holds the scene. The ball's middle and size
are rounded onto steps of their own, so a scene whose bounds wander as it moves keeps one view, and its shadows
keep their pixels. `fov` is in degrees.

signatures.code: shadowView(center: ArrayLike<number>, radius: number, from: ArrayLike<number>): { eye: [number, number, number]; target: [number, number, number]; up: [number, number, number]; fov: number; near: number; far: number; radius: number }

entries.name: SAME_COLOR
entries.doc: Two colors of one part nearer than this in OKLab are gathered into one: the mottle of a painted surface, not a stripe.

entries.name: gatherColors
entries.doc:
Flat fills for a cel: each part's colors gathered into a few, so a mottled or textured surface becomes areas of one
color and a stripe, a spot or a white chest stays its own. `color` holds a color a blob (sRGB, 0–1, three numbers
each) and `partOf` each blob's part (left out, the blobs are one part); a part keeps at most `most` colors, and
fewer where they are within `SAME_COLOR` of one another. The same blobs always give the same colors: the first
color of a part is its commonest, and each next the one furthest from those chosen, before a few rounds settle them.

With `round` (where each blob is, three numbers each, and how far round it to look), a blob then takes the color most
of its part's blobs within that reach have, twice over: speckle finer than the reach goes, and anything wider (a
stripe, a patch, a checker) keeps its edge.

signatures.code: gatherColors(color: ArrayLike<number>, partOf?: ArrayLike<number>, most?: number, round?: { at: ArrayLike<number>; reach: number }): Float32Array

entries.name: NeonPass
entries.doc:
Neon (splat-core/neon.ts): tubes of light along the picture's outlines, over bodies kept dark that catch the
tubes' light. The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the picture in the blobs' own
flat colors, a map of depth and a map of parts), as outlines are (inkLines.ts), and the tubes run where those
lines would: round the subject, where one thing passes in front of another, and between its parts. A tube takes
the color of the thing it goes round at full strength (`neonColor`), or one of the look's colors by its part, and
shines by where it is in the world: pulses of light run through the scene two ways (`shineAt`), so the light
travels along the tubes. The tubes' light is then spread at three sizes, and the last pass paints each body in its
own color times the light that reaches it, with the glow and the tubes over it. Whatever gives its own light
(`Actor.glow`) is a lamp: filled with its color and spread onto the bodies round it as the tubes' light is.

The world should be drawing flat marks with no light of its own and a `glowGain` of `NEON_EMIT` (`Stage.setNeon` sets all three). The frame's camera
must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color, with what gives its own light drawn over white (`NEON_EMIT`), which is how the pass knows a lamp.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the tubes between parts come from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc:
The look, how many device pixels a CSS pixel is, the scene's size in the world (which the pulses are spaced by)
and the stage's time in seconds.

signatures.code: setLook(look: NeonLook, ratio: number, size: number, time: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene in neon into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Neon: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Neon (Matt's idea, 2026-11-19): a scene drawn as tubes of glowing light along its outlines, over bodies kept dark
that catch the light as it runs along the tubes. The arithmetic here is pure; `splat-engine/neonPass.ts` is its
shader twin (change both).

entries.name: NeonLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws neon (`Stage.setNeon`).

props.name: line
props.doc: How wide a tube is, in CSS pixels (2).

props.name: glow
props.doc: How strongly the tubes' light spills round them and onto the bodies: 0 none, 1 as designed, up to 2.

props.name: body
props.doc: How lit the bodies are with no tube near, as a share of their own color (`NEON_BODY`).

props.name: colors
props.doc: The tubes' colors (sRGB 0–1), dealt out part by part. Left out, each tube takes the color of the thing it goes round, at full strength.

props.name: period
props.doc: How many seconds a pulse of light takes to come round again; 0 holds the light still (4). A scene that loops wants a whole number of these in its loop.

props.name: apart
props.doc: How far apart two pulses run, as a share of the scene's size (0.45).

entries.name: NEON_BODY
entries.doc: Bodies with no tube near keep this share of their own color.

entries.name: NEON_REST
entries.doc: A tube between pulses shines this much of its full light.

entries.name: NEON_TAIL
entries.doc: How fast a pulse dies away behind its head: its light is (1 − how far behind, as a share of the way to the next) to this power.

entries.name: NEON_FLOOR
entries.doc: A tube's color keeps at least this much of each channel, so a pure red still has a hot core.

entries.name: NEON_BLACK
entries.doc: A thing darker than this in every channel (linear) has no hue to speak of, and its tube is white.

entries.name: NEON_VIVID
entries.doc: How much stronger than its own a tube's color is made, about its gray.

entries.name: NEON_EMIT
entries.doc:
How many times its own color a thing that gives its own light (`Actor.glow`: a lamp, a lit window, a flame) is
drawn into neon's picture, so the pass can tell it from a pale thing: its color goes over white (`lampShare`).

entries.name: NEON_LAMP
entries.doc: A pixel whose brightest channel is over the first of these is partly a lamp, and over the second wholly one.

entries.name: NEON_LAMP_SHINE
entries.doc: How brightly a lamp shines beside a tube at a pulse's head.

entries.name: NEON_COLORS
entries.doc: The most colors a look may deal out.

entries.name: NEON_WAYS
entries.doc: The two ways pulses run through a scene (not unit: the second set of pulses lies closer together).
entries.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]

entries.name: NEON_SECOND
entries.doc: The second set of pulses' share of the first's light.

entries.name: NEON_SHIFT
entries.doc: How far a part's own number shifts its pulses, in pulses.

entries.name: neonColor
entries.doc:
The color of the tube round a thing of color `rgb` (linear, 0–1): the same hue at full strength, however dark the
thing is. A gray thing gets a white tube.

signatures.code: neonColor(rgb: readonly number[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: pulse
entries.doc: One set of pulses: 1 at a pulse's head, dying away behind it to nothing just before the next. `phase` counts pulses.

signatures.code: pulse(phase: number): number

entries.name: shineAt
entries.doc:
How brightly a tube shines at a place: `along` is the place measured along each of the two ways, in pulses (its
part's shift included), `turn` how many pulses have gone by. Never under `NEON_REST`, 1 at a head.

signatures.code: shineAt(along: readonly [number, number], turn: number): number

entries.name: lampShare
entries.doc:
How much of a pixel of neon's picture is a lamp, from its brightest channel (`top`): nothing up to white, all of
it well over. A lamp is filled with its own light, steady, and that light is spread onto the bodies round it as
the tubes' is.

signatures.code: lampShare(top: number): number

entries.name: colorOf
entries.doc: Which of `count` colors a part takes, from the part's shift (0–1).

entries.name: bodyColor
entries.doc:
A body's color (linear) under the tubes' light: its own color times what it keeps unlit plus the light that
reaches it (`light`, the tubes' light spread out, linear).

signatures.code: bodyColor(own: readonly number[], light: readonly number[], body?: number, glow?: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: GlassPass
entries.doc:
Stained glass (splat-core/glass.ts). The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the
picture in the blobs' own flat colors, a map of depth and a map of parts), as outlines are (inkLines.ts). One pass
then puts each pixel back in the world from its depth and asks which pane it is in: panes are the cells nearest a
scatter of points fixed in the world, so they stay on their surfaces as the view turns. A pane's glass is the
picture's own color there, made richer and lighter and a little different from the next pane's, with the light
behind it. Lead runs between panes, round every part, where one thing passes in front of another, round the
subject, and wherever the picture's color changes, so each piece between leads is one color: it wants blobs in
flat colors with no light baked in. Pixels the subject leaves empty are panes too, fixed on the screen and colored as the look's sky, so the
whole picture is a window.

The world should be drawing flat marks with no light of its own (`Stage.setGlass` sets both). The frame's camera must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the lead between parts comes from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, how many device pixels a CSS pixel is, and the scene's size in the world (which panes are sized by).

signatures.code: setLook(look: GlassLook, ratio: number, size: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene as stained glass into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Stained glass: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Stained glass (Matt picked it, 2026-11-19): a scene drawn as a leaded window. Every surface is cut into panes of
flat colored glass that stay on it as the view turns, with lead between the panes, round every part, wherever
the color changes and round the subject, and the light comes from behind. The arithmetic here is pure; `splat-engine/glassPass.ts` is its
shader twin (change both).

entries.name: GlassLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws stained glass (`Stage.setGlass`).

props.name: pane
props.doc: How big a pane is, as a share of the scene's size (0.06).

props.name: lead
props.doc: How wide the lead is, in CSS pixels (3).

props.name: ink
props.doc: The lead's color (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: sky
props.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]
props.doc: The window round the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1): empty pixels are panes of these. Left out, pale blue over warm white.

props.name: light
props.doc: Where the light behind the window is brightest, across and down the picture (0–1; [0.5, 0.3]).

props.name: shine
props.doc: How much brighter the glass is at the light than far from it: 0 lights the window evenly (0.5).

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much one pane's glass differs from the next's, 0 to 1 (0.5).

entries.name: GLASS_RICH
entries.doc: Glass is richer than paint: its color is made this much stronger about its gray.

entries.name: GLASS_LIFT
entries.doc: And lighter, since the light comes through it: its color is raised to this power (under 1 lightens).

entries.name: GLASS_VARY
entries.doc: One pane's glass is lighter or darker than the next's by up to this share, at full `vary`.

entries.name: GLASS_SKY_PANE
entries.doc: The window round the subject is cut into panes this many times a scene pane's size on screen, as a share of the picture's height.

entries.name: GLASS_JUMP
entries.doc: Lead also runs where the picture's own color (linear) changes by more than this from one pixel to one a lead's width away.

entries.name: GLASS_LEAD
entries.doc: The lead (sRGB 0–1): near black, a little warm.

entries.name: GLASS_SKY
entries.doc: The window with no sky of the subject's own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).
entries.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]

entries.name: cellHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a grid cell, different for each `salt`.

signatures.code: cellHash(x: number, y: number, z: number, salt: number): number

entries.name: seedOf
entries.doc: Where a grid cell's pane has its middle: somewhere in the cell.

signatures.code: seedOf(x: number, y: number, z: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: paneOf
entries.doc:
The pane a point is in, with panes one unit across: the grid cell whose seed is nearest (`cell`, `seed`) and how
far the point is from the nearest other pane (`edge`: its distance to the plane halfway between the two seeds).
Lead is drawn where `edge` is under half the lead's width.

signatures.code: paneOf(p: readonly number[]): { cell: [number, number, number]; seed: [number, number, number]; edge: number }

entries.name: glassColor
entries.doc: A color (linear, 0–1) as glass with the light behind it: richer and lighter.

signatures.code: glassColor(rgb: readonly number[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: paneTint
entries.doc: What a pane's glass is multiplied by: each pane a little lighter or darker than the next, by its cell.

signatures.code: paneTint(cell: readonly number[], vary?: number): number

entries.name: backLight
entries.doc: How bright the light behind the window is at a place in the picture (`at` and `light` across and down, 0–1; `aspect` is width over height): 1 at the light, falling to 1 − `shine` far from it.

signatures.code: backLight(at: readonly number[], light: readonly number[], shine?: number, aspect?: number): number

entries.name: BLOCK_LIGHTS
entries.doc: How many of the stage's lights reach the blocks; the rest are dropped.

entries.name: EDGE_WIDTH
entries.doc: How far in from a face's edge its line reaches, as a share of the face.

entries.name: LAMP_WRAP
entries.doc: How much of a lamp's light a face turned away from it still takes: lamps cast no shadows here, so a little wraps round.

entries.name: BlockActor
entries.doc: What a view needs of an actor: what blocks are made from, and the posed bones that carry them.
entries.type: BlockSource & { skeleton: { matrix: Float32Array; scale: Float32Array; bones: readonly { name: string }[] } }

entries.name: BlockView
entries.doc:
A scene drawn as blocks (blocks.ts): one mesh for each bone that carries cubes, moved by that bone whole, so cubes
never bend. The look's own light is in the corners already; this adds the stage's lamps to each face by where it
is and which way it faces now, keeps a block that gives its own light at its own color, and draws a thin line
round each face. A surface that moves by itself (an actor with `flows`: a pond) is columns whose tops follow its
blobs (`reshape` after they change), drawn after the cubes and as see-through as its blobs are. It draws into a target with four samples a pixel and copies that out, since a cube's edges want
smoothing that soft blobs never did. An actor as big as a world (`far`) is cut into squares at each of its levels,
and each frame every square is drawn at the level its distance asks for (`farLevel`).

ctor.code: new BlockView(actors: readonly BlockActor[], look: BlockLook)

props.name: blocks
props.doc: How many cubes it holds.

props.name: faces
props.doc: How many faces of them it draws: those with no cube of the same bone beside them.

methods.name: reshape
methods.doc: After an actor's blobs were changed in place: a surface that moves (`flows`) lays its columns to them again. Any other actor's cubes stay as built.

signatures.code: reshape(actor: BlockSource): void

methods.name: setFog
methods.doc: Distance fog toward `color` (linear) from `near` to `far` in front of the camera, as `SplatWorld.setFog` (`far` 0 is none).

signatures.code: setFog(color: readonly [number, number, number], near: number, far: number): void

methods.name: setLights
methods.doc: The stage's lights and ambient light, as `SplatWorld.setLights` takes them; `tint` multiplies the ambient (a night's light).

signatures.code: setLights(lights: readonly Light[], ambient?: number | readonly [number, number, number], tint?: readonly [number, number, number]): void

methods.name: pose
methods.doc: Puts every piece where its bone is now.

signatures.code: pose(): void

methods.name: levels
methods.doc: How many of a far actor's squares are drawn at each level now: its own cubes first.

signatures.code: levels(): number[]

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene (this view in it) into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none, with its edges smoothed.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees the meshes and the target.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

entries.name: BlockLook
entries.doc:
Blocks: a scene's blobs snapped onto a grid and drawn as cubes (`Stage.setBlocks`). Every grid cell that holds a
blob becomes one cube in the commonest color among its blobs, on the bone most of them ride, so a scene still
moves: its still parts stay on the grid and a moving part carries its cubes with it. The light is worked out here,
once, for the rest pose: each face is flat in one tone by which way it faces the light, a face something stands
in front of is in shade as a whole, and corners where blocks meet are a little darker. That wants blobs with no
light baked into them. This file is the arithmetic (pure, tested); blockView.ts draws it.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A block's side, in the blobs' units: the grid a scene was cut on, or a whole number of it for bigger blocks.

props.name: from
props.doc: The way to the light (any length; default up, right and toward the front).

props.name: shade
props.doc: How much light a face in shade keeps, 0 to 1 (default 0.45).

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether blocks cast shadows on the faces behind them (default true).

props.name: corners
props.doc: How much darker a face gets in a corner where blocks meet, 0 to 1 (default 0.5).

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much one block's color differs from the next's, 0 to 1 (default 0.35).

props.name: edge
props.doc: How dark the line round each face is, 0 to 1 (default 0.3); 0 for none.

props.name: ambient
props.doc: What the stage's ambient light is multiplied by, linear (a night's dim blue; default none).

props.name: least
props.doc: Blobs fainter than this are left out (mist, haze; default 0.3).

props.name: flow
props.doc:
How a surface that moves by itself is drawn (a source with `flows`: a pond): 'blocks', as columns of cubes whose
tops rise and fall with it in steps, or 'blobs', left as the blobs it is among the cubes (default 'blobs': Matt found
they have more definition, 2026-11-21).

props.name: weather
props.doc: How weather laid over a scene (an actor with `weather`: clouds, rain, snow) is drawn: as cubes too, or left the blobs it is among the cubes (default 'blobs').

props.name: swell
props.doc: How many times higher than it stands a ripple is drawn as blocks (default `FLOW_SWELL`); 0 keeps the tops level, so only their color moves.

props.name: palette
props.doc: Paints every block takes its color from (sRGB 0–255): a cell's commonest color is snapped to the nearest in OKLab before light falls on it (`paletteSnap`). Left out, blocks keep their own colors. Water columns and soft actors keep theirs.

entries.name: BLOCK_FROM
entries.doc: The default way to the light.

entries.name: BLOCK_SHADE
entries.doc: The default light a face in shade keeps.

entries.name: CORNER_MOST
entries.doc: How much of its light a face loses with all of a corner shut in, at `corners` 1.

entries.name: VARY_MOST
entries.doc: How far a block's lightness is from its color's own at most, at `vary` 1.

entries.name: SKY_SHARE
entries.doc: A face in shade is this much darker again when it faces straight down, and as much lighter facing up.

entries.name: SPECK_SIZE
entries.doc:
Loose things in the air (rain, sparks, fireflies: bones whose names start with `~`) are cubes this share of a block
across, on a grid of their own, and take no part in shadows or corners.

entries.name: FACE_VOTE
entries.doc:
How many blobs one blob that glows or is laid over another (`laid`) counts for when a cell's color is picked: a
window is a small pane in a bigger dark frame, and by count the frame took every cell (Matt saw windows as solid
black blocks, 2026-11-21).

entries.name: GLOW_CLEAR
entries.doc: A block that gives this much of its own light or more (the mean of its blobs' `glow`) casts no shadow.

entries.name: BlockSource
entries.doc: What blocks are made from: an actor's blobs, its skin, the names of its bones and the light its blobs give.

props.name: blobs
props.doc: The blobs in the rest pose.

props.name: skin
props.doc: Which bones move each blob: a block rides the bone most of its blobs do.

props.name: skeleton
props.doc: The bones, for their names: one whose name starts with `~` carries loose specks.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How much of its own light each blob gives, a byte a blob (`Actor.glow`).

props.name: laid
props.doc: Blobs of a face laid over another part (voxel.ts `laid`: a pane on its frame), a byte a blob: drawn as blocks, a cell takes their color before the color of what they lie on.

props.name: seen
props.doc: How much of each of the first four lights each blob sees, four bytes a blob (`Actor.seen`): a light some blob sees less than all of is a lamp that stays put, and casts block shadows (`lampSight`).

props.name: flows
props.doc: A surface that moves by itself (a pond): its blobs are sent up again as they change, and its cubes are columns that follow them (`planFlow`).

props.name: blockCell
props.doc: The side of this source's blocks, where it was cut on a grid of its own (a finer cut of the place underfoot); left out, the look's `cell`.

props.name: hole
props.doc:
Cubes whose middles stand in this square (x and z, in the source's rest units) are not drawn: where a finer cut of
the same ground is laid in their place (a patch round the place looked at). The cubes are still made, and nothing
else changes, so moving the square only picks other faces to draw (`holed`).

props.name: keepCubes
props.doc:
Its blobs never change in place, so its cubes are kept with them and made once (`keptBlocks`): a stage that makes
its cubes again for a new actor beside it (a patch moved underfoot) takes these as they were, not over a second's
work again. A source whose colors are changed in place (weather shaded under the sky) must leave it out.

props.name: far
props.doc:
A source as big as a world (an island a hundred and fifty meters across): its cubes are also made twice and four
times as big (`FAR_LEVELS`), every level cut into the same squares (`farChunk`), and a square far enough away
that its own cubes would come under `FAR_BLOCK` pixels on screen is drawn with the bigger ones (`farLevel`), so
the far side of it costs a fraction of its faces. Each square keeps the faces along its edges (`walls`), so
squares of different sizes beside each other leave no slit between them.

props.name: walls
props.doc:
Faces between two cubes in different squares of this size (x and z, the source's rest units, from the origin)
are kept, so each square is closed on its sides: what a far source's levels are made with (`farChunk`).

entries.name: BlockHole
entries.doc: A square of ground, x and z, in a source's rest units.

props.name: min
props.doc: Its least x and z.

props.name: max
props.doc: Its most x and z.

entries.name: BlockPiece
entries.doc: The cubes on one bone of one actor, as a mesh: four corners a face, two triangles.

props.name: actor
props.doc: Which of the sources it came from.

props.name: bone
props.doc: Which of that source's bones carries it.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: How many cubes.

props.name: positions
props.doc: Corner places in the rest pose, three numbers each.

props.name: normals
props.doc: Each corner's face normal.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Each corner's color, linear, the block's own with no light on it.

props.name: light
props.doc: Three numbers a corner: the light its face has from the look's light (shade and shadow in), what is left of any light in its corner, and how much of its own light the block gives.

props.name: uvs
props.doc: Each corner's place on its face, 0 or 1 each way.

props.name: indices
props.doc: Three corners a triangle.

props.name: faceCells
props.doc: Each face's cell and which of the six faces it is, four whole numbers a face in the order of the corners; the face is -1 for a loose speck.

props.name: side
props.doc: The side of its cubes.

entries.name: SolidCells
entries.doc: What is solid in a source's rest pose, a cell at a time, and the box that holds it all.
entries.type: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => boolean & { lo?: number[]; hi?: number[] }

entries.name: blockHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a cell, the same each time.

signatures.code: blockHash(x: number, y: number, z: number): number

entries.name: faceLight
entries.doc:
How much of the look's light each of a cube's six faces has when nothing is in the way, 0 to 1, in the order
+x, -x, +y, -y, +z, -z: by how squarely it faces the light, with the face that faces it most at 1, so no two of
the three faces a view shows are alike unless the light lies evenly between them.

signatures.code: faceLight(from?: readonly [number, number, number]): number[]

entries.name: faceTone
entries.doc: The light a face has: its shade (a little more of it facing the sky, less facing the ground) and its share of the light where that reaches it.

signatures.code: faceTone(face: number, lit: number, shade: number, sun: readonly number[]): number

entries.name: faceLit
entries.doc:
Whether the look's light reaches the face `face` of the cell at x, y, z: a walk from the face's middle toward the
light, half a cell at a time, until a solid cell is met or the walk is out of the box that holds them all.

signatures.code: faceLit(solid: (x: number, y: number, z: number) => boolean, x: number, y: number, z: number, face: number, from: readonly [number, number, number], lo: readonly number[], hi: readonly number[]): boolean

entries.name: buildBlocks
entries.doc:
The sources as blocks: a mesh for each bone that carries any (see `BlockLook`). A cell two bones' blobs share goes
to the bone with more of them, so no two cubes ever stand in one place; faces between two cubes on one bone are
left out. Shadows and corners are worked out within each source, never from one to another.

signatures.code: buildBlocks(sources: readonly BlockSource[], look: BlockLook): { pieces: BlockPiece[]; blocks: number; faces: number; solids: SolidCells[] }

entries.name: holed
entries.doc: A piece's triangles, leaving out every face of a cube whose middle stands in `hole`: all of them when there is none.

signatures.code: holed(piece: BlockPiece, hole?: BlockHole): Uint32Array

entries.name: keptBlocks
entries.doc:
One source's cubes (`buildBlocks` of it alone, which gives the same cubes as among others, since no source shades or
joins another), kept with its blobs when it says they never change (`keepCubes`) and asked for again with the same
look (its ambient aside), the same grid and the same skin, glow and lamps.

signatures.code: keptBlocks(source: BlockSource, look: BlockLook): { pieces: BlockPiece[]; blocks: number; faces: number; solids: SolidCells[] }

entries.name: FAR_LEVELS
entries.doc: How many levels of bigger cubes a far source (`BlockSource.far`) has beside its own: twice and four times as big.

entries.name: FAR_BLOCK
entries.doc: A square of a far source whose cubes would be drawn smaller than this many device pixels across takes the next bigger cubes, where there are any.

entries.name: FAR_CHUNK
entries.doc: How many of a far source's biggest cubes a square is across.

entries.name: FAR_HOLD
entries.doc: How far past `FAR_BLOCK`, as a share of it, a square's cubes must come before it changes level again, so a square at the line does not flicker between two.

entries.name: farChunk
entries.doc: The side of a far source's squares for its own cube side `cell` (x and z, rest units): `FAR_CHUNK` of its biggest cubes.

signatures.code: farChunk(cell: number): number

entries.name: farLevel
entries.doc:
Which level a square of a far source is drawn at (0 its own cubes, 1 twice as big, up to `most`), for `px`, how many
pixels across its own cubes would be on screen, and `now`, the level it is drawn at: the first whose cubes come to
`FAR_BLOCK` pixels, held within `FAR_HOLD` of the line either way.

signatures.code: farLevel(px: number, now: number, most?: number): number

entries.name: BlockChunk
entries.doc: The faces of one square of a piece: their triangles, and the middle and reach (half the box's diagonal) of their corners, in the rest pose.

props.name: key
props.doc: The square, as its place along x and z in squares (`"x,z"`), the same for every level of one source.

props.name: indices
props.doc: Three corners a triangle.

props.name: middle
props.doc: The middle of its corners' box.

props.name: reach
props.doc: Half that box's diagonal.

entries.name: chunkFaces
entries.doc:
Cuts a piece's triangles (`indices`, as `holed` leaves them) into squares of side `chunk` from the origin (x and z),
by each face's cube (a loose speck's by its own corners), so every face is in exactly one.

signatures.code: chunkFaces(piece: BlockPiece, indices: Uint32Array, chunk: number): BlockChunk[]

entries.name: lampsOf
entries.doc: Which of the first four lights are lamps that stay put, by a source's `seen`: those some blob of it sees less than all of.

signatures.code: lampsOf(seen: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> | undefined): boolean[]

entries.name: faceSeesLamp
entries.doc:
Whether a lamp at `at` (in cells) lights the face `face` of the cell at x, y, z: not when the face is turned away
from it, and not when a walk from just outside the face toward the lamp, half a cell at a time, meets a solid cell
before it is within a cell of the lamp. The lamp's own cell never counts, since a lamp sits inside its housing.

signatures.code: faceSeesLamp(solid: SolidCells, x: number, y: number, z: number, face: number, at: readonly [number, number, number]): boolean

entries.name: lampSight
entries.doc:
How much of a lamp each of a piece's faces sees, 1 or 0 a face (`faceSeesLamp`), for a lamp at `at` in the rest
pose's own units with a reach of `range`: faces further than twice its reach are left lit, since its light is gone
there anyway, and so are loose specks.

signatures.code: lampSight(piece: BlockPiece, solid: SolidCells, at: readonly [number, number, number], range: number): Float32Array

entries.name: FLOW_STEPS
entries.doc: A ripple's height as blocks is snapped to this many steps a block.

entries.name: FLOW_SWELL
entries.doc: How many times higher than it stands a ripple is drawn as blocks, when the look does not say.

entries.name: FLOW_DROP
entries.doc: How far under its layer's top a surface rests, as a share of a block: the banks beside it stand a little proud, and no two faces lie in one plane.

entries.name: FLOW_MOST
entries.doc: A column's top is never further than this many blocks from where it rests.

entries.name: FLOW_REACH
entries.doc: A blob of a moving surface lies over a cell's middle when it is within this many of its own sizes of it.

entries.name: FlowPlan
entries.doc: A moving surface as columns on the blocks' grid: which columns there are and which of its blobs each one reads.

props.name: cell
props.doc: A column's side.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many columns.

props.name: cells
props.doc: Each column's place on the grid: along x then along z, a pair a column.

props.name: level
props.doc: The height the blobs lay at, on the whole, when the plan was made: a ripple is measured from it.

props.name: rest
props.doc: Where a column's top is with the surface at rest.

props.name: beside
props.doc: The columns beside each one, toward +x, -x, +z and -z: four a column, -1 where there is none.

props.name: start
props.doc: Where each column's blobs start in `list`, and one more for the end.

props.name: list
props.doc: The blobs each column reads, a column after another.

entries.name: planFlow
entries.doc:
Plans a moving surface's columns: one for every cell of the grid, seen from above, that holds one of its blobs
or whose middle one of them reaches over, so a grid finer than the blobs are spread still has no holes. A column
reads every blob in it or over its middle.

signatures.code: planFlow(blobs: Blobs, cell: number): FlowPlan

entries.name: flowStep
entries.doc:
How far from rest a column's top stands for a surface `lift` over its level there: `swell` times as high, in
whole steps of a block's `FLOW_STEPS`th, and never more than `FLOW_MOST` blocks.

signatures.code: flowStep(lift: number, cell: number, swell?: number): number

entries.name: FlowMesh
entries.doc: A moving surface's columns as a mesh: a top and four sides each, twenty corners a column in that order (top, +x, -x, +z, -z), which `shapeFlow` moves and colors.

props.name: positions
props.doc: Corner places, three numbers each: `shapeFlow` writes the heights.

props.name: normals
props.doc: Each corner's face normal.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Each corner's color, linear, and how solid it is: four numbers, written by `shapeFlow`.

props.name: light
props.doc: As a block's (`BlockPiece.light`): the face's light, 1 for no corner, 0 for no light of its own.

props.name: uvs
props.doc: Each corner's place on its face.

props.name: indices
props.doc: Three corners a triangle.

props.name: tops
props.doc: Each column's top as `shapeFlow` last left it.

entries.name: flowMesh
entries.doc: The mesh for a plan's columns, level at rest and with no color yet: `shapeFlow` it before drawing.

signatures.code: flowMesh(plan: FlowPlan, look: BlockLook): FlowMesh

entries.name: shapeFlow
entries.doc:
Lays a mesh's columns to the surface as its blobs stand now: each top at its blobs' mean height over the level,
in steps (`flowStep`); each side from its own top down to the top of the column beside it, so only the risers
between columns are drawn (where it is the lower of the two it has no height; where there is no column beside it,
it goes a block down, into the bank); and each column in the mean of its blobs' colors, as solid as they make it
two deep.

signatures.code: shapeFlow(plan: FlowPlan, mesh: FlowMesh, blobs: Blobs, look: BlockLook): void

entries.name: GlitchLook
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: amount
props.doc: How often a burst comes, 0 (never) to 1 (most of the time).

props.name: strength
props.doc: How hard a burst is, 0 to 1: how far rows slide, channels split and how many blocks go.

props.name: jitter
props.doc: A burst slides bands of rows sideways.

props.name: split
props.doc: A burst reads red to one side and blue to the other.

props.name: blocks
props.doc: A burst takes blocks of the art from somewhere else.

props.name: pace
props.doc: Steps a second: a burst changes this often, never in between.

props.name: loop
props.doc: The scene's loop in seconds, where it has one: steps and bursts repeat with it.

props.name: still
props.doc: Under reduced motion: no bursts at all (a flicker is exactly what that asks to be spared).

props.name: seed
props.doc: Picks another run of bursts.

entries.name: GlitchState
entries.doc: One step's glitch, in art pixels: what the pass is handed each frame. All whole numbers.

props.name: on
props.doc: A burst is on.

props.name: key
props.doc: The step's own number for `glitchHash`, under 2^24.

props.name: jitter
props.doc: Most a row band slides either way, in art pixels (0: no jitter).

props.name: band
props.doc: Rows to a band.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The share of bands that slide, as a threshold over 2^24.

props.name: split
props.doc: How far red and blue are read to each side (0: no split).

props.name: block
props.doc: A corrupted block's height in art pixels (it is `BLOCK_WIDE` times as wide).

props.name: blocks
props.doc: The share of blocks corrupted, as a threshold over 2^24 (0: none).

entries.name: RUN_MOST
entries.doc: A burst lasts this many steps at most.

entries.name: START_MOST
entries.doc: The share of steps a burst starts on at `amount` 1.

entries.name: JITTER_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, how far a band of rows slides either way.

entries.name: SPLIT_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, how far red and blue are read to each side.

entries.name: BLOCKS_MOST
entries.doc: At full strength, the share of blocks corrupted.

entries.name: GLITCH_PACES
entries.doc: Steps a second the page offers.

entries.name: MIX_A
entries.doc: Two primes under 2^31 that spread a cell's two numbers before the hash.

entries.name: MIX_B
entries.doc: Two primes under 2^31 that spread a cell's two numbers before the hash.

entries.name: SALT
entries.doc: The salts that keep a cell's draws apart: each is one question about a row band or a block.
entries.type: { slides: 1; slide: 2; broken: 3; fromX: 4; fromY: 5; turned: 6; strip: 7 }

entries.name: STRIPS
entries.doc: Broken blocks gather in strips: this share of rows of blocks can break at all (a threshold over 2^24).

entries.name: BLOCK_WIDE
entries.doc: A broken block is this many times as wide as it is high, as a torn line of a picture is.

entries.name: TURNED
entries.doc: The share of broken blocks whose channels are turned (a threshold over 2^24).

entries.name: glitchHash
entries.doc:
The 24-bit hash of a row band or block (`a`, `b`, whole and not negative) for one question (`salt`) in the step
`key`: the GPU's `glitchHash` in pixelPass.ts, in the same unsigned 32-bit steps.

signatures.code: glitchHash(a: number, b: number, key: number, salt: number): number

entries.name: pickOf
entries.doc: A whole number from 0 to `m` − 1 out of a 24-bit hash, exact on both sides: (h · m) >> 24.

entries.name: stepsIn
entries.doc: How many steps a loop of `loop` seconds holds at `pace` a second: whole, and at least one.

entries.name: stepAt
entries.doc: The step a moment falls in, and how many steps go round (0 where nothing loops).

signatures.code: stepAt(t: number, look: GlitchLook): { k: number; n: number }

entries.name: glitchAt
entries.doc: The glitch at a moment: whether a burst is on and, if so, how it reads the art this step.

signatures.code: glitchAt(t: number, look: GlitchLook): GlitchState

entries.name: readFrom
entries.doc:
Where the art pixel at column `x`, row `y` (from the top) reads from, in a picture `w` wide and `h` high:
`x` for green, red `split` to the right of it and blue `split` to the left, and whether its channels are turned.

signatures.code: readFrom(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, g: GlitchState): { x: number; y: number; turned: boolean }

entries.name: wrapX
entries.doc: A column slid off one side comes in at the other.

entries.name: glitchArt
entries.doc:
The finished art with this step's glitch laid on: the CPU twin of the live pass's last step (pixelPass.ts
`toScreen`). Off, it is the art itself.

signatures.code: glitchArt(art: Frame, g: GlitchState): Frame

entries.name: WashPass
entries.doc:
Watercolor (splat-core/wash.ts). The frame is drawn three times with the same moved and sorted blobs (the picture
in the blobs' own flat colors, and for the pencil a map of depth and a map of parts). The picture is softened at
half and at a quarter of its size, and one pass paints the paper: each pixel reads the softened picture a little
to one side (the paper's own wander, fixed on the screen, so a wash's edge runs unevenly), takes its color as
pigment, and lays it on the paper as see-through paint (`washed`): thinner and thicker from place to place,
gathered into the paper's grain, darker where the wash ends or its color changes (the softened picture against
the more softened one), and not at all where the picture is lightest. A look's sky is a wash behind the subject
that stops short of the paper's edge; a faint pencil line runs where outlines would.

The world should be drawing flat marks (`Stage.setWash` sets them).

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts the pencil's lines between parts come from.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is.

signatures.code: setLook(look: WashLook, ratio: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene in watercolor into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Watercolor: the arithmetic

entries.name: WashLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws watercolor (`Stage.setWash`).

props.name: bleed
props.doc: How far a wash's edge runs and wanders, in CSS pixels (4).

props.name: pool
props.doc: How much darker a wash dries at its edges, 0 to 1 (0.6).

props.name: grain
props.doc: How much the paper's grain shows in the paint, 0 to 1 (0.55).

props.name: strength
props.doc: How strong the paint is, 0 to 1: lower is paler, with more paper showing (0.7).

props.name: pencil
props.doc: A pencil line under the paint, 0 for none to 1 (0.55).

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: sky
props.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]
props.doc: A wash behind the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1), laid short of the paper's edge. Left out, the paper is bare.

props.name: border
props.doc: Whether the wash behind stops short of the paper's edge, leaving a border of bare paper (true). False lays it to the edge.

entries.name: WASH_PAPER
entries.doc: The paper (sRGB 0–1): a warm white.

entries.name: WASH_PENCIL
entries.doc: The pencil (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: WASH_WHITE
entries.doc: A color this light or lighter (its brightest channel, linear) is left as bare paper, and one under the second is painted at full strength.

entries.name: WASH_RICH
entries.doc: Paint is richer wet than the picture's color: made this much stronger about its gray.

entries.name: WASH_UNEVEN
entries.doc: A wash is this much thinner or thicker from place to place, as water carries the pigment about.

entries.name: WASH_MARGIN
entries.doc: The wash behind the subject stops this far short of the paper's edge, as a share of the picture's height, give or take as much again.

entries.name: WASH_SKY
entries.doc: And is laid this thin beside the subject's own paint.

entries.name: washed
entries.doc:
Paper with one wash on it: `paint` is the pigment's color (linear, 0–1), `density` how much of it lies there (0
none, 1 a full wash, more where it pooled). Paint only ever takes light away, so the result is never lighter
than the paper.

signatures.code: washed(paper: readonly number[], paint: readonly number[], density: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: pigment
entries.doc: The pigment for a picture's color (linear): a little richer, and never quite black.

signatures.code: pigment(rgb: readonly number[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: whiteness
entries.doc:
How near white a color (linear) is, for `kept`: halfway between its brightest and darkest channels. Its brightest
alone took a strong orange or yellow (a palette's, say) for white and left it bare paper.

entries.name: kept
entries.doc: How much of a color is painted at all: nothing for the lightest (bare paper stands for it), all of it for the rest. `top` is its `whiteness`.

signatures.code: kept(top: number): number

entries.name: density
entries.doc:
How much paint lies at a place: the wash's `cover` there (0 off it, 1 well inside), thinned or thickened by the
water (`water`, 0–1), gathered into the paper's grain (`tooth`, 0–1, by `grain`), and more where it pooled as it
dried (`edge`, 0–1: how near the wash's edge or a change of color, by `pool`).

signatures.code: density(cover: number, water: number, tooth: number, edge: number, look?: { strength?: number; grain?: number; pool?: number }): number

entries.name: HalftonePass
entries.doc:
Halftone screen print (splat-core/halftone.ts is the CPU twin: change one, change both). The frame is drawn once,
every blob flat in its own color under the stage's lights. A small pass then works out every cell of every ink's
screen (a texel a cell, one block of rows an ink): the picture read round the cell's middle, over the sky or the
paper, separated into the inks (`separate`), keeping that ink's share. A second pass prints: each pixel finds its
cell on each ink's turned screen, cuts that cell's dot to its share (`dotCover`) and lays the inks over the paper
(`printed`). The print covers the canvas.

The world should be drawing flat marks (`Stage.setHalftone` sets them).

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is.

signatures.code: setLook(look: HalftoneLook, ratio: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Prints the scene in halftone into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Halftone print: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Halftone screen print (Matt asked for our own, 2026-11-25): the picture printed in a few inks, each laid through
its own screen of dots. A screen is a grid of cells fixed on the paper (so on the screen), turned to the ink's own
angle; each cell holds one dot whose area is how much of that ink the picture wants there, read at the cell's
middle, so a light place is small dots and a dark one dots that run together into a field with small holes. Inks
are see-through and print over one another, so where dots of two inks overlap the paper shows through both. Each
