ink's plate can sit a little off the others (misregistration), and the ink takes unevenly. The arithmetic here is
pure; `splat-engine/halftonePass.ts` is its shader twin (change both).

entries.name: Rgb01
entries.doc: An sRGB color, 0–1.

entries.name: HalftoneInk
entries.doc: One ink and its screen.

props.name: color
props.doc: The ink's color as printed full on white paper (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: angle
props.doc: The screen's angle, in degrees.

props.name: key
props.doc: The key ink (black): it takes over the gray the other inks share, as a printer's black does (one a set, at most).

entries.name: HalftoneLook
entries.doc: How a stage prints in halftone (`Stage.setHalftone`).

props.name: inks
props.doc: The inks, printed in this order; at most `HALFTONE_INKS`.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: cell
props.doc: A cell of the screen, in CSS pixels (7).

props.name: shift
props.doc: How far each plate sits off true, in CSS pixels (1).

props.name: texture
props.doc: How unevenly the ink takes, 0 to 1 (0.4).

props.name: sky
props.doc: The sky printed behind the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1). Left out, the paper is bare there.

entries.name: HALFTONE_INKS
entries.doc: The most inks a print has.

entries.name: HALFTONE_PAPER
entries.doc: The paper (sRGB 0–1): a bright white with a little warmth.

entries.name: SEPARATE_PASSES
entries.doc: How many times the separation goes round the inks.

entries.name: KEY_TAKES
entries.doc: How much of the gray the colored inks share a key ink (black) takes over (`separate`).

entries.name: KEY_FROM
entries.doc:
Black starts only past this much gray, as a printer's skeleton black: small black dots in a light gray read as
dirt, so the lightest grays stay in the colored inks.

entries.name: SPOT_FIT
entries.doc:
The dot's spot function is (cos 2πu + cos 2πv) / 2 over a cell (u, v from -½ to ½ about its middle): round dots
when small, a checkerboard at half, round holes when large. These turn a dot's area into the level the spot
function is cut at, as an odd polynomial in 1 − 2·area (fitted to the spot's own areas, within 0.7%).

entries.name: SHIFT_WAYS
entries.doc: Each plate's direction off true, by its place in the print (radians): spread so no two lie the same way.

entries.name: INK_GRAIN
entries.doc: How wide a patch of unevenly taken ink is, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: INK_UNEVEN
entries.doc: How much darker or lighter ink takes from place to place at full texture.

entries.name: inkLinear
entries.doc: An ink's color in linear light.

entries.name: separate
entries.doc:
How much of each ink a color wants (each 0 to 1), for a print on `paper` (both linear). Dots of inks on different
screens fall over one another as if at random, so a place with shares a of each ink reflects, on average,
paper · Π (1 − aᵢ·(1 − inkᵢ)) in each channel. The shares are found ink by ink with the others held, each step a
Gauss–Newton step on the error in log light, again and again. A `key` ink (black) is left out at first; then it
takes `KEY_TAKES` of the gray the other inks have in common (the least of their shares) past `KEY_FROM`, as a
printer replaces three inks' gray with black, and the others are found again round it. Let in at the start, black took the dark
channel of every color and greens came out gray.

signatures.code: separate(color: readonly number[], paper: readonly number[], inks: readonly (readonly number[])[], key?: number): number[]

entries.name: spotLevel
entries.doc: The level the spot function is cut at for a dot of this area (0 to 1): 1 for none, −1 for a full field.

signatures.code: spotLevel(area: number): number

entries.name: spotAt
entries.doc: The spot function at a place in a cell (u, v from -½ to ½ about its middle).

entries.name: screenAt
entries.doc:
Where a point of the paper (in device pixels) falls on a plate's screen: which cell (counted from the one at the
screen's turning point, `about`), the cell's middle on the paper, and the point's place in its cell. `cell` is in
device pixels, `angle` in degrees, `off` where the plate sits off true. Screens turn about the picture's middle.

signatures.code: screenAt(x: number, y: number, cell: number, angle: number, off?: readonly [number, number], about?: readonly [number, number]): { at: [number, number]; mid: [number, number]; u: number; v: number }

entries.name: CELL_TAPS
entries.doc: Where a cell's color is read, round its middle, along the screen's own two ways: shares of a cell (the middle and four more).

entries.name: cellShare
entries.doc:
How much of ink `i` a plate's cell holds: the picture read round the cell's middle (`mid`, device pixels; `t` from
0 at the top to 1 at the bottom, for the sky), over the sky or the paper, separated into the look's inks.

signatures.code: cellShare(i: number, mid: readonly [number, number], angle: number, cell: number, height: number, picture: (x: number, y: number) => readonly number[], look: HalftoneLook): number

entries.name: dotCover
entries.doc: How much of a pixel a dot of `area` covers at (u, v) in its cell, softened over one pixel (`soft`: a device pixel in cell units).

signatures.code: dotCover(u: number, v: number, area: number, soft: number): number

entries.name: plateOff
entries.doc: Where plate `i` sits off true, in device pixels, for a look's `shift` in device pixels.

entries.name: printed
entries.doc: The paper with inks on it: `cover` is how much of the pixel each ink's dot covers, `thick` how heavily it took there (1 as printed). Linear in, linear out.

signatures.code: printed(paper: readonly number[], inks: readonly (readonly number[])[], cover: readonly number[], thick?: readonly number[]): [number, number, number]

entries.name: inkNoise
entries.doc: A small, smooth noise over the paper (0 to 1), in CSS pixels, for how unevenly ink takes: the shader's twin.

signatures.code: inkNoise(x: number, y: number): number

entries.name: halftoneAt
entries.doc:
One device pixel of the print. `picture(x, y)` is the picture there, linear and premultiplied (r, g, b, a), with y
counted from the top; `width` and `height` are the picture's, `ratio` device pixels a CSS pixel.

signatures.code: halftoneAt(x: number, y: number, picture: (x: number, y: number) => readonly number[], width: number, height: number, look: HalftoneLook, ratio?: number): [number, number, number]

modules.title: Claymation, blueprint, thermal, paper cutout, mosaic and CRT

entries.name: FilterPass
entries.doc:
The six looks laid over the whole picture (splat-core/filters.ts is the CPU twin: change one, change both): a
thermal camera, an old CRT or tape, a blueprint, a mosaic, paper cutouts and claymation. The frame is drawn once
as the world is set to draw it, and, where the look asks, a map of depth and one of parts with the same moved and
sorted blobs (as outlines are, inkLines.ts); then one full-screen pass draws the look over the whole canvas.

`Stage.setFilter` sets the world for each: the blueprint and paper cutouts draw flat marks with no lights; the
thermal camera draws what gives its own light over white (`THERMAL_EMIT`), so it can tell a lamp from a pale thing;
claymation moves in held frames. The frame's camera must be a perspective camera.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture, as the world draws it (half floats, so what glows can go over white).

props.name: ids
props.doc: The map of parts, for the looks that want one.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look, and how many device pixels a CSS pixel is; `size` is the scene's size in the world, `time` the stage's clock.

signatures.code: setLook(look: FilterLook, ratio: number, size: number, time: number): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass's targets, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
Draws the scene in the look into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none. `box` is the
subject's box in the world (the blueprint's dimension lines are drawn round it).

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera, box?: { lo: readonly number[]; hi: readonly number[] }): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: Six filter looks: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
Six looks laid over the whole picture (Matt picked them, 2026-11-25): a thermal camera, an old CRT or tape, a
blueprint, a mosaic, paper cutouts and claymation. Each is drawn by `splat-engine/filterPass.ts` from the frame as
the blobs draw it (and, where a look asks, a map of depth and one of parts), one full-screen pass a look. The
arithmetic here is pure and is the shader's CPU twin: change one, change both.

Places on the screen are device pixels with y counted down from the top; `ratio` is device pixels a CSS pixel, so
a look's sizes (lines, tiles, shadows) are the same size to the eye on every screen.

entries.name: Sky01
entries.doc: A sky, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: fract
entries.doc: The fractional part.

entries.name: hash2
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a place (the shader's `hash`; change both).

entries.name: noise2
entries.doc: Smooth value noise from 0 to 1 over whole-number cells (the shader's `noise`; change both).

signatures.code: noise2(x: number, y: number): number

entries.name: luma
entries.doc: A color's luminance (linear in, linear out).

entries.name: toLinear
entries.doc: sRGB 0–1 to linear light.

entries.name: skyAt
entries.doc: The sky at `t`, from 0 at the top of the picture to 1 at the bottom (linear in, linear out).
entries.type: (top: readonly number[], bottom: readonly number[], t: number) => [number, number, number]

entries.name: Picture
entries.doc: A picture read at a device pixel: linear light, premultiplied (r, g, b, a).

entries.name: ThermalLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as a thermal camera sees it (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: ramp
props.doc: The heat colors from cold to hot (sRGB 0–1), 2 to `THERMAL_STOPS` of them, evenly spread.

props.name: stepped
props.doc: Each heat takes the nearest of the ramp's colors, not a mix of two (a palette's colors stay its own).

props.name: hot
props.doc: How hot what gives its own light runs (a lamp, a fire, breath), 0 to 1.5 (1).

props.name: spread
props.doc: How far heat spreads round what gives its own light, in CSS pixels (20).

props.name: warm
props.doc: How warm lit things are, by how bright they are, 0 to 1 (0.8).

props.name: noise
props.doc: The sensor's grain, 0 to 1 (0.3).

props.name: still
props.doc: The grain holds still (reduced motion, or a frame that must not change by the clock).

entries.name: THERMAL_EMIT
entries.doc: What gives its own light is drawn this many times its color for the thermal camera, so it can be told from a pale thing (as neon's lamps).

entries.name: THERMAL_STOPS
entries.doc: The most colors a heat ramp has.

entries.name: THERMAL_TAPS
entries.doc: Where heat is looked for round each pixel, as shares of the look's spread (eight at the full reach, four at half).

entries.name: THERMAL_SPREAD_GAIN
entries.doc: How much of what glows nearby a pixel takes as its own heat.

entries.name: THERMAL_SKY
entries.doc: How hot the empty sky reads at its top and at the horizon.

entries.name: THERMAL_FPS
entries.doc: How often the grain changes, a second.

entries.name: emitted
entries.doc: How much of its color a pixel gives off by itself (linear, not premultiplied): 0 for anything at or under white, 1 at `THERMAL_EMIT` times.

entries.name: hotShare
entries.doc:
How much of what glows there counts as hot, by how colored it is: a lamp, a flame or the sun is warm-colored and
hot, while a glowing cloud, the moon or a star is white and reads cold, as the sky does to a heat camera.

entries.name: THERMAL_WHITE
entries.doc: How much cooler a white thing reads than a dark one in the same light: white throws the sun back (clouds, snow, white walls).

entries.name: heatOf
entries.doc: A pixel's own heat, 0 to about 1.5, from its color (linear, not premultiplied): warmth by how bright it is lit, and the heat of what glows.

signatures.code: heatOf(c: readonly number[], look: ThermalLook): number

entries.name: rampAt
entries.doc: The color for a heat (0 to 1) along a ramp of linear colors, evenly spread; `stepped` takes the nearest one.

signatures.code: rampAt(ramp: readonly (readonly number[])[], h: number, stepped?: boolean): [number, number, number]

entries.name: paletteRamp
entries.doc: A palette (sRGB 0–255) as a heat ramp: its colors from darkest to lightest, at most `THERMAL_STOPS`, spread evenly over it.

signatures.code: paletteRamp(colors: readonly (readonly number[])[]): Rgb01[]

entries.name: grainFrame
entries.doc: The grain's frame at a time.

entries.name: thermalAt
entries.doc: One device pixel as the thermal camera sees it (linear out).

signatures.code: thermalAt(x: number, y: number, picture: Picture, height: number, look: ThermalLook, ratio?: number, time?: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: CrtLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as an old television playing a tape (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: scan
props.doc: How dark the gaps between scanlines are, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: every
props.doc: How tall a scanline is, in CSS pixels (3).

props.name: bleed
props.doc: How far color smears to the right of where it belongs, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: wobble
props.doc: How much the picture's rows wander and a tracking band rolls up the screen, 0 to 1 (0.4).

props.name: noise
props.doc: Tape noise, 0 to 1 (0.3).

props.name: curve
props.doc: How much the glass bulges, with darker corners, 0 to 1 (0.4).

props.name: sky
props.doc: What stands behind the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: period
props.doc: Seconds the scene takes to come round again: the wobble goes a whole number of times into it, so a recording joins (12).

props.name: still
props.doc: The wobble and noise hold still.

entries.name: CRT_BACK
entries.doc: Behind a subject with no sky of its own (sRGB 0–1): a dim studio blue.

entries.name: CRT_BLEED_PX
entries.doc: How many CSS pixels color smears at full bleed.

entries.name: CRT_BLEED_TAPS
entries.doc: How many taps the smear is read with.

entries.name: CRT_BAND_PX
entries.doc: How far the tracking band throws rows aside at full wobble, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: CRT_BAND
entries.doc: How tall the tracking band is, as a share of the picture.

entries.name: CRT_ROLLS
entries.doc: How many times a loop the tracking band rolls up the screen.

entries.name: CRT_WANDERS
entries.doc: How many times a loop the slow wander of the rows goes round.

entries.name: CRT_FPS
entries.doc: How often the tape noise changes, a second.

entries.name: yiq
entries.doc: YIQ from linear-ish RGB (the television's own split of brightness and color).

entries.name: fromYiq
entries.doc: RGB from YIQ.

entries.name: crtCurve
entries.doc: Where a point of the screen (u, v from 0 to 1) reads the picture through the bulging glass, or undefined off its edge.

signatures.code: crtCurve(u: number, v: number, curve: number): [number, number] | undefined

entries.name: scanShade
entries.doc: How bright a place within a scanline is (`f` from 0 to 1 down the line): bright in its middle, dark between lines.

entries.name: wobbleAt
entries.doc: How far the rows at `v` (0 top, 1 bottom; `y` in CSS pixels) are thrown aside at a time, in CSS pixels.

signatures.code: wobbleAt(v: number, yCss: number, time: number, look: CrtLook): number

entries.name: crtAt
entries.doc: One device pixel of the television (linear out). `picture` is linear and premultiplied.

signatures.code: crtAt(x: number, y: number, picture: Picture, width: number, height: number, look: CrtLook, ratio?: number, time?: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: BlueprintLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as a blueprint (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: ink
props.doc: The lines (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: line
props.doc: The outline's width, in CSS pixels (1.5).

props.name: inner
props.doc: How strong the lines between a thing's parts are beside its outline, 0 to 1 (0.6).

props.name: grid
props.doc: How far apart the grid's lines are, in CSS pixels; 0 draws none (16).

props.name: dims
props.doc: Whether dimension lines are drawn across the subject's width and height (true).

props.name: fill
props.doc: How strongly the subject is washed in the line color, 0 to 1 (0.25).

entries.name: BLUEPRINT_PAPER
entries.doc: A blueprint's paper (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: BLUEPRINT_INK
entries.doc: A blueprint's lines (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: GRID_MINOR
entries.doc: How strong the grid's lines are.

entries.name: GRID_MAJOR
entries.doc: How strong every fifth line of the grid is.

entries.name: DIM_GAP
entries.doc: How far the dimension lines stand off the subject, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: DIM_ARROW
entries.doc: How long the dimension lines' arrowheads are, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: DIM_TICKS
entries.doc: How many marks divide a dimension line.

entries.name: gridAt
entries.doc: How much of the grid's lines cover a pixel (0 to 1); `x`, `y` and `every` in device pixels, `ratio` for the line's width.

signatures.code: gridAt(x: number, y: number, every: number, ratio?: number): number

entries.name: ScreenBox
entries.doc: A box on the screen, in device pixels: left, top, right, bottom.

entries.name: dimPlaces
entries.doc: Where a box's dimension lines go (device pixels): the line under it (`yd`) and beside it (`xd`), each moved over or to the left where there is no room, and where their extension lines run; none for a box too small or off the picture.

signatures.code: dimPlaces(box: ScreenBox, width: number, height: number, ratio?: number): { yd: number; xd: number; fromY: number; toY: number; fromX: number; toX: number } | undefined

entries.name: dimsAt
entries.doc:
Dimension lines round a box (device pixels, y down): one under it across its width and one beside it down its
height (over it and to its left where there is no room), each with extension lines to the box, an arrowhead at each
end and `DIM_TICKS` marks along it. How much of them covers (x, y), 0 to 1.

signatures.code: dimsAt(x: number, y: number, box: ScreenBox, width: number, height: number, ratio?: number): number

entries.name: MosaicLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as a mosaic (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: tile
props.doc: A tile's side, in CSS pixels (10).

props.name: grout
props.doc: The grout between tiles, in CSS pixels (1.5).

props.name: groutColor
props.doc: The grout's color (sRGB 0–1).

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much tiles differ in color from one to the next, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: bevel
props.doc: How much each tile's edges catch light and shade, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: brick
props.doc: Rows set over one another like bricks, half a tile along.

props.name: sky
props.doc: What stands behind the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1): tiles in its colors. Left out, plain tiles of `MOSAIC_GROUND`.

entries.name: MOSAIC_GROUT
entries.doc: The grout (sRGB 0–1): a pale mortar.

entries.name: MOSAIC_GROUND
entries.doc: Tiles behind a subject when no sky is laid (sRGB 0–1): a warm stone.

entries.name: MOSAIC_TAPS
entries.doc: Where a tile's color is read, as shares of the tile about its middle (the middle first).

entries.name: tileAt
entries.doc: The tile a device pixel lies in: its column and row, its middle, and the pixel's place in it (u, v from −½ to ½).

signatures.code: tileAt(x: number, y: number, side: number, brick?: boolean): { cell: [number, number]; mid: [number, number]; u: number; v: number }

entries.name: tileCover
entries.doc:
How much of a pixel a tile covers (0 to 1): a rounded square inset by half the grout, a little smaller or larger
by its own hash so the grout lines wander. `side` and `grout` in device pixels.

signatures.code: tileCover(u: number, v: number, cell: readonly [number, number], side: number, grout: number): number

entries.name: tileTint
entries.doc: A tile's own change of color: how much lighter or darker, and a small shift of each channel.

signatures.code: tileTint(cell: readonly [number, number], vary: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: bevelAt
entries.doc: How a tile's face is lit by its bevel at (u, v): lighter toward its top left edge, darker toward its bottom right.

signatures.code: bevelAt(u: number, v: number, bevel: number): number

entries.name: CutoutLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as layered cut paper (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: shadow
props.doc: How far a layer's shadow falls on what is behind it, in CSS pixels (6).

props.name: soft
props.doc: How soft the shadow's edge is, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: light
props.doc: Where the light comes from on the screen, in degrees (0 from the right, 90 from above; 120).

props.name: grain
props.doc: The paper's fibers, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: edge
props.doc: The pale cut edge on the side toward the light, in CSS pixels (1).

props.name: ragged
props.doc: How ragged the cut edges are, 0 to 1 (0.4).

props.name: sky
props.doc: The card behind everything, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: CUTOUT_CARD
entries.doc: The card behind a subject with no sky of its own (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: CUTOUT_SHADE
entries.doc: How dark a shadow is at full.

entries.name: CUTOUT_LAYER
entries.doc: How much a layer must be nearer than the one under it to cast on it, as a share of the depth.

entries.name: CUTOUT_TAPS
entries.doc: Where a soft shadow's edge is read, as shares of its softness, across the light's way.

entries.name: RAGGED_PX
entries.doc: How far a ragged edge wanders at full, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: RAGGED_GRAIN
entries.doc: How far apart a ragged edge's turns are, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: lightWay
entries.doc: The way toward the light on the screen (device y down), for a light from `deg` (0 from the right, 90 from above).

entries.name: raggedAt
entries.doc: Where a pixel reads the picture so cut edges wander a little: an offset in device pixels.

signatures.code: raggedAt(x: number, y: number, ragged: number, ratio?: number): [number, number]

entries.name: grainAt
entries.doc: The paper's fibers at a pixel: a brightness from about 0.94 to 1.06 at full grain.

signatures.code: grainAt(x: number, y: number, grain: number, ratio?: number): number

entries.name: shadowAt
entries.doc:
How much shadow falls on a pixel (0 to 1): where, a shadow's length toward the light, there is a layer nearer than
this one (or anything at all, where this pixel is the card), read at a few places across the light's way for a
soft edge. `at(x, y)` says whether something is there and its depth (0 for nothing) and part.

signatures.code: shadowAt(x: number, y: number, at: (x: number, y: number) => { depth: number; part: number }, look: CutoutLook, ratio?: number): number

entries.name: ClayLook
entries.doc: How a stage is drawn as stop-motion clay (`Stage.setFilter`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which look this is.

props.name: fps
props.doc: Frames a second the scene moves at, as stop motion; 0 moves every frame (12).

props.name: prints
props.doc: How deep the thumbprints are, 0 to 1 (0.6).

props.name: size
props.doc: How big a thumbprint is, as a share of the scene's size (0.05).

props.name: smooth
props.doc: How smooth the clay is: each thing's own colors softened together, 0 to 1 (0.5).

props.name: sheen
props.doc: How much the clay shines, 0 to 1 (0.3).

props.name: boil
props.doc: How much the thumbprints shift from one frame to the next, as an animator's hands leave them (0.4).

props.name: sky
props.doc: What stands behind the subject, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1).

entries.name: CLAY_BACK
entries.doc: Behind a subject with no sky of its own (sRGB 0–1): a painted studio backdrop.

entries.name: CLAY_KEY
entries.doc: The clay's key light in the view's own frame (x right, y up, z toward the viewer): from the top left, in front.

entries.name: PRINT_R
entries.doc: How far a thumbprint reaches from its middle, in the prints' own size (a cell of the world is 1).

entries.name: PRINT_TILT
entries.doc: How steeply a thumbprint's walls tip the clay's facing at full depth (its slope per unit of `printAt`'s gradient).

entries.name: PRINT_LIP
entries.doc: How high the clay pushed out of a thumbprint stands round its edge, as a share of the dent's depth.

entries.name: PRINT_LIP_W
entries.doc: How wide that lip is, as a share of the print's reach.

entries.name: PRINT_SHUT
entries.doc: How much darker the bottom of a thumbprint is at full depth, shut in by its own walls.

entries.name: PRINT_LIGHT
entries.doc: How much more a thumbprint's tipped walls turn toward or away from the light than the clay's soft key alone shows.

entries.name: PRINT_SHARE
entries.doc: The share of the clay's cells that hold a thumbprint.

entries.name: CLAY_SMOOTH_PX
entries.doc: How far round each pixel the clay is softened, in CSS pixels at full smoothness.

entries.name: CLAY_TAPS
entries.doc: Where it is softened, as shares of that reach (eight ways at the full reach, eight between them at half).

entries.name: CLAY_SHADE_PX
entries.doc: How far round each pixel the clay looks for nearer clay that shades it, in CSS pixels.

entries.name: CLAY_HOLLOW
entries.doc: How dark a pixel shut in on every side by nearer clay gets.

entries.name: CLAY_DEEP
entries.doc: How much nearer than a pixel its neighbor must be, as a share of its depth, to shade it fully.

entries.name: hollowOf
entries.doc: How shut in a pixel is (0 open to 1 shut in), from its own depth and its neighbors' round it (0 for nothing there): soft shade in the creases between lumps of clay.

signatures.code: hollowOf(depth: number, round: readonly number[]): number

entries.name: printHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a cell of the world (the shader's `cellHash` in filterPass.ts; change both).
entries.type: (x: number, y: number, z: number, salt: number) => number

entries.name: clayFrame
entries.doc: The stop-motion frame a time falls in, which the thumbprints shift by.

entries.name: Print
entries.doc: A thumbprint at a point: its height (−1 at the bottom of the dent up to `PRINT_LIP` on its lip, 0 elsewhere) and that height's slope, per unit of the prints' own size, in the world's frame.

props.name: h
props.doc: The height: −1 at the bottom of the dent, up to `PRINT_LIP` on its lip, 0 away from any print.

props.name: g
props.doc: How fast the height rises, each way of the world, per unit of the prints' own size.

entries.name: printProfile
entries.doc: A thumbprint's height across it, from its middle (0) out (`PRINT_R` is 1), and how fast that changes outward.

signatures.code: printProfile(u: number): [number, number]

entries.name: printAt
entries.doc:
The thumbprints at a point of the world, in the prints' own size (the world divided by a print's size). A print is
a round dent pressed into the clay with a little clay pushed up round its edge; each cell of the world holds one or
none, and each frame shifts it a little (`boil`), as hands do. The dent is lit by tipping the clay's facing
(`pressed`), so its wall toward the light falls in shade and the far wall catches it.

signatures.code: printAt(p: readonly [number, number, number], frame: number, boil: number): Print

entries.name: pressed
entries.doc:
Clay facing `n` (the view's frame, unit length) with a thumbprint pressed in, its slope `g` already turned into the
view's frame: the facing tipped by the print's walls, and how much the light there changes beyond what `clayShade`
gives that facing (deeper shade on the wall toward the light, the bottom shut in).

signatures.code: pressed(n: readonly [number, number, number], g: readonly [number, number, number], h: number, prints: number): { n: [number, number, number]; light: number }

entries.name: clayShade
entries.doc: The clay's own shading for a surface facing `n` (the view's frame, unit length): a soft wrapped key light and a little sheen.

signatures.code: clayShade(n: readonly [number, number, number], sheen: number): { shade: number; shine: number }

entries.name: FilterLook
entries.doc: Any of the looks laid over the whole picture.
entries.type: ThermalLook | CrtLook | BlueprintLook | MosaicLook | CutoutLook | ClayLook

entries.name: FilterKind
entries.doc: Which of them.

entries.name: KnitPass
entries.doc:
The picture as knitting (splat-core/knit.ts is the CPU twin: change one, change both). The frame is drawn once,
every blob flat in its own color. One small pass decides every stitch of the grid (the yarn nearest what the
picture shows there, or the sweater's own pattern where it shows nothing; kept in a target a stitch a pixel,
beside the one from the frame before so a stitch can keep its yarn), and a second draws each stitch as a V of
yarn. The knitting covers the canvas.

The world should be drawing flat marks with no light of its own (`Stage.setKnit` sets both).

props.name: picture
props.doc: The picture: every blob flat in its own color.

props.name: grid
props.doc: The grid of the frame just drawn: a pixel a stitch, the yarn's number in red.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look.

signatures.code: setLook(look: KnitLook): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the pass for a picture in device pixels, with stitches `width` by `height` of them.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number, stitch: { width: number; height: number }): void

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Forgets the frame before: for when what is being drawn is swapped for something else.

signatures.code: forget(): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene as knitting into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: Camera): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its targets.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

entries.name: KnitLook
entries.doc: How a stage draws knitting (`Stage.setKnit`).

props.name: size
props.doc: A stitch's width, in CSS pixels (9).

props.name: yarns
props.doc: The yarns (sRGB 0–1), at most `KNIT_YARNS`: the first is the sweater's body, the second the pattern's main yarn, the third its second. The picture is knitted in every yarn but the body's.

props.name: bands
props.doc: The pattern round the picture: the bands from the edge inward, each an id of `MOTIFS`. Left out or empty, none.

props.name: snow
props.doc: Small dots of the pattern's yarn over the plain field between the bands.

props.name: steady
props.doc: How much nearer another yarn must be (OKLab) before a stitch of the picture changes yarn; 0 decides each frame afresh (`KNIT_STEADY`).

entries.name: KNIT_YARNS
entries.doc: The most yarns a look can have.

entries.name: STITCH_TALL
entries.doc: A stitch is this many times as tall as wide: knitting is wider than it is tall.

entries.name: KNIT_COVER
entries.doc: A stitch belongs to the picture when this much of it is covered.

entries.name: KNIT_STEADY
entries.doc: A stitch of the picture keeps its yarn unless another is this much nearer (OKLab distance).

entries.name: KNIT_LIGHT
entries.doc: How much lightness counts beside hue when a yarn is picked for a color: a red thing in shade takes the dark red yarn before a brown one as light as it.

entries.name: BAND_SHARE
entries.doc: The bands at the top take up to this share of the rows, and those at the bottom as much.

entries.name: SNOW_STEP
entries.doc: Snow dots stand this many stitches apart, each row of them half a step aside from the last.

entries.name: PICTURE_MARK
entries.doc: Added to a stitch's yarn number in the grid when it shows the picture, so the next frame can tell.

entries.name: LEG_TOP
entries.doc: Where a V's two legs run, in a stitch's own square (x across, y down, both 0 to 1): from `LEG_TOP` out at the side to `LEG_TIP` near the middle, which lies a quarter of a stitch into the row below.

entries.name: LEG_TIP
entries.doc: Where a V's leg ends, near the middle and a quarter of a stitch into the row below (see `LEG_TOP`).

entries.name: YARN_HALF
entries.doc: Half a strand's width, as a share of the stitch's.

entries.name: GAP_SHADE
entries.doc: How dark the gap between strands is beside the yarn.

entries.name: YARN_ROUND
entries.doc: How much darker a strand is at its edges than along its middle.

entries.name: YARN_VARY
entries.doc: How much one stitch's yarn is lighter or darker than the next's.

entries.name: stitchAt
entries.doc:
What is at a point of a stitch (x across, y down, 0 to 1): `above` when it is the tip of the stitch above, which
lies over this one, and `shade`, what the yarn's color is multiplied by there (a strand is lighter along its
middle; between strands is the dark of the gap, in the stitch's own yarn).

signatures.code: stitchAt(x: number, y: number): { above: boolean; shade: number }

entries.name: stitchHash
entries.doc: A number from 0 to 1 for a stitch, as the shader makes it.

signatures.code: stitchHash(col: number, row: number): number

entries.name: yarnFor
entries.doc: The yarn nearest a color (sRGB 0–1) in OKLab with lightness counted `KNIT_LIGHT`, never the body's (yarn 0): its number, and how far off it is. `was` is the yarn the stitch had, kept unless another is `steady` nearer.

signatures.code: yarnFor(color: readonly number[], yarns: readonly Rgb3[], was?: number, steady?: number): { yarn: number; off: number }

entries.name: Motif
entries.doc: A small picture knitted over and over along a band: rows of stitches, `.` the body, `x` the pattern's main yarn, `o` its second. Every row is one repeat wide.

props.name: id
props.doc: Its name in a look's `bands`.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows, top first.

props.name: upright
props.doc: It stands on the ground (a tree, a reindeer), so the bottom bands don't turn it over.

entries.name: MOTIFS
entries.doc: The motifs a band can be.

entries.name: knitChart
entries.doc:
The sweater's own pattern for a grid of stitches: a yarn number a stitch (0 the body, 1 and 2 the pattern's),
rows from the top. The bands are laid from the top edge inward, each with a plain row after it, for as long as
they fit in `BAND_SHARE` of the rows (one too tall is left out), and again from the bottom edge up, turned over
unless they stand upright. Every motif is laid so that the middle of the grid is the middle of a repeat, so the
pattern is the same on both sides. Snow dots fill the field between.

signatures.code: knitChart(cols: number, rows: number, look: Pick<KnitLook, "bands" | "snow">): Uint8Array

entries.name: stitchSize
entries.doc: How many device pixels a stitch is wide and tall: whole, so every stitch is the same size.

signatures.code: stitchSize(size: number, ratio: number): { width: number; height: number }

entries.name: knitCell
entries.doc:
One stitch decided: `cover` is how much of it the picture covers and `color` what it shows there (sRGB 0–1,
straight), `beside` whether a stitch next to it (left, right, above or below) shows the picture, `chart` the
sweater's own yarn there and `was` the grid's number for it the frame before (-1 for none). The picture wins;
a stitch right beside it is plain body, so the pattern never runs into the picture. Gives the grid's number:
the yarn, plus `PICTURE_MARK` for a stitch of the picture.

signatures.code: knitCell(cover: number, color: readonly number[], beside: boolean, chart: number, yarns: readonly Rgb3[], was?: number, steady?: number): number

entries.name: AnaglyphPass
entries.doc:
3D glasses (splat-core/anaglyph.ts): the frame drawn twice, from a left and a right eye a little either side of the
camera, each looking the same way with its picture slid so that the screen (`eyesFor`) lands in the same place for
both, then one pass lays them over each other in red and cyan (`mixEyes`, the CPU twin: change both). Each eye's
picture sits over the look's backdrop, which is the same for both, so it stands at the screen.

Each eye is its own view, so the blobs are sorted for each: two sorts and two draws a frame. Lines and points are
drawn in both pictures, as anything else is.

props.name: eyes
props.doc: The left eye's picture and the right's: linear color times cover, and cover.

methods.name: setLook
methods.doc: The look: how deep, where the screen stands, how the pictures are mixed and what is behind.

signatures.code: setLook(look: AnaglyphLook): void

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sizes the eyes' pictures, in device pixels.

signatures.code: setSize(width: number, height: number): void

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Draws the scene for both eyes and lays them over each other into the renderer's current target, or onto the screen when it has none. `distance` is how far the camera is from what it looks at.

signatures.code: render(renderer: WebGPURenderer, scene: Object3D, camera: PerspectiveCamera, distance: number): void

methods.name: dispose
methods.doc: Frees its pictures.

signatures.code: dispose(): void

modules.title: 3D glasses: the arithmetic
modules.doc:
3D glasses (Matt's idea, 2026-11-25): the scene drawn twice, from two eyes a little apart, and the two pictures laid
one over the other in red and cyan. Without glasses things stand doubled, a red ghost to one side and a cyan one to
the other; through red and cyan glasses each eye sees only its own picture and the scene comes together in depth.

Pure: the eyes' geometry and how the two pictures are mixed, which `AnaglyphPass` (splat-engine/anaglyphPass.ts)
repeats in its shader. Change both.

entries.name: AnaglyphMix
entries.doc: How the two pictures are mixed into one.

entries.name: AnaglyphLook
entries.doc:
How the eyes are set and the pictures mixed. Glasses are red over the left eye and cyan over the right, the
usual pair.

props.name: depth
props.doc: How far apart the eyes are, as a share of the usual (`EYE_SHARE` of the distance to what the view looks at): 0 is flat, 1 the usual, 2 twice as deep.

props.name: pop
props.doc: Where the screen stands, past what the view looks at, as a share of the distance to it: 0 puts that at the screen, 0.5 puts the screen half as far again behind it, so more comes out toward you.

props.name: mix
props.doc: How the two pictures are mixed.

props.name: back
props.doc: What is behind the scene, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1), the same in both eyes so it sits at the screen.

entries.name: EYE_SHARE
entries.doc: The usual eyes: a thirtieth of the distance to what the view looks at, a stereo photographer's rule of thumb.

entries.name: ANAGLYPH_BACK
entries.doc: What is behind a scene with no sky of its own (sRGB): a dark gray, which shows the least ghosting through either lens.

entries.name: eyesFor
entries.doc:
The two eyes for a view looking at something `distance` away: how far each stands to the side of the camera
(`half`, the left eye at −half along the camera's right, the right at +half), and how far away the screen is
(`screen`), where a thing is drawn in the same place for both eyes.

signatures.code: eyesFor(distance: number, look: AnaglyphLook): { half: number; screen: number }

entries.name: eyeSlide
entries.doc:
How far an eye's picture is slid across (in clip space, per unit of w) so that a point `screen` away, straight
ahead of the camera, lands in the middle of both: `side` is the eye's place along the camera's right, `p00` the
projection's x scale. Add it to the projection matrix's element 8 (x from z) negated, as `eyeProjection` does.
entries.type: (side: number, p00: number, screen: number) => number

entries.name: eyeProjection
entries.doc: An eye's projection matrix (column-major, as three.js keeps it): the camera's own with x slid by `eyeSlide`.

signatures.code: eyeProjection(p: ArrayLike<number>, side: number, screen: number): number[]

entries.name: eyeX
entries.doc:
Where a point in the camera's own frame (x right, y up, looking down −z) lands across the picture for an eye,
in normalized device coordinates: that eye stands at `side` along x and uses `eyeProjection`. The CPU check of
what the shader is given.

signatures.code: eyeX(p: ArrayLike<number>, side: number, screen: number, at: readonly [number, number, number]): number

entries.name: EYE_MIX
entries.doc:
Each mix as two 3×3 matrices, rows for red, green and blue of the result, columns for the left and right
pictures' red, green and blue (linear). `optimized` is Eric Dubois's least-squares red–cyan projection, which
keeps most color while each lens passes little of the other eye's picture; `color` hands the left eye's red and
the right eye's green and blue over as they are (bright, but reds ghost); `half` gives the left eye its gray and
the right its color; `gray` gives both their gray (no color, least ghosting).
entries.type: Record<AnaglyphMix, { left: readonly Rgb3[]; right: readonly Rgb3[] }>

entries.name: ANAGLYPH_MIXES
entries.doc: The mixes in the order the page offers them.

entries.name: mixEyes
entries.doc: One pixel of the finished picture (linear, 0–1) from the two eyes' pixels there (linear, over the backdrop).

signatures.code: mixEyes(left: Rgb3, right: Rgb3, mix?: AnaglyphMix): [number, number, number]

entries.name: BakeTarget
entries.doc:
Draws a rigged creature's moves from 4 or 8 sides and turns each frame into
pixel art with Splat to Sprite's pipeline (render big, average down, cut the
alpha, one palette for the whole sheet, tidy, outline).

The camera circles the creature (which faces +Z) with a narrow lens from far
off, so the sprite is close to orthographic, and stays at one distance for
every frame, so the creature is the same size in all of them.

props.name: renderer
props.doc: The renderer to draw with.

props.name: scene
props.doc: A scene holding only what should be in the sprite (the creature's SplatWorld).

props.name: actor
props.type: { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }
props.doc: The creature being drawn.

props.name: posed
props.doc: Tells the world its skeleton (and, after `morph`, its blobs) moved.

props.name: morph
props.doc: Reshapes the actor's blobs by a clip's morph weights at a time, on the CPU, for an actor with morphs.

entries.name: BakeOptions
entries.doc: How a sprite sheet is baked.

props.name: directions
props.doc: Directions each move is drawn from.

props.name: size
props.doc: A frame's width and height, in pixels.

props.name: colors
props.doc: Colors in the palette.

props.name: outline
props.doc: Whether each sprite gets a dark outline.

props.name: maps
props.doc: Bake a normal map and a depth map beside the sheet, frame for frame (`BakedSheet.normals`, `depths`), for a game that lights its sprites.

entries.name: BakedSheet
entries.doc: A baked sprite sheet: its frames and how they are laid out.

props.name: plan
props.doc: The rows and columns.

props.name: frames
props.doc: Every frame, row by row.

props.name: size
props.doc: A frame's width and height, in pixels.

props.name: anchorY
props.doc: Where the feet are: one past the lowest solid row of any frame.

props.name: framing
props.doc: The sphere the camera was fitted to.

props.name: png
props.doc: The whole sheet as one PNG.

props.name: normals
props.doc: With `BakeOptions.maps`: each frame's facing as a normal map (x right, y up, z toward the viewer; spriteMaps.ts).

props.name: depths
props.doc: With `BakeOptions.maps`: each frame's depth, white nearest and black furthest across the creature's framing.

props.name: mapPng
props.doc: The normal or depth maps laid out as the sheet is, as one PNG.

entries.name: bakeSheet
entries.doc:
Draws every frame of every move from each direction, all at one camera distance, and turns them into pixel art.
`progress` is called as frames are done.

signatures.code: bakeSheet(t: BakeTarget, moves: SheetMove[], o: BakeOptions, progress?: (done: number, total: number) => void): Promise<BakedSheet>

entries.name: SheetMove
entries.doc:
A rigged creature's moves as a pixel-art sprite sheet: the plan (which row
is which move from which side), the framing, and the two JSON files that go
with the PNG. Pure, so Node tests can check it; the drawing is bakeSheet.ts.

Rows are move by move, and within a move one row per direction, in the
order Splat to Sprite uses: 4 directions follow Tinkerkit (down, left,
right, up), 8 go round clockwise from down. Each row holds that move's
frames, evenly spaced through one loop of its clip.

props.name: name
props.doc: Names the animations: `<name>-<direction>`.

props.name: clip
props.doc: Undefined for a still pose (the rest pose).

props.name: frames
props.doc: How many frames it gets.

entries.name: SheetRow
entries.doc: One row of a sheet: a move seen from one direction (`turn` is that direction's angle).

props.name: move
props.doc: The move.

props.name: dir
props.doc: The direction's name, such as 'down'.

props.name: turn
props.doc: How far the creature is turned for it, in degrees.

entries.name: SheetPlan
entries.doc: A sheet's rows, and as many columns as its longest move has frames.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows, top to bottom.

props.name: cols
props.doc: Columns: the longest move's frames.

entries.name: planSheet
entries.doc: Lays a sheet out: a row for each move seen from each direction.

signatures.code: planSheet(moves: SheetMove[], directions: 4 | 8): SheetPlan

entries.name: loopSeconds
entries.doc: How long one loop of a move lasts, in seconds (0 for a still pose).

entries.name: frameTimes
entries.doc: When each frame of a move is taken: evenly through one loop, so the last frame leads back into the first.

entries.name: moveFps
entries.doc: Frames per second that plays a move at its real speed.

entries.name: Framing
entries.doc: A sphere that holds the creature through every frame of every move.

props.name: center
props.doc: The sphere's middle.

props.name: radius
props.doc: Its radius.

entries.name: frameAll
entries.doc:
A sphere round the creature through every frame of every move, so one
camera distance fits them all and the creature is the same size in every
frame. Moves a sample of blob centers by their bones on the CPU (the same
blend as the GPU), and pads each by its largest scale.

signatures.code: frameAll(actor: { blobs: Blobs; skin: Skin; skeleton: Skeleton }, moves: SheetMove[], sample?: number, morph?: (clip: Clip | undefined, t: number) => void): Framing

entries.name: tinkerkitJson
entries.doc:
Mirrors Tinkerkit's `SpriteSheet` document (packages/format/src/spritesheet.ts,
format version 71). Adds `idle-<direction>` (the first frame of the first
move) when no move is called idle, since Tinkerkit's characters stand on it.

signatures.code: tinkerkitJson(name: string, image: string, plan: SheetPlan, size: number, anchorY?: number): { kind: string; formatVersion: number; id: string; name: string; image: string; imageWidth: number; imageHeight: number; frameWidth: number; frameHeight: number; pixelScale: number; anchor: { x: number; y: number }; footprint: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }; animations: Record<string, { frames: number[]; fps: number; loop: boolean }> }

entries.name: asepriteJson
entries.doc:
The JSON-array sheet Aseprite writes (and TexturePacker, Phaser and most
engines' importers read): one entry per frame, with a tag per animation.

signatures.code: asepriteJson(image: string, plan: SheetPlan, size: number): { frames: object[]; meta: { app: string; version: string; image: string; format: string; size: { w: number; h: number }; scale: string; frameTags: object[] } }

entries.name: Style
entries.doc: How a scene is drawn: as pixel art (plain or glitching), or as one of Brush and Ink's looks.
entries.type: typeof PIXEL.id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof id | typeof FILTERS[number]["id"] | typeof LOOKS[number]["id"]

entries.name: STYLES
entries.doc: Blocks first, then pixel art and tech glitch (pixel art too), then the looks in Brush and Ink's own order (the plain blobs last).
entries.type: { id: Style; label: string; note: string }[]

entries.name: HIDDEN_STYLES
entries.doc: Styles kept in the code, the address and kept scenes but offered in no picker (Matt, 2026-11-25: claymation is not ready yet).

entries.name: offered
entries.doc: Whether a style is offered in a picker.

entries.name: PICKED_STYLES
entries.doc: The styles a picker offers: `STYLES` without the hidden ones.
entries.type: { id: Style; label: string; note: string }[]

entries.name: DEFAULT_STYLE
entries.doc: The style a page starts in, and the one a plain address means: blocks. Every other style is named in the address (`?style=pixel`).

entries.name: styleAsked
entries.doc:
The style an address or a kept scene asks for (`?style=oil`), or the default. Text keeps the id `ascii` (`?style=text`
means it too), and a Text picture in box drawing or quarter blocks (`?style=ascii&chars=lines`, kept before
2026-11-25) is Box Art now, so `chars` is the address's or the kept Text settings' set of characters.

signatures.code: styleAsked(asked: string | null, chars?: string | null): Style

entries.name: styleWords
entries.doc: A style as the end of "drawn …", for the line under the view and the view's own label.

signatures.code: styleWords(style: Style): string

entries.name: isPixelStyle
entries.doc: Whether a style is drawn as pixel art underneath (pixel mode, its palette and finish): pixel art itself and tech glitch.

entries.name: lightsItself
entries.doc: Whether a style lights the scene itself, so the scene is cut with no light baked in: cel shading, neon, stained glass, blocks, knitting and paper cutout (which want each thing in its own flat colors).

modules.title: The catalog: every style's settings
modules.doc:
The styles API (Matt, 2026-11-22: no page uses a version of a style all its own). Two things, both data:

- the catalog (`CATALOG`): every style's settings written once, each with its kind, its choices or range, where it
  starts and its name in the address. Controls are drawn from it (`SettingsControls.tsx`), the address is read by it
  (`fromAddress`) and kept settings are checked against it (`settingsFrom`), so a setting added here is on every
  page that offers the style, in its links and in its saved scenes.
- the value (`StyleValue`): which style, and each style's settings, which a page holds, a saved scene keeps and a
  link carries.

An experiment tries a setting of its own by adding it to the style here marked `trial` with the experiment's name:
only that page shows it. Folding it in is taking the mark off. Pure, so it is tested.

entries.name: Unit
entries.doc: How a number reads beside its slider.

entries.name: Shows
entries.doc: What a setting's `when` is told about the page: the style on show and what the subject has.

props.name: style
props.doc: The style on show.

props.name: water
props.doc: Whether the subject has water.

props.name: weather
props.doc: Whether weather is out over the subject.

props.name: cycle
props.doc: Whether the scene has a color cycle.

props.name: colors
props.doc: How many colors the palette on show has (0 is full color).

props.name: heat
props.doc: The scene's own heat haze, in art pixels.

entries.name: Tab
entries.doc: Where on a page a setting is laid: a style whose settings are spread over two tabs says which (pixel art's Style and Finish; `switches` is the Finish tab's run of switches).

entries.name: Drawn
entries.doc: How a setting is drawn when not as its own kind: what the control shows for the settings as they are, and what a press changes.
entries.type: { kind: "toggle"; at: (v: V) => boolean; set: (to: boolean, on: Shows) => Partial<V> } | { kind: "choice"; options: readonly { id: string; label: string }[]; at: (v: V) => string; set: (id: string) => Partial<V> }

entries.name: RangeSetting
entries.doc: A slider.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says it is a slider.

props.name: min
props.doc: The least it goes to.

props.name: max
props.doc: The most it goes to.

props.name: step
props.doc: How far one step of the slider moves it.

props.name: unit
props.doc: How its number reads beside the slider.

props.name: zero
props.doc: What 0 reads as ("None").

props.name: whole
props.doc: Held to whole steps.

entries.name: ChoiceSetting
entries.doc: One of a few, as chips. `open` choices are the page's to list (a scene's palettes): any id is kept.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says it is a choice.

props.name: options
props.type: readonly { id: string | number; label: string; about?: string }[]
props.doc: What can be picked: each one's kept value, its name, and a line about it.

props.name: open
props.doc: The page lists the choices itself (a scene's palettes), so any id is kept.

entries.name: ToggleSetting
entries.doc: A switch. One that starts `null` follows its style (`auto`) until the visitor says. `on` is the address's word for it when not 1.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says it is a switch.

props.name: about
props.doc: A line beside the switch.

props.name: auto
props.doc: What a switch that starts `null` does for a style until the visitor says.

props.name: on
props.doc: The address's word for on, when it is not 1.

entries.name: SeedSetting
entries.doc: A whole number a button moves on, for another run of something random.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says it is a seed.

entries.name: TextSetting
entries.doc: A line of text the visitor types (the words a picture is written in).

props.name: kind
props.doc: What says it is text.

props.name: most
props.doc: The most characters it keeps.

entries.name: StyleSetting
entries.doc: A setting of a style: a slider, a choice, a switch, a seed or a line of text.

entries.name: StyleDef
entries.doc: One style's settings (or those of a few styles that share them, as the brush marks do).

props.name: id
props.doc: The name its settings are kept under.

props.name: styles
props.doc: The styles that use these settings.

props.name: start
props.doc: Where every setting starts.

props.name: settings
props.doc: The settings, in the order a page lays them out.

entries.name: MarkSettings
entries.doc: The brush marks (gouache, oil, ink and wash, hatching, stipple) and the plain blobs, which can take the pen's outline too.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big a mark is beside its blob.

props.name: outline
props.doc: Whether a pen outlines things; null is on for the pen looks and off for paint.

props.name: pen
props.doc: The pen's width, in CSS pixels.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper and ink, an id of `PAPERS`.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: AsciiSettings
entries.doc: The settings of the picture drawn as characters.

props.name: chars
props.doc: Which characters: ASCII, braille, words or a typewriter's (Box Art's sets are its own style).

props.name: words
props.doc: The text the picture is written in, drawn as words.

props.name: letter
props.doc: A character's height, in CSS pixels.

props.name: weight
props.doc: How heavy the characters are drawn.

props.name: strokes
props.doc: Whether edges are drawn as strokes (| _ / \\).

props.name: strands
props.doc: Whether fur and grass are drawn as strokes along the way they lie.

props.name: own
props.doc: Whether each character takes the color of what it shows.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The ground and ink, an id of `PAPERS`.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: BoxArtSettings
entries.doc: The settings of the picture drawn as Box Art: the box-drawing and block characters, apart from Text (Matt, 2026-11-25).

props.name: chars
props.doc: Which characters: box drawing ('lines') or quarter blocks and shades ('blocks').

props.name: letter
props.doc: A character's height, in CSS pixels.

props.name: weight
props.doc: How heavy the characters are drawn.

props.name: own
props.doc: Whether each character takes the color of what it shows.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The ground and ink, an id of `PAPERS`.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: CelSettings
entries.doc: Cel shading's settings.

props.name: turn
props.doc: Where the light is, in degrees round the subject from the starting view.

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the light stands, in degrees.

props.name: tones
props.doc: How many tones the light is cut into.

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether things cast shadows.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: How far the light is smoothed over a surface before it is cut, in pixels.

props.name: fills
props.doc: How many flat colors each part's own are gathered into; 0 leaves them as painted.

props.name: backdrop
props.doc: What stands behind, an id of `BACKDROPS`; '' is the subject's own sky where it has one.

props.name: outline
props.doc: Whether an even line is drawn round things.

props.name: pen
props.doc: The line's width, in CSS pixels.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is lit: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: PixelSettings
entries.doc: Pixel art's settings, as the Style and Finish controls set them.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette's id: 'own' is the scene's, else one of the shared ones.

props.name: size
props.doc: Each art pixel this many device pixels across.

props.name: rate
props.doc: Frames a second the scene moves at; 0 is every frame the screen shows.

props.name: dither
props.doc: How much dither, 0 to 1.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How strongly glowing things light what is round them and shine into the pixels beside them.

props.name: outline
props.doc: A line round the scene, and whether it takes a darker tone of each thing it goes round.

props.name: own
props.doc: Whether the outline takes a darker tone of each thing it goes round.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Lines inside the scene: where things meet (and, where the scene asks, where colors jump).

props.name: sky
props.doc: Whether the scene's sky is drawn behind it.

props.name: heat
props.doc: Heat haze over glowing things, in art pixels; 0 is none.

props.name: bands
props.doc: Glow in flat rings.

props.name: selout
props.doc: A softer outline on lit sides.

props.name: cycle
props.doc: Color cycling, where the scene has one.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Painted in steps of the palette as the scene is cut.

props.name: texel
props.doc: Light in this many bands a blob, as the scene is cut; 0 is smooth light.

props.name: shade
props.doc: Light worked out a pixel at a time (cel shading in the small picture), with the scene cut unlit.

props.name: rock
props.doc: The scene's own gentle rocking of the view.

props.name: exact
props.doc: The exact (radix) sort.

entries.name: PIXEL_SIZES
entries.doc: The pixel sizes on offer.

entries.name: PIXEL_RATES
entries.doc: The paces on offer, in frames a second; 0 is smooth.

entries.name: TEXEL_BANDS
entries.doc: How many steps of sun Light in bands gives (`banded`): three, none, half and full, kept the paint's texture best.

entries.name: PIXEL
entries.doc:
Pixel art. Where a scene has a finish of its own it starts these (`pixelStart` in styleSettings.ts); this start is
a scene with none. Its controls are spread over two tabs (`tab`), and a few are drawn as another kind than they are
kept as (`draw`): the outline's two switches are one choice of three, and the bands and the haze are switches.

entries.name: GLITCH_DEF
entries.doc: Tech glitch: pixel art with bursts laid on, so it has pixel art's settings and these.

entries.name: MARKS
entries.doc: The settings the brush marks and the plain blobs share: mark size, outline, pen and paper.

entries.name: WORDS_START
entries.doc: What a picture drawn as words says until the visitor writes something else.

entries.name: ASCII
entries.doc: The settings of the picture drawn as characters.

entries.name: BOX_SETS
entries.doc: Box Art's sets of characters, which Text drew until 2026-11-25: `?style=ascii&chars=lines` is Box Art now.

entries.name: BOX_ART
entries.doc: The settings of the picture drawn as Box Art (Matt, 2026-11-25: box drawing and quarter blocks, out of Text).

entries.name: CEL_DEF
entries.doc: Cel shading's settings.

entries.name: BLOCKS_DEF
entries.doc: The settings of the Blocks style.

entries.name: NEON_DEF
entries.doc: Neon's settings.

entries.name: GLASS_DEF
entries.doc: Stained glass's settings.

entries.name: WASH_DEF
entries.doc: Watercolor's settings.

entries.name: HALFTONE_DEF
entries.doc: Halftone screen print's settings.

entries.name: CLAY_DEF
entries.doc: Claymation's settings.

entries.name: BLUEPRINT_DEF
entries.doc: The blueprint's settings.

entries.name: THERMAL_DEF
entries.doc: The thermal camera's settings.

entries.name: CUTOUT_DEF
entries.doc: Paper cutout's settings.

entries.name: MOSAIC_DEF
entries.doc: The mosaic's settings.

entries.name: CRT_DEF
entries.doc: CRT / VHS's settings.

entries.name: KNIT_DEF
entries.doc: Knitting's settings.

entries.name: ANAGLYPH_DEF
entries.doc: 3D glasses' settings.

entries.name: SceneSettings
entries.doc:
The scene's own settings, which every style respects: '' is the scene as it is written (its own weather, its own
time), and a detail of '' is the one its style starts at (`detailStart`). Weather and cloud cover are one choice on
the page (a weather brings its own clouds), kept as two so a cover can be told from a weather.

props.name: time
props.doc: The time of day; '' is the scene as written.

props.name: weather
props.doc: The weather; '' is the scene's own, 'none' turns a scene's own off.

props.name: clouds
props.doc: The cloud cover; '' is the scene's own.

props.name: wind
props.doc: The wind; '' is what the weather brings.

props.name: overhead
props.doc: Clouds floating over the scene; null is the scene's own way.

props.name: transition
props.doc: How one scene gives way to the next; 'cut' is at once.

props.name: detail
props.doc: The detail the scene is cut at, an id of `SCENE_DETAIL`; '' is the one its style starts at.

entries.name: SCENE
entries.doc: The scene's own settings, written as a style's are so the same code reads, keeps and draws them.

entries.name: sceneStart
entries.doc: The scene's settings as they start, with what the address asks (`?time=night`, `?weather=snow`, `?wind=gale`, `?transition=cut`, `?detail=fine`).

entries.name: DrawnSettings
entries.doc: The settings of the looks `useDrawnLook` draws: every style but pixel art and its glitch.

entries.name: StyleValue
entries.doc: How a scene is drawn: the style, every style's settings (so going to another style and back loses nothing), and the scene's own.

props.name: style
props.doc: The style on show.

props.name: styles
props.doc: Every style's settings.

props.name: scene
props.doc: The scene's own settings.

entries.name: keysOf
entries.doc: The settings a style uses, in the order they are laid on: tech glitch is pixel art's and its own.

entries.name: fromAddress
entries.doc: A style's settings as the address asks for them, over `start`: only settings with an `address`, and only sound values.

signatures.code: fromAddress<V>(def: StyleDef<V>, start: V, q: URLSearchParams): V

entries.name: settingsFrom
entries.doc: Settings that were kept (a saved scene, a link) read back over `start`: each one kept only where the catalog finds it sound.

signatures.code: settingsFrom<V>(def: StyleDef<V>, start: V, kept: unknown): V

entries.name: StartFor
entries.doc: What a page tells the start about itself.

props.name: coarse
props.doc: A phone or tablet: knitting starts two pixels a stitch finer, so its bands fit a small view.

entries.name: drawnStart
entries.doc: The drawn looks' settings as they start, with what the address asks (`?block=`, `?tones=3`, `?chars=braille`, `?outline=0`, …).

signatures.code: drawnStart(q?: URLSearchParams, on?: StartFor): DrawnSettings

entries.name: drawnFrom
entries.doc: Kept drawn settings read back over a start: `kept` is an object by style (`{ cel: {…}, blocks: {…} }`), any of it missing or unsound left as it starts.

signatures.code: drawnFrom(start: DrawnSettings, kept: unknown): DrawnSettings

entries.name: valueWords
entries.doc: A setting's value as words, as its slider shows it.

signatures.code: valueWords<V>(s: RangeSetting<V>, v: number): string

entries.name: shownSettings
entries.doc: The settings a page shows for a style (in one of its tabs, where it has them): those whose `when` holds, and no other page's trials.

signatures.code: shownSettings<V>(def: StyleDef<V>, value: V, on: Shows, page?: string, tab?: Tab): StyleSetting<V>[]

entries.name: SCENE_DETAIL
entries.doc: The detail levels a scene written as data is cut at: the grid's spacing for each, coarsest first.
entries.type: readonly [{ id: "chunky"; label: "Chunky"; spacing: 0.042 }, { id: "medium"; label: "Medium"; spacing: 0.03 }, { id: "fine"; label: "Fine"; spacing: 0.022 }, { id: "finest"; label: "Finest"; spacing: 0.017 }]

entries.name: LookId
entries.doc: How the blobs are drawn: as they are, or as one of the marks.

entries.name: isMark
entries.doc: Whether a look is one of the marks drawn blob by blob.

entries.name: LOOKS
entries.doc: The drawn looks a page offers, each with its name and a line about it; the plain blobs last.
entries.type: { id: LookId; label: string; note: string }[]

entries.name: PAPERS
entries.doc: Paper and pen for the drawn looks.
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; paper: readonly [number, number, number]; ink: readonly [number, number, number] }[]

entries.name: GROUND
entries.doc: What the painted looks stand on: a dark, warm ground, as a primed board.

entries.name: SCREEN
entries.doc: What the characters stand on, by default: near black, as a terminal.

entries.name: CEL
entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.name: BACKDROPS
entries.doc: What the cel stands on, and the shade and line that go with it.
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; back: string; shade: readonly [number, number, number]; ink: readonly [number, number, number] }[]

entries.name: lightFrom
entries.doc: The way to a light `turn` degrees round the upright (0 is from +z, 90 from +x, as a view's azimuth) and `height` degrees up.

signatures.code: lightFrom(turn: number, height: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: CelChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: turn
props.doc: Where the light is, in degrees round the subject from the starting view.

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the light stands, in degrees.

props.name: tones
props.doc: How many tones the light is cut into.

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether things cast shadows.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: How far the light is smoothed over a surface before it is cut, in pixels.

props.name: line
props.doc: The outline's width, in CSS pixels; 0 is none.

props.name: backdrop
props.doc: What stands behind, an id of `BACKDROPS`.

props.name: fills
props.doc: How many colors each part's own are gathered into (`gatherColors`); 0 leaves them as painted.

entries.name: CEL_START
entries.doc: Where cel shading's settings start.

entries.name: celLook
entries.doc: The look for the stage.

signatures.code: celLook(c: CelChoice): CelLook

entries.name: FILL_REACH
entries.doc: Flat fills take out speckle finer than this many of a typical blob's size; an eye or an apple a few blobs across stays.

entries.name: NIGHT_SKY
entries.doc: A sky this dark or darker (the mean lightness of its top and bottom, sRGB 0–1) is night, and one this light or lighter is day.

entries.name: DAY_SKY
entries.doc: See `NIGHT_SKY`.

entries.name: MOONLIGHT
entries.doc: What a night's light multiplies every tone by (linear): dim and blue, as moonlight is painted.

entries.name: nightOf
entries.doc: How much a sky (top and bottom, sRGB 0–255) is a night's: 0 by day, 1 at night, between at dusk.

signatures.code: nightOf(sky: readonly [readonly number[], readonly number[]]): number

entries.name: nightLight
entries.doc: What cel shading's tones are multiplied by under a sky that much a night's (`CelLook.ambient`): nothing by day, `MOONLIGHT` at night.

signatures.code: nightLight(night: number): [number, number, number]

entries.name: BLOCKS
entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.name: BlockChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: size
props.doc: A block's side, in cells of the grid the subject was cut on.

props.name: turn
props.doc: Where the light is, in degrees round the subject from the starting view.

props.name: height
props.doc: How high the light stands, in degrees.

props.name: shadows
props.doc: Whether blocks cast shadows on each other.

props.name: corners
props.doc: How dark the corners where blocks meet are, 0 to 1.

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much a block's color differs from the next, 0 to 1.

props.name: edge
props.doc: How strong the line round each face is, 0 to 1.

props.name: backdrop
props.doc: What stands behind: 'scene' for the subject's own sky, or a plain color (`BLOCK_GROUNDS`); '' is the subject's own sky where it has one, else daylight.

props.name: water
props.doc: A subject's water: columns of blocks that rise and fall, or the blobs it is among the cubes.

props.name: weather
props.doc: Weather over the subject (clouds, rain, snow): cubes as the scene is, or the soft blobs it is in the other styles.

props.name: swell
props.doc: How many times higher than it stands a ripple is drawn as blocks.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the blocks are painted from: 'none' keeps each block's own color, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one (Diorama's `PALETTES`).

entries.name: BLOCK_START
entries.doc: Where the Blocks style's settings start.

entries.name: BLOCK_GROUNDS
entries.doc:
What to stand in front of when it is not the subject's own sky: daylight, or a plain color. The time of day is the
scene's own setting (timeOfDay.ts), not this look's: it reaches here as the subject's sky and the stage's light.
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; back: string }[]

entries.name: BlockBack
entries.doc: What a choice of backdrop comes to: what goes behind the canvas and what light it gives (none is day's).

props.name: id
props.doc: Which backdrop it is.

props.name: back
props.doc: What goes behind the canvas, as CSS.

props.name: light
props.doc: The light it gives; day's when left out.

entries.name: blockBack
entries.doc:
The backdrop for a choice. `sky` is the subject's own sky as CSS and how much it is a night's (`nightOf`), where it
has one: it is what an empty choice means, and under a dark one the light is a night's, unless the page has set a
time of day (`timed`), whose light is already the stage's.

signatures.code: blockBack(choice: string, sky?: { back: string; night: number }, timed?: boolean): BlockBack

entries.name: SWELL_MOST
entries.doc: The most a ripple's height is multiplied by.

entries.name: BLOCK_SIZES
entries.doc: The sizes on offer, in cells of the subject's grid.

entries.name: BLOCK_SPAN
entries.doc: A subject cut on no grid gets blocks as if its longest side were this many cells.

entries.name: gridOf
entries.doc:
The side of one cell for a subject: the grid the page says it was cut on, else the grid the cut records (`Built.grid`,
from voxel.ts), else a share of its longest side. A guessed cell that is not the cut's own grid falls between the
blobs' rows and leaves rows of empty cells, so blocks drawn from a cut always snap to its grid.

signatures.code: gridOf(spacing: number | undefined, centers: ArrayLike<number>, count: number, own?: number): number

entries.name: blockLook
entries.doc: The look for the stage: `grid` is one cell's side, `azimuth` the starting view's turn, `ambient` a night's light.

signatures.code: blockLook(c: BlockChoice, grid: number, azimuth?: number, ambient?: readonly [number, number, number], palette?: readonly (readonly [number, number, number])[]): BlockLook

entries.name: NEON
entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.name: NEON_GROUND
entries.doc: What neon stands on: near black, a little violet, as a night street.

entries.name: NEON_SETS
entries.doc: The tubes' colors: each thing's own at full strength, or a set dealt out part by part (sRGB 0–1).
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; colors?: readonly (readonly [number, number, number])[] }[]

entries.name: NEON_PACES
entries.doc: How fast the light runs: the seconds a pulse takes to come round again, about (0 holds it still).
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; period: number }[]

entries.name: NeonChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: line
props.doc: A tube's width, in CSS pixels.

props.name: glow
props.doc: How strongly the tubes' light spreads.

props.name: body
props.doc: How much of its own color a body keeps in the dark, 0 to 1.

props.name: set
props.doc: The tubes' colors, an id of `NEON_SETS`.

props.name: pace
props.doc: How fast the light runs, an id of `NEON_PACES`.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: NEON_START
entries.doc: Where neon's settings start.

entries.name: periodIn
entries.doc:
The period nearest `about` seconds that goes a whole number of times into a loop of `loop` seconds, so a recorded
loop joins up; `about` itself where nothing loops.

signatures.code: periodIn(about: number, loop?: number): number

entries.name: neonLook
entries.doc: The look for the stage. Under reduced motion the light holds still.

signatures.code: neonLook(c: NeonChoice, loop?: number, still?: boolean): NeonLook

entries.name: GLASS
entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.name: GLASS_GROUND
entries.doc: What shows before the window is drawn: the lead's own color.

entries.name: GLASS_FILLS
entries.doc: How many flat colors each part's own are gathered into (`gatherColors`) before it is glazed.

entries.name: GlassChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: pane
props.doc: A pane's size, as a share of the whole scene.

props.name: lead
props.doc: The lead's width, in CSS pixels.

props.name: shine
props.doc: How strong the light behind the window is, 0 to 1.

props.name: vary
props.doc: How much one pane's glass differs from the next, 0 to 1.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: GLASS_START
entries.doc: Where stained glass's settings start.

entries.name: glassLook
entries.doc: The look for the stage; `sky` is the subject's own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–255), where it has one.

signatures.code: glassLook(c: GlassChoice, sky?: readonly [readonly number[], readonly number[]]): GlassLook

entries.name: WASH
entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.name: WASH_PAPERS
entries.doc: The papers a wash can be laid on (sRGB 0–1). All light: paint only darkens what is under it.
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; paper: readonly [number, number, number] }[]

entries.name: WashChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: bleed
props.doc: How far a wash's edge wanders over the paper, in CSS pixels.

props.name: pool
props.doc: How much darker paint gathers where a wash ends, 0 to 1.

props.name: grain
props.doc: How much the paper's tooth shows, 0 to 1.

props.name: strength
props.doc: How much paint is laid on, 0 to 1.

props.name: pencil
props.doc: How strong the pencil line is, 0 for none.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper, an id of `WASH_PAPERS`.

props.name: border
props.doc: Whether a border of bare paper is left round the wash behind the subject.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is drawn: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: WASH_START
entries.doc: Where watercolor's settings start.

entries.name: washGround
entries.doc: The color to put behind the canvas before the paper is drawn.

entries.name: WASH_SKY_COLORS
entries.doc:
The wash behind a subject with no sky of its own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1): a pale blue going warm toward the
ground, so the paper still has a painted sky on it (Matt, 2026-11-22: bare paper read as no background at all).
entries.type: readonly [readonly [number, number, number], readonly [number, number, number]]

entries.name: washLook
entries.doc: The look for the stage; `sky` is the subject's own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–255), or `WASH_SKY_COLORS` where it has none.

entries.doc: The chip beside the drawn looks (brushLooks.ts).

entries.type: { id: string; label: string; about: string; inks: HalftoneInk[] }[]

entries.name: HALFTONE_PAPERS
entries.doc: The papers a print can be pulled on (sRGB 0–1). All light: ink only darkens what is under it.
entries.type: { id: string; label: string; paper: Rgb01 }[]

entries.name: HalftoneChoice
entries.doc: What the page's controls make.

props.name: cell

props.name: shift
props.doc: How far each plate sits off true, in CSS pixels.

props.name: texture
props.doc: How unevenly the ink takes, 0 to 1.

props.name: paper
props.doc: The paper, an id of `HALFTONE_PAPERS`.

props.name: sky
props.doc: Whether the subject's sky is printed behind it, or the paper left bare there.

props.name: palette
props.doc: The palette the scene is painted from before it is printed: 'none' keeps its own colors, 'own' is the scene's, else a shared one.

entries.name: HALFTONE_START
entries.doc: Where halftone's settings start.

entries.name: halftoneGround
entries.doc: The color to put behind the canvas before the print is drawn.

entries.name: HALFTONE_SKY
entries.doc: The sky printed behind a subject with no sky of its own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–1): a pale blue going warm toward the ground.

entries.doc: The look for the stage; `sky` is the subject's own, top and bottom (sRGB 0–255), or `HALFTONE_SKY` where it has none.

modules.title: Cloth solver
modules.doc:
A small position-based dynamics solver (XPBD, "small steps" form: many
substeps, one pass over the constraints in each), for cloth and hair hung
on a rig. Points carry an inverse mass (0 = pinned, moved by the caller);
links keep two points at a length, goals pull a point toward where the
animation puts it, and capsules push points out of the body. Compliance is
the inverse of stiffness: 0 is rigid.

It always steps by `STEP`, carrying what's left of a frame to the next, so
the same frames give the same motion and a recorded loop can be played back.
Pure and tested.

entries.name: Capsule
entries.doc: A segment from `a` to `b` with a radius; `a` and `b` the same is a ball.

props.doc: Its radius.

entries.name: SUBSTEPS
entries.doc: Substeps the solver takes in each `STEP`.

entries.name: Xpbd
entries.doc:
A small XPBD solver: points joined by links, pulled toward goals and kept out of capsules. It steps at a fixed
`STEP`, carrying the rest of a frame over, so the same frames always give the same motion.

A solid thing in a material simulation: fixed, or a rigid body with weight. Its shape is a distance function; a
